title: FATHERLAND
description: From the director of IDA and COLD WAR: FATHERLAND follows Nobel Prize-winning author Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler, KINGS OF THE ROAD) and his actress daughter Erika (Sandra Hüller, ANATOMY OF A FALL) as they drive across a war-ravaged 1949 Germany. Returning home after years of exile in the U.S. and exuding a superhuman gravitas, Mann finds the Germany he knew to be gone, replaced by a country with contradictory ideologies. Erika, who acts as his travel coordinator and translator, strives to pierce his detached persona while quietly struggling with a family tragedy.

title: MY UNDESIRABLE FRIENDS: PART II – EXILE: Chapters 4-5
description: When Russia shuts down all independent media, a group of young dissident journalists must flee Moscow so they can keep reporting and not go to prison. In her riveting follow-up to last year’s awards-sweeping MY UNDESIRABLE FRIENDS — LAST AIR IN MOSCOW, Julia Loktev follows these courageous, sharply funny women (and a few men) as they fan out across a dozen countries, to Istanbul, Tbilisi, Prague, Vienna, Amsterdam, New York, and beyond. Over the course of four years, they continue to report the truth to Russians from exile, covering their country’s war crimes, even as they face death threats and are declared extremists and terrorists—as they find new meanings of family, friendship, love, and home far from the country to which they may never return. (Viewers can follow EXILE without first seeing LAST AIR IN MOSCOW.)

title: VOICE OF LA RAZA and THE FIRST WORLD FESTIVAL OF NEGRO ARTS
description: “The film appeals, beginning with the term la raza, or ‘the people,’ in its title, to the spirit of the radical movements that had emerged in Mexican-American and Puerto Rican communities during the late 1960s... Shot in 16mm on the streets of Los Angeles, New York, and Albuquerque, Voice of La Raza focuses on everyday people, with significant portions devoted to sequences of Quinn engaged in conversation with young people on the street. In heavily accented English, street slang, or with traces of regional accents, these men (and one young woman), shown in close-up, recount their experiences of being discriminated against by employers or educators.” – Laura Isabel Serna, William Greaves, Filmmaking as Mission (Columbia University Press, 2021) The official documentary film of the festival held in Dakar, Senegal in 1966, in which over 2,000 writers, artists, and performers from Africa and the African Diaspora participated. Featuring Duke Ellington, Langston Hughes, Alvin Ailey, Aimé Césaire, Leopold Senghor, and many other artists, performers, and dignitaries from thirty countries. “You have to realize that the reason why I went into motion pictures was to make films like The First World Festival of Negro Arts. It was the first opportunity I had to make films that expressed a black perspective on reality. Until then I had not had access to financing which would permit that.” – William Greaves

title: ONCE UPON A TIME IN HARLEM
description: August 1972: A reunion of Harlem Renaissance luminaries is held at Duke Ellington’s St. Nicholas Ave. townhouse. Though many of these figures haven’t seen each other in 50 years, sharp memories, vigorous debates, and unsettled scores soon flow through this stunner of a cocktail party, which features (among others): artists Romare Bearden, Aaron Douglas, and Richard Bruce Nugent; composer Eubie Blake; poet Arna Bontemps; photographer James Van Der Zee; and activists Richard B. Moore and Louise Patterson. After organizing and shooting this extraordinary gathering, filmmaker William Greaves (SYMBIOPSYCHOTAXIPLASM: TAKE ONE) was unable to complete the film before his death in 2014. One of the cameramen that day was his son David, who expertly reshaped this never-before-seen, newly-restored footage into “a film for the ages…one of the greatest cinematic works of creative nonfiction that I’ve ever seen.” – Richard Brody, The New Yorker

title: STILL A BROTHER: INSIDE THE NEGRO MIDDLE CLASS and IN THE COMPANY OF MEN
description: Completed and originally aired by National Educational Television in the wake of the assassination of Martin Luther King Jr., STILL A BROTHER: INSIDE THE NEGRO MIDDE CLASS continues to resonate as one of the most searching cinematic explorations of African American identity in relation to class in the United States. William Greaves probes the expansion of the Black middle class to uncover enduring social discrimination and economic inequality on the basis of racial difference. In the process, he finds both seismic conflict and hopeful development within a Black community increasingly rejecting the false promises of upward mobility: the emergence of progressivism in the typically apolitical Black bourgeoisie; the strengthening ties between traditional Black Christianity and militant Black power; the rise of the “Black is beautiful” movement to counter racial self-hatred; and the call among activist youth for Black history to enter the academic and cultural mainstream. Narrated by actor Ossie Davis—and featuring trenchant interviews with Black leaders as well as searing footage from the decade’s civil-rights protests and ghetto uprisings—STILL A BROTHER questions the possibility of racial advancement undercapitalism by formulating alternative paths toward a truly egalitarian society. “Examines racial friction between white management and chronically underemployed African Americans in a Southern auto plant. Greaves’s idea was to use a Moreno-trained psychodramatist, Walter Klavun, to create a sociodrama to deal with racial conflict within the workplace. His approach proved to be novel for a sponsored film.” – J. J. Murphy, William Greaves, Filmmaking as Mission (Columbia University Press, 2021)

title: UNZIPPED
description: “Isaac Mizrahi as he conceived and contorted the way through to his fall 1994 show, [dashing] around a deserted SoHo with pal Sandra Bernhard; [meeting] with Naomi Campbell, Linda Evangelista, and baby Kate Moss for fittings; and [racing] uptown to an audience with Eartha Kitt... Hair-raising deadlines, delirious Bette Davis impressions, and the hostile but exhilarating act of executing a designer’s vision come together in a work that set the bar for all fashion films after.” – Vogue

title: A BRONX TALE
description: Rose-tinted nostalgia collides with hardbitten realities in Robert De Niro’s stylish and sensitive ‘60s-set directorial debut, a knotty morality play in the well-tailored clothes of a mobster flick. Coming of age on the cusp of change, a boy’s divided loyalties reflect a struggle for America’s soul.

title: SYMBIOPSYCHOTAXIPLASM: TAKE ONE
description: Screen tests are being shot in Central Park for the leads in a possible feature, while another crew films the filming of the tests, and a third films the first two in the context of life in the park going on around them. Avant-garde verité that slipped off the radar for 30 years. The official documentary film of the festival held in Dakar, Senegal in 1966, in which over 2,000 writers, artists, and performers from Africa and the African Diaspora participated. title: The History of Concrete
description: Fri, Sep 18: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Edy Modica (actress, comedian, filmmaker), after 4:40 show! Fri, Sep 18: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Rachel Kaly (comedian, writer, actor), after 7:15 show! Sun, Sep 20: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Sarah Sherman after 2:10 show! Following the finale of his TV show, filmmaker John Wilson searches for a new creative outlet. After attending a workshop on how to write and sell a Hallmark movie, he attempts to apply the same formula to a documentary about concrete.

title: One in a Million
description: Wed, Oct 21: Q&A with dirs. Itab Azzam and Jack MacInnes and film subject Israa, moderated by Julie Goldman, after 7:00 show! Thurs, Oct 22: Q&A with dirs. Itab Azzam and Jack MacInnes and film subject Israa after 7:00 show! Filmed over ten years, ONE IN A MILLION follows Israa from childhood to adulthood on an extraordinary journey from Syria to Germany — and back again. We first meet her at age 11 as she and her family are preparing to cross the Aegean Sea, risking everything in search of safety and a better life in Europe. What unfolds is a deeply personal chronicle of war, exile and heartbreak, as Israa grows up navigating adolescence, identity and belonging far from the home she was forced to leave. As Israa settles into life in Germany, new freedoms collide with the stabilizing pull of Syrian traditions, testing bonds and reshaping her sense of self. Co-directed by Itab Azzam and Jack MacInnes, the film bears witness to the remarkable trust between filmmakers and family, following Israa and her loved ones across borders, cultures and shifting circumstances. An intimate and nuanced coming-of-age story, ONE IN A MILLION illuminates the complexities of the refugee experience while asking a universal question: what does it truly mean to call a place home? Additional showtimes for Oct 21-27 to be announced.

title: The Devils
description: All screenings on a new 35mm print of the 4K restoration of the film. An enduring, singular masterpiece of cinema starring Academy Award-winner Vanessa Redgrave and Oliver Reed, KEN RUSSELL’S THE DEVILS is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption – and a defining work of art from seminal filmmaker Ken Russell. Assembled from the original camera negative, this new 4K restoration presents Ken Russell’s definitive vision of The Devils by referencing the edit he privately constructed in 2004. The film’s sound has been remastered from original English Composite 35mm Mag Film, transferred at 96kHz, plus other original film elements in selected spots as needed. The Picture and Sound restoration was performed by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color, and Warner Bros. Sound.

title: The Great Experiment
description: Fri, Oct 16: Q&A with co-director Steve Maing, moderated by filmmaker Laura Poitras ( Citizenfour ) after 7:15 show! Sat, Oct 17: Q&A with co-director Steve Maing & True/False Fest Artistic Director Farihah Zaman, moderated by filmmaker Geeta Gandbhir after 7:15 show! What holds a people together when the story they tell about themselves begins to fracture? THE GREAT EXPERIMENT is an epic poem in documentary form – a mirror held to an American nation at war with its own reflection, asking not who is right, but whether the experiment itself can survive. Filmed in striking black and white across the US over four consequential years, from 2017 to 2021, the film considers the results of what George Washington once called “our last great experiment” in democracy. Additional showtimes for October 16-22 to be announced. Previously screening as part of DOC NYC Selects: Summer 2026

title: SYMBIOPSYCHOTAXIPLASM: TAKE 2½
description: “TAKE 2½ returns to the scene of the original experiment, creates a new scenario built upon the events of the past, and sets about another aggressive peeling away of artifice and falsity, not just in the performances but in the filmmaking itself. The result is a uniquely exhilarating movie about moviemaking in which we are never quite certain whether we are situated behind the scenes or in front of them.” – Scott Foundas, LA Weekly

title: Fjord (Open Captioning)
description: Tue, Oct 6: Sneak preview + Q&A with director Cristian Mungiu and co-star Sebastian Stan after the 6:15 show! Tues, Oct 6: Extended intro with director Cristian Mungiu and co-star Sebastian Stan at the 8:15 show! Please note that there are additional showtimes of FJORD that screen without open captions (on-screen display of dialogue and sounds). For those showtimes, click here. From two-time Palme d’Or winner Cristian Mungiu, a Norwegian woman and her devout Romanian husband relocate with their five children to a remote, close-knit, coastal town. Their teenage children form a fast bond with a neighboring family as unease begins to simmer around their rigid beliefs. When allegations of abuse emerge, they are forced to confront a system of judgment that blurs the line between concern and prejudice.

title: Naza
description: In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them. We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA ’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence. — Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

description: “We have such sights to show you…” In horror polymath Clive Barker’s adaptation of his novella The Hellbound Heart , horny hedonist Uncle Frank plays with a mysterious puzzle box, summons the Cenobites (led by Doug Bradley in an iconic performance) and endangers his unsuspecting niece (Ashley Laurence). A work of remarkable specificity and imagination, this inimitable, hot and bothered horror landmark is presented in a new 4K restoration. “The best horror film ever to be made in Britain.” – Melody Maker Opens Wed Oct 21, showtimes to be announced.

title: MIRACLE IN HARLEM
description: “Generally considered a technical landmark in the history of race movies, MIRACLE IN HARLEM appeared toward the end of the early Black independent film movement. Ostensibly the movie’s a murder mystery centering on a candy-store swindle. But beneath its glossy veneer lies an interesting subtext: it’s a look at post-World War II Black America’s vision of its new tomorrow of promise and prosperity. Its lead characters—serious, noble, educated, bourgeois, less ethnic—stand as embodiments of the new social/economic philosophy: they are attractive, optimistic, capitalistic go-getters, who believe in the American system of free enterprise and are determined to make the system work for them.” – Donald Bogle, Blacks in American Film and Television (Garland Publishing, 1988) Collection of the Smithsonian National Museum of African American History and Culture, Gift of Randall and Sam Nieman

title: Miss Representation: Rise Up
description: Thu, Oct 22: Q&A w/ Reshma Saujani (Founder, Moms First and Girls Who Code) and Alyse Nelson (CEO, Vital Voices) after 6:30 show! Over a decade after MISS REPRESENTATION exposed the media’s contribution to the underrepresentation of women in leadership, this follow-up dives deep into the cultural backlash against women’s agency and power. With the proliferation of AI and deepfakes, a new era of tech-facilitated violence is exacerbating sexism and misogyny in an attempt to control and silence women and girls. With inspiring young women at its core, MISS REPRESENTATION: RISE UP interweaves their personal journeys with powerful voices in media, culture, leadership, and academia to reimagine a future that finally uplifts women and girls.

title: Naza
description: In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them. We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA ’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence. — Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

title: Fjord
description: Tue, Oct 6: Sneak preview + Q&A with director Cristian Mungiu and co-star Sebastian Stan after the 6:15 show! Tues, Oct 6: Extended intro with director Cristian Mungiu and co-star Sebastian Stan at the 8:15 show! From two-time Palme d’Or winner Cristian Mungiu, a Norwegian woman and her devout Romanian husband relocate with their five children to a remote, close-knit, coastal town. Their teenage children form a fast bond with a neighboring family as unease begins to simmer around their rigid beliefs. When allegations of abuse emerge, they are forced to confront a system of judgment that blurs the line between concern and prejudice.

title: Portrait (ПОРТРЕТ)
description: Portrait (ПОРТРЕТ). 2002. Russia. Written and directed by Sergei Loznitsa. DCP courtesy Atoms & Void. No dialogue. 28 min. Ominous rain clouds, a recurring trope of Sergei Loznitsa’s early films, once again gather as the curtains open on Portrait. Like some contemporary August Sander, Loznitsa documents the Russian peasantry in stark frontal poses. The commonality of rural life anywhere and everywhere—the familiar weather-bitten faces, the stock expressions of humility and resilience, the well-handled tools of the trade, whether axe or logging sled or wheelbarrow—is belied by the evocative specificity of their particular circumstances: the two men who could pass for twins, the lumberjack with his crosscut saw poised in mid-action, the hobo (hobo?) who with his rucksack seems to be just heading off to the train behind him. These characters, or their types, seem frozen in time and place, but the landscape is perpetually changing, from the icy winter with its unforgiving winds to the spring thaw of birdsong, dandelion seeds, and freshly tilled earth in shimmering heat. Settlement (ПОСЕЛЕНИЕ). 2001. Russia. Written and directed by Sergei Loznitsa. DCP courtesy Atoms & Void. 80 min. Winner of a jury prize at the Karlovy Vary Film Festival, Sergei Loznitsa’s debut feature observes the daily lives of people with mental disabilities in Oksochi, a communal psychiatric hospital in the Russian countryside. There is an air of peaceful contentment as the men and women tend the livestock, air the carpets, write letters, and read books, but darker images also intrude: images of collective fieldwork, silent canteen meals, and uniformly shaved heads that seem to echo a Soviet past of castigation, confinement, and rote labor. Loznitsa’s language is vernacular and unvarnished, his camera positioned frontally or at a remove, his soundscape an almost hyperreal concatenation of buzz saw, crackling fire, and muttered chatter. The film’s denouement, a progression of portraits set to Vladimir Vavilov’s “Ave Maria,” ennobles and enriches this marginalized community. Tragically, in 2013, 12 years after the film’s release, a fire tore through the 19th-century timber hospital, killing 36 patients and a nurse who tried to rescue them.

title: The Devils
description: All screenings on a new 35mm print of the 4K restoration of the film. An enduring, singular masterpiece of cinema starring Academy Award-winner Vanessa Redgrave and Oliver Reed, KEN RUSSELL’S THE DEVILS is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption – and a defining work of art from seminal filmmaker Ken Russell. Assembled from the original camera negative, this new 4K restoration presents Ken Russell’s definitive vision of The Devils by referencing the edit he privately constructed in 2004. The film’s sound has been remastered from original English Composite 35mm Mag Film, transferred at 96kHz, plus other original film elements in selected spots as needed. The Picture and Sound restoration was performed by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color, and Warner Bros. Sound.

title: UNZIPPED
description: “Isaac Mizrahi as he conceived and contorted the way through to his fall 1994 show, [dashing] around a deserted SoHo with pal Sandra Bernhard; [meeting] with Naomi Campbell, Linda Evangelista, and baby Kate Moss for fittings; and [racing] uptown to an audience with Eartha Kitt... Hair-raising deadlines, delirious Bette Davis impressions, and the hostile but exhilarating act of executing a designer’s vision come together in a work that set the bar for all fashion films after.” – Vogue

title: FROM THESE ROOTS and BLACK POWER IN AMERICA: MYTH… OR REALITY?
description: “A return to Greaves’s own roots growing up in Harlem. With little stock footage of Harlem and its intellectuals available, Greaves decided to construct a film composed exclusively of photographs. What emerged was a compelling portrait of a community made strong by relative freedom and opportunity. Within the larger context of documentary practice, the film helped to inaugurate a cycle of city neighborhood films that focused on local communities.” – Adam Knee and Charles Musser, William Greaves, Filmmaking as Mission (Columbia University Press, 2021) Through interviews with prominent Black leaders including Franklin Thomas, head of the Ford Foundation, and congresswoman Eleanor Holmes Norton, this documentary examines how the Civil Rights Movement of the 1960s changed the Black community and the rest of American society.

title: FATHERLAND
description: From the director of IDA and COLD WAR: FATHERLAND follows Nobel Prize-winning author Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler, KINGS OF THE ROAD) and his actress daughter Erika (Sandra Hüller, ANATOMY OF A FALL) as they drive across a war-ravaged 1949 Germany. Returning home after years of exile in the U.S. and exuding a superhuman gravitas, Mann finds the Germany he knew to be gone, replaced by a country with contradictory ideologies. Erika, who acts as his travel coordinator and translator, strives to pierce his detached persona while quietly struggling with a family tragedy.

title: ONCE UPON A TIME IN HARLEM
description: August 1972: A reunion of Harlem Renaissance luminaries is held at Duke Ellington’s St. Nicholas Ave. townhouse. Though many of these figures haven’t seen each other in 50 years, sharp memories, vigorous debates, and unsettled scores soon flow through this stunner of a cocktail party, which features (among others): artists Romare Bearden, Aaron Douglas, and Richard Bruce Nugent; composer Eubie Blake; poet Arna Bontemps; photographer James Van Der Zee; and activists Richard B. Moore and Louise Patterson. title: The History of Concrete
description: Fri, Sep 18: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Edy Modica (actress, comedian, filmmaker), after 4:40 show! Fri, Sep 18: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Rachel Kaly (comedian, writer, actor), after 7:15 show! Sun, Sep 20: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Sarah Sherman after 2:10 show! Following the finale of his TV show, filmmaker John Wilson searches for a new creative outlet. After attending a workshop on how to write and sell a Hallmark movie, he attempts to apply the same formula to a documentary about concrete.

title: FREDERICK DOUGLASS: AN AMERICAN LIFE and BOOKER T. WASHINGTON: THE LIFE AND THE LEGACY
description: This short biopic depicts the incredible life of Frederick Douglass, one of the most important political thinkers and social advocates in American history. Born into slavery, Douglass (Hugh Morgan) taught himself how to read and write and eventually escaped bondage; in the North, he found his calling as an activist, speaker, and writer for the abolitionist cause, with his autobiography Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass, an American Slave becoming one of the movement’s central texts. Directing from a script he cowrote, William Greaves celebrates Douglass’s monumental accomplishments yet refuses to shy away from darker moments, such as Douglass’s ambivalent relationship with abolitionist John Brown or his children’s opposition to his controversial second marriage. Infusing fiction with elements of documentary, William Greaves’s short biopic of legendary African American activist Booker T. Washington focuses on how his leadership of the Tuskegee Institute—which equally emphasized practical labor skills and classroom learning—influenced educational philosophy and practice throughout the United States. Screenwriter Lou Potter sets the action during the lifetime of Washington (Maurice Woods), but a modern-day narrator (Gil Noble) interviews the historical personages—and frequently challenges their answers. This experimental format highlights the still-contentious nature of Washington’s political stances, especially his accommodationist strategy for Black integration within the racially hostile South.

title: Bread Day preceded by The Train Stop
description: Every Tuesday, the scant elderly residents of an isolated, nearly abandoned village outside St. Petersburg push an unmanned train car along a spur off the main line that leads into town, supplying themselves and their neighbors with a week’s daily bread—a ritual that, in Dvortsevoy’s hands, appears as both a miracle of tenacity and a pointed commentary on systemic dysfunction. Screens with The Train Stop, Loznitsa’s sumptuously photographed record of sleepers in a station waiting room. “In Loznitsa’s The Train Stop, in the middle of the night, the train doesn’t arrive. The waiting room is full of heavy sleepers, some folded over on their laps, some splayed out over the benches. What could rouse them? Maybe the answer is not a train, but a film. Consider Dvortsevoy’s similarly existential Bread Day. Sure, the rickety cart carrying the week’s delivery of bread to Township 3 of Zhikharevo barely seems to count as a train. It’s manually pushed by the pensioners who will soon argue strenuously with each other as they divvy up its contents. But their shouting is so vigorous, their insults so inventive, that questions of categorization quickly dissipate as the elderly residents, their goats in tow, battle to have the last word.” —Series curator Genevieve Yue The Train Stop (Sergei Loznitsa, 2000, 25 mins) Bread Day (Sergei Dvortsevoy, 1998, 55 mins) Introduction by Genevieve Yue on Saturday, September 5th Part of Trains: Local Routes

title: TROMEO AND JULIET (Lloyd Kaufman in person on Sun, Nov 1!)
description: “The first of director Lloyd Kaufman’s official adaptations of William Shakespeare, TROMEO & JULIET is a wild, punk reimagining of The Bard’s eternal doomed romance, only with non-stop gore, nudity, and giant mutant genitals! Set amongst the denizens and outcasts of squalid New Jersey, standing in for a modern vision of Verona, and featuring a screenplay co-written by soon-to-be major director in his own right, James Gunn (SLITHER, GUARDIANS OF THE GALAXY), TROMEO features scream queen Debbie Rochon, Sean Gunn in his on-screen debut, music superstar Lemmy (Motörhead), and Will Keenan as Tromeo.” –VINEGAR SYNDROME Lloyd Kaufman will be here in person, along with actor Will Keenan, on Sun, Nov 1 at 3:30!

title: Once Upon a Time in... Hollywood (70mm)
description: Quentin Tarantino’s Once Upon a Time in… Hollywood visits 1969 Los Angeles, where everything is changing, as TV star Rick Dalton (Leonardo DiCaprio) and his longtime stunt double Cliff Booth (Brad Pitt) make their way around an industry they hardly recognize anymore. The ninth film from the writer-director features a large ensemble cast and multiple storylines in a tribute to the final moments of Hollywood’s golden age.

title: WIF x AC Spooky Shorts Night
description: Join the American Cinematheque and WIF for a specially curated night of spooky short films from women directors, as well as a Q&A with the filmmakers.

title: One in a Million
description: Wed, Oct 21: Q&A with dirs. Itab Azzam and Jack MacInnes and film subject Israa, moderated by Julie Goldman, after 7:00 show! Thurs, Oct 22: Q&A with dirs. Itab Azzam and Jack MacInnes and film subject Israa after 7:00 show! Filmed over ten years, ONE IN A MILLION follows Israa from childhood to adulthood on an extraordinary journey from Syria to Germany — and back again. We first meet her at age 11 as she and her family are preparing to cross the Aegean Sea, risking everything in search of safety and a better life in Europe. What unfolds is a deeply personal chronicle of war, exile and heartbreak, as Israa grows up navigating adolescence, identity and belonging far from the home she was forced to leave. As Israa settles into life in Germany, new freedoms collide with the stabilizing pull of Syrian traditions, testing bonds and reshaping her sense of self. Co-directed by Itab Azzam and Jack MacInnes, the film bears witness to the remarkable trust between filmmakers and family, following Israa and her loved ones across borders, cultures and shifting circumstances. An intimate and nuanced coming-of-age story, ONE IN A MILLION illuminates the complexities of the refugee experience while asking a universal question: what does it truly mean to call a place home? Additional showtimes for Oct 21-27 to be announced.

title: Possible Love
description: The lives of two married couples from different social strata collide in Lee Chang-dong’s brilliantly unfolding narrative about economic precarity, in which a laid-off factory worker and his wife become the camera subjects for a documentary filmmaker. Winner of the Silver Lion at the 2026 Venice Film Festival and South Korea’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: STILL A BROTHER: INSIDE THE NEGRO MIDDLE CLASS and IN THE COMPANY OF MEN
description: Completed and originally aired by National Educational Television in the wake of the assassination of Martin Luther King Jr., STILL A BROTHER: INSIDE THE NEGRO MIDDE CLASS continues to resonate as one of the most searching cinematic explorations of African American identity in relation to class in the United States. William Greaves probes the expansion of the Black middle class to uncover enduring social discrimination and economic inequality on the basis of racial difference. In the process, he finds both seismic conflict and hopeful development within a Black community increasingly rejecting the false promises of upward mobility: the emergence of progressivism in the typically apolitical Black bourgeoisie; the strengthening ties between traditional Black Christianity and militant Black power; the rise of the “Black is beautiful” movement to counter racial self-hatred; and the call among activist youth for Black history to enter the academic and cultural mainstream. Narrated by actor Ossie Davis—and featuring trenchant interviews with Black leaders as well as searing footage from the decade’s civil-rights protests and ghetto uprisings—STILL A BROTHER questions the possibility of racial advancement undercapitalism by formulating alternative paths toward a truly egalitarian society. “Examines racial friction between white management and chronically underemployed African Americans in a Southern auto plant. Greaves’s idea was to use a Moreno-trained psychodramatist, Walter Klavun, to create a sociodrama to deal with racial conflict within the workplace. His approach proved to be novel for a sponsored film.” – J. J. Murphy, William Greaves, Filmmaking as Mission (Columbia University Press, 2021)

title: The Taking of Pelham One Two Three
description: Lower East Side native Walter Matthau wears perhaps the broadest tie in film history as a grousing Transit Authority lieutenant who gets an unlikely shot at heroism when a group of criminals take a downtown 6 train hostage and demand a million dollars from the flat-broke city. Engineered with perfect pace and verve by the underrated Sargent, with growly, jowly Matthau at his hangdog best. “Featuring one of the grittiest New Yorkers ever seen on film: the ruddy-cheeked wino who, despite the commotion on her hijacked 6 train, sleeps through the entire ordeal.” —Series curator Genevieve Yue Introduction by Genevieve Yue and Erika Balsom, with a book signing following the screening, on Saturday, October 3rd Part of Trains: Local Routes

title: House of Wax
description: Part of our Dark Castle series presented by Justin LaLiberty

title: Virgina
description: When a fourth daughter is born to a family “cursed” by superstition to bear no male heirs, the decision is made to raise the child with a boy’s name—Stevan—as well as a man’s rights and responsibilities… though as Stevan passes adolescence, first love and a brush with personal tragedy will spark rebellion in his breast. An acutely observed study of a 19th-century peasant culture steeped in misogyny, and a strikingly sensual story of self-discovery, presented in a new 2K restoration in its NYC premiere. “I’ve gotten to do many cool and amazing things in my work over the years, but tracking down the negative of Virgina, after the director Srđan Karanović thought it had been lost in the aftermath of the Yugoslav Wars, is definitely one of the highlights of my career. Virgina is a stunning film, a complex and interesting narrative about gender, with unique pleasures for a queer audience.” —Series curator Jenni Olson, queer film historian and archivist The new 2K restoration was completed by the Department for Digitisation and Digital Restoration of the Yugoslav Film Archive in Belgrade. The film was scanned from a 35mm internegative using an ArriscanXT scanner with archival gate overscan, with color correction by Masha Badalić under the supervision of director Srđan Karanović. Audio was sourced from the original 35mm mono sound negative and restored by the Sound Department of the Academy of Arts in Novi Sad. An Altered Innocence release Introduction and post-screening discussion by Jenni Olson on Friday, October 23rd Introduction by Jenni Olson on Saturday, October 24th Part of Jenni Olson Selects: Mini Masc

Poland’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

description: In 1972, legendary filmmaker William Greaves gathered an extraordinary group of artists, writers, actors, musicians, and thinkers of the Harlem Renaissance. After more than 50 years, his son David Greaves has completed his breathtaking miracle of a movie.

description: “The debut from Black filmmaker Ronald K. Armstrong, BUGGED is an ultra-fun and ambitious DIY creature feature. Following a freak lab accident with major RE-ANIMATOR vibes, a woman named Devine hires the Dead and Buried Exterminators to rid her house of some overgrown crickets. The bug-busters soon realize that these aren’t just large crickets, but radioactive beasties with a lust for blood! Filled with goopy practical effects and a charming mood, BUGGED is an important and overlooked chapter of 1990s horror from a Black perspective.” –AGFA

We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA ’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence. — Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

title: The History of Concrete
description: Fri, Sep 18: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Edy Modica (actress, comedian, filmmaker), after 4:40 show! Fri, Sep 18: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Rachel Kaly (comedian, writer, actor), after 7:15 show! Sun, Sep 20: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Sarah Sherman after 2:10 show! Following the finale of his TV show, filmmaker John Wilson searches for a new creative outlet. After attending a workshop on how to write and sell a Hallmark movie, he attempts to apply the same formula to a documentary about concrete.

title: JIGOKU
description: Shocking, outrageous and poetic, JIGOKU (HELL, a.k.a. THE SINNERS OF HELL ) is the most innovative creation from Nobuo Nakagawa, the father of the Japanese horror film. After a young theology student flees a hit-and-run accident, he is plagued by both his own guilt-ridden conscience and a mysterious, diabolical doppelgänger. But all possible escape routes lead straight to hell—literally. In the gloriously gory final third of the film, Nakagawa offers up his vision of the underworld in a tour de force of torture and degradation. A striking departure from traditional Japanese ghost stories, JIGOKU, with its truly eye-popping (and -gouging) imagery, created aftershocks that are still reverberating in contemporary world horror cinema.

title: Chungking Express
description: A hot-shot to the heart, pop masterpiece Chungking Express tells the stories of two lovelorn cops (Takeshi Kaneshiro and Tony Leung) and the women who baffle them (Brigitte Lin and Faye Wong, who contributes a Cantopop cover of The Cranberries’ “Dreams”), its bifurcated structure suggesting the A- and B-sides of a 45. Wong’s international breakthrough introduced new audiences to his rich, sensorial brand of filmmaking, inviting one to disappear into, sink into, live inside, a voluptuary world bigger and brighter than our own—but just as heartbreaking. Part of Like the Wind: Lensed by Christopher Doyle

title: Ghost in the Shell: 30th Anniversary Remaster
description: “My codename is Project 2501, and I am a life form that was born in a sea of information.” In the year 2029, the world looks like a hybridization of Hong Kong, Tokyo, and New York, yielding to entropy and technocracy. Cyborg Major Kusanagi, a perfect specimen of human-brained computer engineering is on the case to track and destroy an omnipotent entity known as The Puppet Master—a hacker? a virus?—who threatens world order. Her physical and existential journey deftly detailed by Oshii’s animation, combining traditional hand-drawn cells and computer-generated graphics, creating a haunting, awe-inspiring magnum opus. Part of A Cyberpunk Canon

title: The Others             / The Orphanage
description: In 1945, Grace Stewart (Nicole Kidman) and her two children live an unusually isolated existence behind the locked doors and drawn curtains of a secluded mansion on one of the Channel Islands. The arrival of mysterious new servants (Fionnula Flanagan, Ed Sykes) and her apparently war-fatigued husband Charles (Christopher Eccleston), raise the unworldly feeling that there is far more to this house than can be seen, provoking Grace into a terrifying fight to save her children and preserve her sanity. (Rialto Pictures)

title: Extra Geography
description: Set in an English boarding school, Extra Geography follows two teenage girls as they grapple with all the challenges of girlhood: friendship, boys, studies, growing up and their summer project, "to fall in love".

title: The History of Concrete

John Wilson, moderated by Rachel Kaly (comedian, writer, actor), after 7:15 show! Sun, Sep 20: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Sarah Sherman after 2:10 show! title: Closure
description: After his teenage son, Chris, is last seen by a surveillance camera on a bridge over Warsaw’s turbulent Vistula River, Daniel embarks on an all-consuming search. Armed with self-built boats, drones, and underwater cameras, he relentlessly scours the river’s depths. As months pass, while his own family struggles to live with the uncertainty of Chris’s disappearance, Daniel begins helping other families with missing loved ones find answers — and, at times, the closure that continues to elude him. Additional showtimes for Oct 30-Nov 3 to be announced.

title: Possible Love
description: Four strangers' paths cross by chance, leading to complex emotional entanglements that challenge their existing relationships and force them to confront uncomfortable truths about love and commitment.

title: The Devils
description: All screenings on a new 35mm print of the 4K restoration of the film. An enduring, singular masterpiece of cinema starring Academy Award-winner Vanessa Redgrave and Oliver Reed, KEN RUSSELL’S THE DEVILS is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption – and a defining work of art from seminal filmmaker Ken Russell. Assembled from the original camera negative, this new 4K restoration presents Ken Russell’s definitive vision of The Devils by referencing the edit he privately constructed in 2004. The film’s sound has been remastered from original English Composite 35mm Mag Film, transferred at 96kHz, plus other original film elements in selected spots as needed. The Picture and Sound restoration was performed by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color, and Warner Bros. Sound.

title: On The Road
description: ‘Veneno’, a rebellious young drifter, frequents roadside diners where he sleeps with truck drivers. Urgently needing a ride, he meets ‘Muñeco’, a hard-edged driver who keeps to himself. He convinces Muñeco to take him deep into the hyper-masculine world of long-haul trucking across the north of Mexico. As they travel together and an unexpected intimacy builds between them, shadows from Veneno’s past resurface, putting both their lives at risk. Regular engagement begins Wed, Oct 28 – showtimes to be announced.

title: Tad and the Magic Lamp
description: A family of archeologists find a magic lamp that sends them back in time in this animated fantasy comedy adventure.

title: Paw Patrol 3: The Dino Movie
description: The Paw Patrol lands on a mysterious dinosaur island after a storm, where they meet Rex, a stranded pup. When Humdinger's reckless mining triggers a volcano, the team faces their biggest rescue mission yet to save the island Sunday 2nd Aug 11am Charity Screening All proceeds from this performance will be donated to MEDICINEMA Cinema-based healthcare programmes inside hospitals

title: Monster Mia
description: All her life, Mia (12) has not only felt out of place in her town, she has felt out of place in her own family. Her twin sister, Marie, is the picture-perfect Primrose girl – permanently dressed in pink and puppy obsessed. Mia, on the other hand, loves skateboarding, quirky clothes, and her scruffy pet rat, Quentin. After one too many problems at school, the Primrose headmistress transfers Mia to the mysterious Rotwood Academy to work on her behavior. Rotwood is nothing like Primrose. It’s dark, bat-infested, and it gives Mia the creeps. The place looks more like a castle than a school. And that’s not even the craziest part. At Rotwood, the students are... monsters! This must be a mistake. Monsters and humans do NOT get along. Mia can’t let anyone at Rotwood know she’s a human or she could be in serious trouble. Her only option is to convince everyone that she’s a monster, too until she can get the heck out of that creepy school. As time goes on, Mia begins to realize that her monster classmates aren’t so different from her former human classmates. She even finds some friends who take her under their wing. Paprika is a vampire and Oskar is a... well, Oskar’s head keeps fall- ing off. Mia has finally found a place where she belongs. But things aren’t all sunshine and roses at her new monster school. Vice Principal Van Vlad has a particular disdain for humans and Mia has a feeling he’s plotting something dreadful.

title: Nadja
description: In 1993, invited by David Lynch to come up with a low-budget genre movie, Michael Almereyda ( Tesla , Experimenter , Hamlet ) came up with a moody, postmodern reimagining of the Dracula myth which draws inspiration from Dracula’s Daughter (1936) and André Breton’s surrealist novel Nadja . The film follows estranged vampire twins Nadja (Elina Löwensohn) and Edgar (a young Jared Harris) as they reunite following their father’s death by the flamboyantly unhinged Dr. Van Helsing, played with relish by Peter Fonda. The film’s striking visuals combine high-contrast black-and-white 35mm cinematography with the hallucinatory grain of Pixelvision video is now newly restored in 4K.

title: ONCE UPON A TIME IN HARLEM
description: August 1972: A reunion of Harlem Renaissance luminaries is held at Duke Ellington’s St. Nicholas Ave. townhouse. Though many of these figures haven’t seen each other in 50 years, sharp memories, vigorous debates, and unsettled scores soon flow through this stunner of a cocktail party, which features (among others): artists Romare Bearden, Aaron Douglas, and Richard Bruce Nugent; composer Eubie Blake; poet Arna Bontemps; photographer James Van Der Zee; and activists Richard B. Moore and Louise Patterson. After organizing and shooting this extraordinary gathering, filmmaker William Greaves (SYMBIOPSYCHOTAXIPLASM: TAKE ONE) was unable to complete the film before his death in 2014. One of the cameramen that day was his son David, who expertly reshaped this never-before-seen, newly-restored footage into “a film for the ages…one of the greatest cinematic works of creative nonfiction that I’ve ever seen.” – Richard Brody, The New Yorker

title: Forgotten Island
description: When two best friends are sucked through a magical portal they find themselves menaced by a dangerous creature and in danger of losing the memories that bond them together.

title: FATHERLAND
description: From the director of IDA and COLD WAR: FATHERLAND follows Nobel Prize-winning author Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler, KINGS OF THE ROAD) and his actress daughter Erika (Sandra Hüller, ANATOMY OF A FALL) as they drive across a war-ravaged 1949 Germany. Returning home after years of exile in the U.S. and exuding a superhuman gravitas, Mann finds the Germany he knew to be gone, replaced by a country with contradictory ideologies. Erika, who acts as his travel coordinator and translator, strives to pierce his detached persona while quietly struggling with a family tragedy.

title: MY UNDESIRABLE FRIENDS: PART II – EXILE: Chapters 4-5
description: When Russia shuts down all independent media, a group of young dissident journalists must flee Moscow so they can keep reporting and not go to prison. In her riveting follow-up to last year’s awards-sweeping MY UNDESIRABLE FRIENDS — LAST AIR IN MOSCOW, Julia Loktev follows these courageous, sharply funny women (and a few men) as they fan out across a dozen countries, to Istanbul, Tbilisi, Prague, Vienna, Amsterdam, New York, and beyond. Over the course of four years, they continue to report the truth to Russians from exile, covering their country’s war crimes, even as they face death threats and are declared extremists and terrorists—as they find new meanings of family, friendship, love, and home far from the country to which they may never return. (Viewers can follow EXILE without first seeing LAST AIR IN MOSCOW.)

title: Fatherland
description: Oscar-nominated director Paweł Pawlikowski (Cold War, NYFF56) won Best Director at Cannes for his most potent film yet, following novelist Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler) and his daughter Erika Mann (Sandra Hüller) on a road trip across Germany in the aftermath of World War II. Poland’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: Suspiria [1977]
description: Suzy (Jessica Harper) travels to Germany to attend ballet school. When she arrives, late on a stormy night, no one lets her in, and she sees Pat (Eva Axén), another student, fleeing from the school. When Pat reaches her apartment, she is murdered. The next day, Suzy is admitted to her new school, but has a difficult time settling in. She hears noises, and often feels ill. As more people die, Suzy uncovers the terrifying secret history of the place.

title: Disney Junior Cinema Club 2026
description: Packed with fun for preschoolers and their grown-ups, this interactive big-screen experience brings together some favourite Disney Junior stories from Mickey Mouse Clubhouse+, Minnie's Bow-Toons: Pet Hotel, Marvel's Iron Man and His Awesome Friends, Sofia the First: Royal Magic and Toy Story Toons, in a fun-filled extravaganza! Expect sing-alongs, dance moments, exciting games and magical surprises, where audience participation is a must.

title: Fjord
description: Tue, Oct 6: Sneak preview + Q&A with director Cristian Mungiu and co-star Sebastian Stan after the 6:15 show! Tues, Oct 6: Extended intro with director Cristian Mungiu and co-star Sebastian Stan at the 8:15 show! From two-time Palme d’Or winner Cristian Mungiu, a Norwegian woman and her devout Romanian husband relocate with their five children to a remote, close-knit, coastal town. Their teenage children form a fast bond with a neighboring family as unease begins to simmer around their rigid beliefs. When allegations of abuse emerge, they are forced to confront a system of judgment that blurs the line between concern and prejudice.

title: In The Mood For Love
description: In 1962 Hong Kong, neighbors Su Li-zhen (Mrs. Chan) and Chow Mo-wan (Mr. Chow) discover their spouses are having an affair. As they spend time together, they develop feelings for each other, but their relationship remains chaste and unspoken, reflecting societal constraints and their own moral compass.

title: NAZA
description: NAZA (15) is the new release from Yuval Abraham & Rachel Szor, directors of the acclaimed No Other Land. Filmed at night from Tel Aviv rooftops, this investigative documentary examines the civilian casualties of Israel's military operations in Gaza and the systems behind targeted killings of Palestinians. A Guardian produced documentary, NAZA (15) premiered at Venice Film Festival, taking home the Special Jury Prize after receiving the longest ovation in the event’s history. Its title comes from an acronym used euphemistically by Israeli intelligence to denote expected civilian casualties in an airstrike.

title: Ghosts: The Possession of Button House
description: Three friends attempt to communicate with the spirits occupying a haunted house, and become embroiled in a supernatural adventure.

title: Habit
description: “My main contribution to the horror genre was to tell a very personal story about addiction and obsession in New York City with an affectionate nod to vampire tropes and mood. Shot on 16mm by Frank DeMarco with a un-self-conscious spare style, we filmed on and off for 45 days with a crew of 5 for 60K. Also steeped in ambiguity, it seems to resonate with anyone who has ever suffered a breakup or felt overwhelmed by existential loneliness, which is to say, most everyone and most every cinephile.” – Larry Fessenden, director

title: Possible Love
description: The lives of two married couples from different social strata collide in Lee Chang-dong’s brilliantly unfolding narrative about economic precarity, in which a laid-off factory worker and his wife become the camera subjects for a documentary filmmaker. Winner of the Silver Lion at the 2026 Venice Film Festival and South Korea’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: Naza
description: Directed by Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, two of the co-directors of the 2024 Oscar-winning documentary No Other Land , Naza reveals the systems behind Israel’s bombing of Gaza and its mass killing of Palestinian civilians. Winner of Special Jury Prize at the 2026 Venice Film Festival.

title: The Social Reckoning (15) (AD)
description: In this companion piece to The Social Network , screenwriter Aaron Sorkin returns to the Metaverse with a tale of the whistleblower who started the social media reckoning we're seeing play out today.

title: Shaun the Sheep: The Beast of Mossy Bottom
description: The new adventure sees the residents of Mossy Bottom Farm looking forward to Halloween - until the clumsy Farmer trashes the Flock's beloved pumpkin patch. When Shaun turns mad scientist to fix the problem, things rapidly spiral out of control, leading to a wild beast roaming the woods.

title: Invasion of the Body Snatchers/Monolith Monsters
Wildwood
description: After her baby brother is abducted by a murder of crows, headstrong teenager Prue McKeel launches a desperate rescue mission into the Impassable Wilderness - an enchanted forest hidden just beyond Portland, Oregon. Joined by her hapless but loyal classmate Curtis Mehlberg, Prue navigates a world of talking animals, bandits, and powerful figures driven by grief and ambition. As the pair is drawn into a conflict threatening the balance of the forest itself, Prue must discover strength and belief she never knew she possessed. If she hopes to save her brother and protect Wildwood’s fragile future, she will have to risk everything. From Oscar-nominated and BAFTA-winning LAIKA, Wildwood is a sweeping adventure about love, sacrifice, and the magic that reveals itself when we dare to look beyond the familiar.

title: Fatherland
description: The new offering from Oscar-winner Pawel Pawlikowski Fatherland centres on the relationship between the Nobel Prize-winning writer Thomas Mann and his daughter Erika, actress, writer and rally driver. In the summer of 1949, at the height of the Cold War, father and daughter embark on a challenging and emotional road trip in a black Buick taking them across a Germany in ruins – from US dominated Frankfurt to Soviet controlled Weimar. Returning home after sixteen years of exile in the US, Thomas Mann has to face not only a divided fatherland, but also deep fracture within his own family.

title: Wildwood
description: The Portland-set story follows Prue McKeel, who enters an enchanted wonderland when her baby brother Mac is taken by a murder of crows into the forest’s depths.

title: Ken Russell's The Devils 35mm
description: An enduring masterpiece of cinema starring Oliver Reed and Vanessa Redgrave, THE DEVILS is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption - and a defining work of art from seminal filmmaker Ken Russell. Fully restored and presented uncut and unfiltered as Russell always envisioned, the film screens from a stunning, brand new 35mm print.

title: Possible Love
description: Possible Love follows the intertwined relationship of two married couples facing different paths and hidden desires. Mi-ok (Jeon Do-yeon) lives quietly with her laid-off husband Ho-seok (Sul Kyung-gu) and their young son Cheol until a funeral brings them into the orbit of Ye-ji (Cho Yeo-jeong), a documentary filmmaker chronicling laid-off workers, and her husband Sang-woo (Zo In-sung) – a couple whose affluent lifestyle stands in sharp contrast to their own. When Mi-ok agrees to be filmed, she grows close to Ye-ji, and finds herself uneasily drawn to the unreadable Sang-woo. As their worlds collide, fractures begin to appear in their daily existence. Marking his first release in eight years, highly acclaimed director Lee Chang-dong ( Burning , Poetry , Secret Sunshine ) brings his signature nuance to Possible Love , capturing shifting emotions, conflicts, and contrasting outlooks that shape these relationships.

title: The Shining [UK Version]
description: Jack Torrance (Jack Nicholson) becomes winter caretaker at the isolated Overlook Hotel in Colorado, hoping to cure his writer's block. He settles in along with his wife, Wendy (Shelley Duvall), and his son, Danny (Danny Lloyd), who is plagued by psychic premonitions. As Jack's writing goes nowhere and Danny's visions become more disturbing, Jack discovers the hotel's dark secrets and begins to unravel into a homicidal maniac hell-bent on terrorizing his family.

title: HACKNEY CHILDREN'S FILM FEST: THE LURE OF PONIES:  A SPELLBOUND ATTIC MYSTERY
description: Hackney Children’s Film Festival | Sat 24 - Sat 31 October Tickets £5 or £3 with a Hackney Library Card A Rio Cinema Project  The kids have waited long enough! This October half term, the Rio brings Hackney its first ever Children's Film Festival, with a lively and enchanting film programme curated ...

title: LOST BOUNDARIES
description: “Louis de Rochemont’s independent production LOST BOUNDARIES, based on a true story, recounted the experiences of a light-skinned Black doctor and his wife (played, respectively, by white performers Mel Ferrer and Beatrice Pearson), who move to a small white community in New England. There, in search of opportunities, he sets up a successful medical practice as the two pass for white, and even raise their two children as such. When their deep, dark secret is revealed, their otherwise placid community is thrown into turmoil and must examine itself. Though most of the cast in this Picture Problem was white, a standout was the refreshing young African American actor William Greaves in a supporting role.” – Donald Bogle, Hollywood Black: The Stars, the Films, the Filmmakers 35mm print courtesy UCLA Film & Television Archive

title: Sense and Sensibility (U) (AD)
description: An irresistible new take on Jane Austen ’s iconic Sense and Sensibility : a charming, witty and deeply relatable story of love and sisterhood, starring Daisy Edgar-Jones and Esmé Creed-Miles .

title: Ghosts: The Possession of Button House
description: Three friends attempt to communicate with the spirits occupying a haunted house, and become embroiled in a supernatural adventure.

title: Nirvanna the Band the Show the Movie
description: When their plan to book a show at the Rivoli goes horribly wrong, Matt and Jay accidentally travel back to the year 2008.

title: SHAUN THE SHEEP: THE BEAST OF MOSSY BOTTOM
description: SHAUN THE SHEEP: THE BEAST OF MOSSY BOTTOM sees the residents of Mossy Bottom Farm looking forward to Halloween -- until the clumsy Farmer trashes the Flock's beloved pumpkin patch! When Shaun turns MAD SCIENTIST to fix the problem, things rapidly spiral out of control... With The Farmer missing and...

title: Street Fighter
description: Set in 1993, estranged Street Fighters Ryu (Andrew Koji) and Ken Masters (Noah Centineo) are thrown back into combat when the mysterious Chun-Li (Callina Liang) recruits them for the next World Warrior Tournament: a brutal clash of fists, fate, and fury. But behind this battle royale lies a deadly conspiracy that forces them to face off against each other and the demons of their past. And if they don’t, it’s GAME OVER!

description: A scuba diver in search of his deceased father's remains gets swallowed by an 80-foot, 60-ton sperm whale and has only one hour to escape before his oxygen runs out. After giving up on life, the young man is surprised to find a reason to live in the most dangerous and unlikely of places.

title: Clayface
description: A shape-shifting creature made of magical clay haunts Gotham City, alternating between villain and ally of Batman. Multiple tragic figures have taken on the Clayface mantle over the years.

title: The Natural History of Destruction
description: The Natural History of Destruction. 2022. Germany/Netherlands/France. Written and directed by Sergei Loznitsa. DCP courtesy Atoms & Void. In German, English; English subtitles. 109 min. At a time when the traditional rules of wartime engagement are increasingly violated, civilian populations are used as human shields, and cities are targeted and laid to waste without consequence or legal redress, W. G. Sebald’s book On the Natural History of Destruction has assumed an even deeper moral gravity than when he wrote it in 1999. Sergei Loznitsa’s brilliantly edited archival documentary uses German, British, and American wartime footage in ironic counterpoint to evoke not only the appalling devastation of the Allied air raids that decimated some 131 German cities and towns in the last years of the war, including Cologne, Dresden, and Hamburg (the latter in “Operation Gomorrah”), but also the sense of willed national amnesia—the widespread appeal of kitschy Heimat nostalgia to banish feelings of shame, complicity, and defeat—that Sebald diagnoses and exposes in postwar German society.

title: Hellraiser
description: “We have such sights to show you…” In horror polymath Clive Barker’s adaptation of his novella The Hellbound Heart , horny hedonist Uncle Frank plays with a mysterious puzzle box, summons the Cenobites (led by Doug Bradley in an iconic performance) and endangers his unsuspecting niece (Ashley Laurence). A work of remarkable specificity and imagination, this inimitable, hot and bothered horror landmark is presented in a new 4K restoration. “The best horror film ever to be made in Britain.” – Melody Maker Opens Wed Oct 21, showtimes to be announced.

title: UNZIPPED
description: “Isaac Mizrahi as he conceived and contorted the way through to his fall 1994 show, [dashing] around a deserted SoHo with pal Sandra Bernhard; [meeting] with Naomi Campbell, Linda Evangelista, and baby Kate Moss for fittings; and [racing] uptown to an audience with Eartha Kitt... Hair-raising deadlines, delirious Bette Davis impressions, and the hostile but exhilarating act of executing a designer’s vision come together in a work that set the bar for all fashion films after.” – Vogue

title: Possible Love
description: The lives of two married couples from different social strata collide in Lee Chang-dong’s brilliantly unfolding narrative about economic precarity, in which a laid-off factory worker and his wife become the camera subjects for a documentary filmmaker. Winner of the Silver Lion at the 2026 Venice Film Festival and South Korea’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: Off-Circuit: The Night is Fading Away
description: Pelu is a thirty-something barely scraping by on his salary as a projectionist at a film theatre that belongs to Cordoba's city hall. After losing his job due to budget cuts, he agrees to stay on as the night watchman, and through a series of increasingly unfortunate twists, he ends up secretly living inside the cinema, surrounded by the films he watches every night. Growing more comfortable in his new home, Pelu begins to form a small community that inhabits the cinema after hours: a group of three naranjitas (informal homeless parking attendants) he lets sleep there, who eventually become his closest friends, and Vale, a former friend he allows to record videos for her OnlyFans channel inside the screening room. But the precarious economic conditions they live under are part of a broader crisis that threatens to shut down the cinema and jeopardise their fragile community. Ramiro Sonzini and Ezequiel Salinas's The Night is Fading Away is a luminous tale of friendship, community, and the power of cinema. The screening on the Friday 23 October will be followed by an in-person Q&A with Ramiro Sonzini and Ezequel Salinas.

title: NAZA (15)
description: Cloaked in darkness on the rooftops of Tel Aviv, Israeli journalist Yuval Abraham conducts shattering one-on-one interviews with Israeli soldiers and intelligence personnel.

title: FATHERLAND
description: From the director of IDA and COLD WAR: FATHERLAND follows Nobel Prize-winning author Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler, KINGS OF THE ROAD) and his actress daughter Erika (Sandra Hüller, ANATOMY OF A FALL) as they drive across a war-ravaged 1949 Germany. Returning home after years of exile in the U.S. and exuding a superhuman gravitas, Mann finds the Germany he knew to be gone, replaced by a country with contradictory ideologies. Erika, who acts as his travel coordinator and translator, strives to pierce his detached persona while quietly struggling with a family tragedy.

title: Fatherland
description: Oscar-nominated director Paweł Pawlikowski (Cold War, NYFF56) won Best Director at Cannes for his most potent film yet, following novelist Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler) and his daughter Erika Mann (Sandra Hüller) on a road trip across Germany in the aftermath of World War II. title: Miss Representation: Rise Up
description: Thu, Oct 22: Q&A w/ Reshma Saujani (Founder, Moms First and Girls Who Code) and Alyse Nelson (CEO, Vital Voices) after 6:30 show! Over a decade after MISS REPRESENTATION exposed the media’s contribution to the underrepresentation of women in leadership, this follow-up dives deep into the cultural backlash against women’s agency and power. With the proliferation of AI and deepfakes, a new era of tech-facilitated violence is exacerbating sexism and misogyny in an attempt to control and silence women and girls. With inspiring young women at its core, MISS REPRESENTATION: RISE UP interweaves their personal journeys with powerful voices in media, culture, leadership, and academia to reimagine a future that finally uplifts women and girls.

title: ONCE UPON A TIME IN HARLEM
description: August 1972: A reunion of Harlem Renaissance luminaries is held at Duke Ellington’s St. Nicholas Ave. townhouse. Though many of these figures haven’t seen each other in 50 years, sharp memories, vigorous debates, and unsettled scores soon flow through this stunner of a cocktail party, which features (among others): artists Romare Bearden, Aaron Douglas, and Richard Bruce Nugent; composer Eubie Blake; poet Arna Bontemps; photographer James Van Der Zee; and activists Richard B. Moore and Louise Patterson. After organizing and shooting this extraordinary gathering, filmmaker William Greaves (SYMBIOPSYCHOTAXIPLASM: TAKE ONE) was unable to complete the film before his death in 2014. One of the cameramen that day was his son David, who expertly reshaped this never-before-seen, newly-restored footage into “a film for the ages…one of the greatest cinematic works of creative nonfiction that I’ve ever seen.” – Richard Brody, The New Yorker

title: Possession
description: After Anna (Isabelle Adjani) reveals to her husband, Mark (Sam Neill), that she is having an affair, she leaves him and their son. Mark is devastated, and seeks out Heinrich (Heinz Bennent), the man who cuckolded him, only to receive a beating. After a series of violent confrontations between Mark and Anna, Mark hires a private investigator to follow her. Anna descends into madness, and it's soon clear that she is hiding a much bigger secret -- one that is both inexplicable and shocking.

title: Ghosts: The Possession of Button House
description: Three friends attempt to communicate with the spirits occupying a haunted house, and become embroiled in a supernatural adventure.

title: The Social Reckoning
description: A companion piece to the hit film The Social Network, Sorkin’s original screenplay is based on the events that gave rise to the Wall Street Journal’s shocking exposé The Facebook Files. The film is inspired by the true story of how Frances Haugen (Madison), a young Facebook engineer, enlists the help of Jeff Horwitz (White), a Wall Street Journal reporter, to go on a dangerous journey that ends up blowing the whistle on the social network’s most guarded secrets.

title: The Social Reckoning (15) (AD)
description: In this companion piece to The Social Network , screenwriter Aaron Sorkin returns to the Metaverse with a tale of the whistleblower who started the social media reckoning we're seeing play out today.

title: Street Fighter
description: Set in 1993, estranged Street Fighters Ryu (Andrew Koji) and Ken Masters (Noah Centineo) are thrown back into combat when the mysterious Chun-Li (Callina Liang) recruits them for the next World Warrior Tournament: a brutal clash of fists, fate, and fury. But behind this battle royale lies a deadly conspiracy that forces them to face off against each other and the demons of their past. And if they don’t, it’s GAME OVER!

title: Brother
description: Legendary comedian and TV host turned director Takeshi Kitano writes, directs, and stars in his first and only American co-production. Disgraced yakuza Yamamoto (Kitano) seeks refuge in Los Angeles, reconnecting with his younger half-brother Ken (Claude Maki) after his clan suffered defeat at the hands of a rival gang back in Tokyo. Cool and detached, Brother marries Japanese and American disillusionment in Kitano’s signature violent minimalist style through the growing bonds between Yamamoto and the multinational gang that he cultivates in L.A. Brother is featured as part of Gangsters Have Feelings Too, a season exploring the sensitive gangster film. The season is presented with the National Film and Television School’s Film Studies, Programming and Curation MA.

title: Wildwood
description: After her baby brother is abducted by a murder of crows, headstrong teenager Prue McKeel launches a desperate rescue mission into the Impassable Wilderness - an enchanted forest hidden just beyond Portland, Oregon. Joined by her hapless but loyal classmate Curtis Mehlberg, Prue navigates a world of talking animals, bandits, and powerful figures driven by grief and ambition. As the pair is drawn into a conflict threatening the balance of the forest itself, Prue must discover strength and belief she never knew she possessed. If she hopes to save her brother and protect Wildwood’s fragile future, she will have to risk everything. From Oscar-nominated and BAFTA-winning LAIKA, Wildwood is a sweeping adventure about love, sacrifice, and the magic that reveals itself when we dare to look beyond the familiar.

title: Animation in Love: Night is Short, Walk on Girl (15)
description: One wild night on the streets of Kyoto as a student plans the perfect meet-cute from the irrepressible anime auteur, Masaaki Yuasa .

title: Film Africa: TUTU
description: More than an archbishop, Desmond Tutu was a moral force whose courage, compassion and unwavering belief in justice helped transform South Africa and inspired the world. Drawing on previously unseen archive footage and intimate first-hand accounts, Sam Pollard’s powerful documentary reveals the man b...

title: CITIZEN TOXIE: THE TOXIC AVENGER IV (Lloyd Kaufman in person on Wed, Oct 28!)
description: “When the notorious Diaper Mafia take the students of the Tromaville School For The Very Special hostage, only the Toxic Avenger, and his sidekick Lardass, can save them. However, a horrific explosion creates a portal between Tromaville and its dimensional counterpart, Amortville. While Toxie is trapped in Amortville, Tromaville comes under the control of his evil doppelgänger, the Noxious Avenger. Will Toxie return to Tromaville in time to stop Noxie’s rampage or is he doomed to remain a second-class citizen in Amortville forever? With a veritable cast of dozens, including Lemmy, Al Goldstein, Stan Lee, James Gunn, Hank the Angry Dwarf, Julie Strain, Eli Roth, Hugh Hefner, and Corey Feldman, CITIZEN TOXIE is Lloyd Kaufman’s ‘Tromasterpiece’” –AGFA Lloyd Kaufman will be here in person on Wed, Oct 28!
