title: Naza
description: In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them. We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA ’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence. — Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

title: Depraved
description: “It took 9 years shopping my modern Frankenstein to Hollywood after the collapse of my remake of THE ORPHANAGE for Guillermo del Toro. I eventually started building the set in a Brooklyn loft before I had full financing and I cast an unknown as the monster (as Boris Karloff had been in 1931). The result was a low budget re-telling of Mary Shelley’s masterpiece steeped in the national PTSD of the Iraq war and Pharmaceutical over-reach, with Alex Breaux as Adam, the doomed creature.” – Larry Fessenden, director See more and save! Get an O ptic Nerve 3-Ticket Pack ($30 for IFC Center members and $45 for non-members) . Ticket packs are good for any three screenings in the series.

title: Reality Bites
description: Arguably the most consciously “Gen X” movie ever made, Stiller’s shambolically charming directorial debut stars Ryder as Lelaina Pierce, a university valedictorian whose postgraduate malaise threatens to become a full-fledged identity crisis when she’s faced with the choice between two very different eligible suitors: corporate climber Michael (Stiller) and slack motherfucker Troy (Ethan Hawke), the latter a staple of the Houston, Texas open mic circuit. Featuring a pip of a soundtrack (Juliana Hatfield Three! Lisa Loeb and Nine Stories!), career-best supporting work from Janeane Garofalo, and cameo appearances by Lemonheads frontman Evan Dando and Ryder’s then-beau, Soul Asylum’s Dave Pirner. Be there or be a cob nobbler.

title: Godzilla (1954)
description: Godzilla is the roaring granddaddy of all monster movies. It’s also a remarkably humane and melancholy drama, made in Japan at a time when the country was reeling from nuclear attack and H-bomb testing in the Pacific. Its rampaging radioactive beast, the poignant embodiment of an entire population’s fears, became a beloved international icon of destruction, spawning almost thirty sequels.

title: Antichrist
description: While a married couple (Willem Dafoe, Charlotte Gainsbourg) is having sex, their infant son in a nearby room falls out a window to his death. She becomes distraught and is hospitalized, but her husband, who is a psychiatrist, attempts to treat her. Deciding that she needs to face her fears, he takes her to a cabin in the woods where she spent a previous summer with the boy. Once they are there, she becomes more unhinged and starts perpetrating sexual violence on her husband and herself.

title: Possible Love
description: Possible Love follows the intertwined relationship of two married couples facing different paths and hidden desires. Mi-ok (Jeon Do-yeon) lives quietly with her laid-off husband Ho-seok (Sul Kyung-gu) and their young son Cheol until a funeral brings them into the orbit of Ye-ji (Cho Yeo-jeong), a documentary filmmaker chronicling laid-off workers, and her husband Sang-woo (Zo In-sung) – a couple whose affluent lifestyle stands in sharp contrast to their own. When Mi-ok agrees to be filmed, she grows close to Ye-ji, and finds herself uneasily drawn to the unreadable Sang-woo. As their worlds collide, fractures begin to appear in their daily existence. Marking his first release in eight years, highly acclaimed director Lee Chang-dong ( Burning , Poetry , Secret Sunshine ) brings his signature nuance to Possible Love , capturing shifting emotions, conflicts, and contrasting outlooks that shape these relationships.

description: The new offering from Oscar-winner Pawel Pawlikowski Fatherland centres on the relationship between the Nobel Prize-winning writer Thomas Mann and his daughter Erika, actress, writer and rally driver. In the summer of 1949, at the height of the Cold War, father and daughter embark on a challenging and emotional road trip in a black Buick taking them across a Germany in ruins – from US dominated Frankfurt to Soviet controlled Weimar. Returning home after sixteen years of exile in the US, Thomas Mann has to face not only a divided fatherland, but also deep fracture within his own family.

title: Heat
description: A group of high-end professional thieves start to feel the heat from the LAPD when they unknowingly leave a verbal clue at their latest heist. Original Cut from a 35mm print.

title: Yi Yi
description: The last work of a master filmmaker who died far too young, the gentle, restrained, and terribly humane Yi Yi observes the interplay between three generations of an upper middle-class Taipei family. Comic when dealing in the foibles of its excellent ensemble cast and the mores of the urban bourgeoise, yet also possessed throughout by an air of unmistakable melancholy and lingering regret at missed opportunities, this feeling made all the deeper when one considers the great films Yang might still have produced. A work of epic length that avoids even a hint of bombast, dedicated instead to working its way into the hidden, niche spaces of everyday people’s emotional lives, it’s a film as rich and as sad as life itself. Part of Jiā: Histories of Home

title: Girl, Interrupted
description: Based on a 1993 memoir of the same name by Susanna Kaysen, Mangold’s powerhouse picture sets its scene at a New England psychiatric hospital c. 1967 where Winona Ryder (in the Kaysen role; also a producer on the film) lands after suffering a nervous breakdown. Among the committed at Claymoore are a hall-of-fame lineup of ’90s female acting talent, including self-harmer Brittany Murphy, schizophrenic burn victim Elisabeth Moss and, in a star-making turn, Angelina Jolie as sociopath agitator Lisa Rowe. Ryder’s is not the flashiest role here, but she holds the film together with her quiet, alert intensity, offering a springboard for her co-stars to dive off into the deep end. Part of Winona Ryder Analogue Youth

title: The Devils
description: Ken Russell’s infamous adaptation of Aldous Huxley’s book, about the apparent possession of a group of nuns after one (Vanessa Redgrave) accuses a priest (Oliver Reed) of collaborating with the devil, is at long last available in its full, uncensored splendor.

title: Off-Circuit: The Night is Fading Away
description: Pelu is a thirty-something barely scraping by on his salary as a projectionist at a film theatre that belongs to Cordoba's city hall. After losing his job due to budget cuts, he agrees to stay on as the night watchman, and through a series of increasingly unfortunate twists, he ends up secretly living inside the cinema, surrounded by the films he watches every night. Growing more comfortable in his new home, Pelu begins to form a small community that inhabits the cinema after hours: a group of three naranjitas (informal homeless parking attendants) he lets sleep there, who eventually become his closest friends, and Vale, a former friend he allows to record videos for her OnlyFans channel inside the screening room. But the precarious economic conditions they live under are part of a broader crisis that threatens to shut down the cinema and jeopardise their fragile community. Ramiro Sonzini and Ezequiel Salinas's The Night is Fading Away is a luminous tale of friendship, community, and the power of cinema. The screening on the Friday 23 October will be followed by an in-person Q&A with Ramiro Sonzini and Ezequel Salinas.

title: Poem of the Sea
description: Based on a script left behind by Dovzhenko at his death, Poem of the Sea was finally filmed by his widow, Solntseva, a formidable filmmaker in her own right, her stated intention to work wholly “in accordance with Dovzhenko’s artistic conception, putting aside every trace of my own individual vision.” A companion piece of sorts to Ivan, likewise dealing with the construction of a dam and its impact on the surrounding countryside—in particular one soon-to-be-submerged village, birthplace of one General Fedorchenko (Boris Livanov), whose arrival for a visit in its final days stirs long-dormant memories. The feat of civil engineering documented here is the Kakhovka Hydroelectric Power Plant, opened in 1956 and destroyed by Russian forces in 2023, with catastrophic ecological results. 35mm SovScope print courtesy of Austrian Filmmuseum, Vienna Part of Oleksandr Dovzhenko: Earth and Empire

title: Black Narcissus
description: This explosive work about the conflict between the spirit and the flesh is the epitome of the sensuous style of Michael Powell and Emeric Pressburger. A group of nuns—played by some of Britain's finest actresses, including Deborah Kerr, Kathleen Byron, and Flora Robson—struggle to establish a convent in the Himalayas, while isolation, extreme weather, altitude, and culture clashes all conspire to drive the well-intentioned missionaries mad. A darkly grand film that won Oscars for Alfred Junge's art direction and Jack Cardiff's cinematography, Black Narcissus is one of the greatest achievements by two of cinema's true visionaries.

title: MARDI GRAS MASSACRE
description:
While New Orleans parties, a ritual killer turns its nightlife into his hunting ground. Detectives follow a trail of sacrifices through bars, bedrooms and the clammy underside of the carnival.
Jack Weis’s notorious regional splatter film mixes a police procedural with disco-era sleaze and the primitive shock tactics of BLOOD FEAST. Its rough surfaces are part of the experience: a drive-in nightmare with no studio polish to soften the impact. A deeply disreputable entry in the history of the British video-nasty panic.

description:
In James Gray’s deeply felt and intense drama, two brothers become entangled in a scheme that turns out to be too good to be true. As they try to navigate their way through the dangerous world of the Russian mafia, family bonds begin to fray with life-altering consequences.

Starring Adam Driver, Miles Teller and Scarlett Johansson.

11/3 - Early Access Preview Screening featuring a Q&A with Writer and Director James Gray (Schedule permitting)

description: In West Hollywood, a gay adult performer’s brutal murder went cold for decades. When filmmakers began documenting his story, the community’s involvement led to shocking discoveries through vintage footage linking suspects to the crime.

title: Excalibur
description: John Boorman’s medieval masterpiece Excalibur captures the legend of King Arthur and the knights of the Round Table in epic emerald hues and rolling landscapes blanketed in mysterious fog. When a young Arthur (Nigel Terry) pulls the mystical sword from the stone, he becomes king, and with the help of the wizard Merlin (Nicol Williamson), marries the beautiful and somewhat mercurial Guenevere (Cherie Lunghi), fulfilling his heart’s desire. Despite the prosperity his kingdom enjoys, the unrequited love between Guenevere and his best knight Lancelot (Nicholas Clay), creates a jealous fracture within Camelot that spreads to a crippling, melancholy pall over the land. Only the holy grail can restore peace and prosperity to the kingdom that once held so much promise. The ensemble performances create a Shakespearean feel to Boorman’s vision, and Helen Mirren is an enchantress as the power-hungry Morgana. Alex Thomson’s stunning visuals received an Academy Award nomination for Best Cinematography. “Behold! Excalibur! Forged when the world was young, and death was but a dream!”

title: Being John Malkovich
description: On the seventh and a half floor of a nondescript office lies a door which invites curious travelers to do the impossible: see the world through the eyes of actor John Malkovich — for 15 minutes — before spitting them out on the New Jersey turnpike. But when a struggling puppeteer (John Cusack), his pet enthusiast wife (Cameron Diaz), and his office crush (Catherine Keener) begin to impose, their control over the life of the real Malkovich begins to turn the thespian into a bona fide head case. Starring the man himself, John Malkovich. Malkovich. Malkovich.

title: The Enchanted Desna
description: The third film made by Solntseva from a script by her late husband and creative collaborator, The Enchanted Desna—an intimate epic in the magic-realist vein filmed on 70mm Sovscope and boasting state-of-the-art stereophonic sound—draws on Dovzhenko’s memories of his childhood on the banks of the Desna River in Chernihiv Oblast, moving freely between pre-revolutionary bucolic idyll, the horrors of World War II, and contemporary-set scenes. Winner of a Special Jury Prize at the San Sebastián Film Festival, Jean-Luc Godard’s favorite film of 1965 and, per critic Jonathan Rosenbaum, “among the most ravishingly beautiful and poetic spectacles ever made.” DCP courtesy of Berkeley Art Museum and Pacific Film Archive, scanned from a 35mm print in their collection. Part of Oleksandr Dovzhenko: Earth and Empire

title: The Devils
description: Censored for more than half a century, Ken Russell’s visionary masterpiece returns to the big screen fully restored in 4K and cut to Russell’s direction – the first publicly released version of the film as intended by the filmmaker. Unveiled at the 79th Cannes Film Festival, the definitive version arrives 55 years after the film’s original release. An enduring masterpiece of cinema starring Oliver Reed and Vanessa Redgrave, Ken Russell’s The Devils is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption. Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, accused of bewitching a convent of nuns, the film lays bare the collusion of church and state through a searing vision of religious persecution, collective hysteria and institutional corruption. In addition to powerhouse performances from Reed and Redgrave, Ken Russell’s The Devils showcases the stunning work of artists at the peak of their craft: Academy Award-winning cinematographer David Watkin ( Out of Africa , Chariots of Fire ); editor Michael Bradsell ( Local Hero , Jabberwocky ); and visual artist Derek Jarman ( Jubilee , Caravaggio ), whose work as production designer marked his feature film debut.

title: Ken Russell's The Devils: The Director's Cut
description: Censored for over half a century, Ken Russell’s film returns in a landmark director’s cut reconstruction that reveals the full power of his original vision. Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, accused of bewitching a convent of nuns, The Devils lays bare the collusion of church and state through a searing vision of religious persecution, collective hysteria and institutional corruption. The restoration many believed would never happen reaffirms Russell’s incendiary masterpiece as among the most overwhelming and uncompromising achievements in British cinema. Assembled from original camera negative, this 4k restoration is Ken Russell’s 2004 preferred edit. Picture and sound restoration by Warner Bros. Frederick R. Friedel’s regional independent filmmaking gives the danger an unusually intimate texture: dusty locations, awkward silences and people who never quite fit the roles the plot has assigned them. Also known as KIDNAPPED COED, this is a rough-edged drive-in discovery whose unsettling unpredictability is its strongest weapon.

Almost Famous
description: Before breaking into movies with his screenplay for Fast Times at Ridgemont High, Cameron Crowe was a teenage journalist with a regular byline in Rolling Stone magazine in the hedonistic early 1970s, and he draws from a deep well of memories of those pot-hazy days in his poignant-funny, semi-autobiographical Almost Famous, starring Patrick Fugit as a fresh-faced rock rag writer on the road with hesher idols Stillwater, Kate Hudson as road-warrior Stillwater superfan “Penny Lane,” and Philip Seymour Hoffman as an impassioned, opinionated, marvelously disheveled Lester Bangs. “In Almost Famous, a loose, affectionate look back on his earlier career as a teenage music journalist, Mr. Crowe has devoted a whole movie to the love of rock 'n' roll. The soul he lays open—a sweet, forgiving and generous one—is his own … He may be the least cynical director working in Hollywood today.” —A.O. Scott, The New York Times Introduction by Jon Caramanica and Joe Coscarelli of “Popcast” on Friday, October 16th Part of The New York Times presents Stop the Presses

title: A Bittersweet Life
description: A mob enforcer (Lee Byung-hun, No Other Choice) with a sterling record of loyal service finds himself fighting for his life after sparing the life of his boss’s straying mistress (Shin Min-a) in Kim’s drum-tight neo-noir thriller, unusually grounded by both emotional stakes and a sense of real physical danger in the action set pieces, choreographed for the widescreen with much panache. Jang’s second collaboration with Kim, after The Foul King, earned him and collaborator (and Peach Present collective bandmate) Dalparan Best Music honors from the Busan Film Critics Association, responding to the composers’ sophisticated melange of samba, flamenco, solo cello, and electronic elements. description: 23-year-old Amélie is lonely. After an isolating childhood, she moves to Paris and becomes a waitress at the Café des Deux Moulins, a bar restaurant filled with a colourful cast of diners and employees. One night, Amélie happens across a box of treasures hidden in her apartment, left by a little boy in the Fifties, that changes the course of her life. Henceforth, she dedicates herself to giving back to her community, tracking down the owner of these keepsakes, consoling a widowed neighbour and befriending a reclusive artist. When completing these good deeds, she crosses paths with Nino, a photobooth collagist who shares her oddball sensibilities. She quickly falls in love with him.

Possible Love
description: Possible Love follows the intertwined relationship of two married couples facing different paths and hidden desires. Mi-ok (Jeon Do-yeon) lives quietly with her laid-off husband Ho-seok (Sul Kyung-gu) and their young son Cheol until a funeral brings them into the orbit of Ye-ji (Cho Yeo-jeong), a documentary filmmaker chronicling laid-off workers, and her husband Sang-woo (Zo In-sung) – a couple whose affluent lifestyle stands in sharp contrast to their own. When Mi-ok agrees to be filmed, she grows close to Ye-ji, and finds herself uneasily drawn to the unreadable Sang-woo. As their worlds collide, fractures begin to appear in their daily existence. Marking his first release in eight years, highly acclaimed director Lee Chang-dong ( Burning , Poetry , Secret Sunshine ) brings his signature nuance to Possible Love , capturing shifting emotions, conflicts, and contrasting outlooks that shape these relationships.

Winner of Special Jury Prize at the 2026 Venice Film Festival.

title: La La Land
description: Sebastian (Ryan Gosling) and Mia (Emma Stone) are drawn together by their common desire to do what they love. But as success mounts they are faced with decisions that begin to fray the fragile fabric of their love affair, and the dreams they worked so hard to maintain in each other threaten to rip them apart.

title: All We Imagine as Light
description: Winner of the Grand Prix at the 2024 Cannes Film Festival, Kapadia’s fiction feature debut concerns itself with the intimate, everyday concerns of Kani Kusruti and Divya Prabha as Prabha and Anu, roommates and co-workers at a Mumbai hospital, and their recently retired co-worker Parvaty, played by Chhaya Kadam, facing homelessness in the aftermath of an act of slum clearance. Formally and structurally audacious, in its rich color palette and its free movement between slice-of-life realism to transcendental mysticism, and throughout deeply humane. “On some of the older cars in Mumbai’s local railway, the doors don’t close. This is how we meet Prabha, her hands on a pole, the wind in her hair, the city’s lights gently blurred behind her. Aboard the ladies compartment, there’s a sense of ease that she doesn’t find elsewhere in her life, in this crowded city. Among these other women, who chat, listen to music, or doze, she seems to notice just how good the air feels.” —Series curator Genevieve Yue

title: Dogtooth [Kynodontas]
description: Newly restored in 4K, DOGTOOTH follows a controlling, manipulative father who locks his three adult children in a state of perpetual childhood by keeping them prisoner within the sprawling family compound.

title: Bus Stop
description: This contemporary Western—in which Marilyn Monroe stars as saloon singer Cherie, who dreams of one day making it big in Hollywood—marked a turning point in Marilyn Monroe’s career. She had recently formed Marilyn Monroe Productions and signed a new contract with 20th Century-Fox, earning a higher salary and more creative agency in the process. For the role of Cherie, which was one of the more dramatic and serious of her career to date, she began working with Method acting pioneers Lee and Paula Strasberg, who placed an emphasis on delving into an actor’s own experiences.
director: Joshua Logan PRODUCED BY: Buddy Adler

title: Midnight in Paris
description: Screenwriter, would-be novelist, and romantic-at-heart Owen Wilson, on vacation in the City of Lights with level-headed fiancée Rachel McAdams, sets out on his own one night after a wine tasting and finds himself suddenly in the Jazz Age Paris of Fitzgerald and Hemingway, Dali and Picasso—an invigorating draught of bohemian freedom that sets our protagonist to seriously interrogating his life choices. “We talked about pushing the color even more in the period scenes, in order to distinguish them from the present-day ones. The Paris of today would be normal and generic, bland and desaturated, and when you entered the Paris of the 1920s the colors would be more warm, lush and flamboyant, with lots of brown and gold and red.” —Darius Khondji Part of Radical Chiaroscuro: The Work of Darius Khondji

title: Off-Circuit: The Night is Fading Away
description: Pelu is a thirty-something barely scraping by on his salary as a projectionist at a film theatre that belongs to Cordoba's city hall. After losing his job due to budget cuts, he agrees to stay on as the night watchman, and through a series of increasingly unfortunate twists, he ends up secretly living inside the cinema, surrounded by the films he watches every night. Growing more comfortable in his new home, Pelu begins to form a small community that inhabits the cinema after hours: a group of three naranjitas (informal homeless parking attendants) he lets sleep there, who eventually become his closest friends, and Vale, a former friend he allows to record videos for her OnlyFans channel inside the screening room. But the precarious economic conditions they live under are part of a broader crisis that threatens to shut down the cinema and jeopardise their fragile community. Ramiro Sonzini and Ezequiel Salinas's The Night is Fading Away is a luminous tale of friendship, community, and the power of cinema. The screening on the Friday 23 October will be followed by an in-person Q&A with Ramiro Sonzini and Ezequel Salinas.

title: Fatherland
description: The new offering from Oscar-winner Pawel Pawlikowski Fatherland centres on the relationship between the Nobel Prize-winning writer Thomas Mann and his daughter Erika, actress, writer and rally driver. In the summer of 1949, at the height of the Cold War, father and daughter embark on a challenging and emotional road trip in a black Buick taking them across a Germany in ruins – from US dominated Frankfurt to Soviet controlled Weimar. Returning home after sixteen years of exile in the US, Thomas Mann has to face not only a divided fatherland, but also deep fracture within his own family.

title: In the Shadows
description: IN THE SHADOWS is based on the truly inspirational story of Ramla Ali, a Somali refugee who, without her family’s knowledge, became the first Somali British Boxing Champion. Presented by @civicstudios and Affine Films, IN THE SHADOWS is directed by double Emmy and triple BAFTA-winning director Anthony Wonke and written by Ursula Rani Sarma. BAFTA-winning Jasmine Jobson plays the lead role of Ramla Ali, with Finn Cole as her husband, Richard Moore, and Gershwyn Eustache Jnr as Clinton, Ramla’s coach. Other key Somali cast members include Hodan Yusuf, Suhayla Ahmed, Roda Asha Aden, Mustafa Aden, Moe Hashim and Samater Ahmed.

title: All That Heaven Allows
description: Perhaps the very finest of Sirk’s Ross Hunter-produced melodramas, All That Heaven Allows pairs Jane Wyman and Rock Hudson as, respectively, a well-off widow in country club Connecticut, and the broad-necked, Thoreau-reading gardener who she falls for. Her priggish children, aghast, conspire to break off the pairing, an endeavor that ends in a bone-chilling Christmas conciliation—the presentation of a gift television set as a kind of death sentence. Of this scene Rainer Werner Fassbinder, profoundly marked by his encounter with Sirk’s film, would write: “At that point everyone in the moviehouse breaks down. They suddenly understand something about the world and what it does to people.” Right on. Part of The Leaves Are Falling

title: SEX WORLD
description:
An exclusive resort promises to make its guests’ fantasies real. Arriving strangers bring desires they can name and anxieties they cannot; the encounters soon reveal a gap between getting what you want and understanding why you want it.
Anthony Spinelli borrows the polished surfaces and speculative premise of seventies science fiction for an unusually ambitious adult ensemble film. Interlocking stories, sleek production design and an electronic score give its experiments in intimacy a distinctive atmosphere. A key example of porno chic treating fantasy as both an attraction and a problem.
This film contains hardcore unsimulated sex scenes.

title: BORED TEENAGERS
description: [BRENNENDE LANGEWEILE] “In the late 1970s, Wolfgang Büld first made a name for himself with his documentary PUNK IN LONDON. The follow-up to this authentic document of youth culture was the ZDF production BORED TEENAGERS, part of the “Das kleine Fernsehspiel” series; it was filmed in 1979 in the wake of the RAF panic – wanted posters are visible in the background several times throughout the film. The movie blends concert footage of the English punk band The Adverts with a loose narrative thread about a young punk named Peter and his hairdresser girlfriend, Karin, as they follow the band – led by TV Smith and Gaye Advert – on their tour through Germany. It is an entertaining yet quirky journey through a late-70s musical subculture.” –OX-FANZINE

title: THE DRAWING CENTER PRESENTS: FORM, SHADOW, MOTION (FREE SCREENING!)
description: This program of artist films and videos is presented in conjunction with The Drawing Center’s current exhibition “Form, Shadow, Motion: Selections from the Burger Collection, Hong Kong”, opening on October 23, 2026 and on view until January 2027. The screening showcases a selection of artist pieces that extend the exhibition's visual essay on shared historical, poetic, and philosophical concerns, with Hong Kong and New York as twin points of reference and Eastern thought and Western philosophy as its guiding frameworks. “Form, Shadow, Motion: Selections from the Burger Collection, Hong Kong” is organized by Olivia Shao, Burger Collection & TOY Meets Art Curator. Cici Wu UNFINISHED RETURN OF YU MAN HON (2019, 19 min, 16mm-to-DCP) Tang Kwok Hin GRANDPA TANG (2017, 13 min, DCP) Chan Hau Chun THE MEMORY OF A CICADA IS LONGER THAN ITS LIFE (2024, 12 min, DCP. Music and sound: Chui Chi Yin.) Simon Liu PROCEDURES (2026, 17 min, 16mm-to-DCP) Total running time: ca. 65 min.

title: Excalibur
description: John Boorman’s medieval masterpiece Excalibur captures the legend of King Arthur and the knights of the Round Table in epic emerald hues and rolling landscapes blanketed in mysterious fog. When a young Arthur (Nigel Terry) pulls the mystical sword from the stone, he becomes king, and with the help of the wizard Merlin (Nicol Williamson), marries the beautiful and somewhat mercurial Guenevere (Cherie Lunghi), fulfilling his heart’s desire. Despite the prosperity his kingdom enjoys, the unrequited love between Guenevere and his best knight Lancelot (Nicholas Clay), creates a jealous fracture within Camelot that spreads to a crippling, melancholy pall over the land. Only the holy grail can restore peace and prosperity to the kingdom that once held so much promise. The ensemble performances create a Shakespearean feel to Boorman’s vision, and Helen Mirren is an enchantress as the power-hungry Morgana. Alex Thomson’s stunning visuals received an Academy Award nomination for Best Cinematography. “Behold! Excalibur! Forged when the world was young, and death was but a dream!”

description: In 2006, To Catch a Predator host Chris Hansen sets out to make television history. When a high stakes operation goes fatally wrong, his veneered dream of fame curdles into a nightmare of performative justice.

title: Strangers on a Train
description: “Criss cross.” Hitchcock’s adaptation of Highsmith’s 1951 page-turner kicks off with a casual encounter that reads like a same-sex pickup, as tennis star Guy Haines (Farley Granger) inadvertently agrees to “swap murders” with preening rich kid Bruno Anthony (Robert Walker, in a career performance), and continues through some of the finest set pieces of Hitch’s career: a tennis match at Forest Hills, Bruno stalking his prey through a vulgar county fair, and an out-of-control carousel. “In Hitchcock, the people you meet on trains can spell romance, adventure, or, in the case of Strangers on a Train’s Guy Haines, a colossal headache! Tip: beware anyone wearing spectator shoes.” —Series curator Genevieve Yue Part of Trains: Local Routes

title: My Dad is 100 Years Old with Rome, Open City
description: My Dad Is 100 Years Old This short tribute casts celebrated actress Isabella Rossellini as herself as well as various filmmakers who influenced or were influenced by her father, filmmaker Roberto Rossellini. Conceived by Isabella on the eve of her father’s centenary, she took a “docu-fantasia” concept to avant-garde filmmaker Guy Maddin after her delightful experience on his 2003 feature, The Saddest Music in the World. A beautiful cinema poem for a beloved father and artist.

title: The Devils
description: Censored for more than half a century, Ken Russell’s visionary masterpiece returns to the big screen fully restored in 4K and cut to Russell’s direction – the first publicly released version of the film as intended by the filmmaker. Unveiled at the 79th Cannes Film Festival, the definitive version arrives 55 years after the film’s original release. An enduring masterpiece of cinema starring Oliver Reed and Vanessa Redgrave, Ken Russell’s The Devils is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption. Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, accused of bewitching a convent of nuns, the film lays bare the collusion of church and state through a searing vision of religious persecution, collective hysteria and institutional corruption. In addition to powerhouse performances from Reed and Redgrave, Ken Russell’s The Devils showcases the stunning work of artists at the peak of their craft: Academy Award-winning cinematographer David Watkin ( Out of Africa , Chariots of Fire ); editor Michael Bradsell ( Local Hero , Jabberwocky ); and visual artist Derek Jarman ( Jubilee , Caravaggio ), whose work as production designer marked his feature film debut.

title: Electra, My Love
description: Jancsó’s radically original, downright hypnotic retelling of the Ancient Greek myth against the backdrop of the puszta, Hungary’s vast, muddy plains, is among the long-take master’s most bravura stylistic performances, its 70-minute runtime made up of only twelve intricately composed shots. Reworking the tale of Electra and her ill use at the hands of Aegisthus—the man who loved her mother and murdered her father 15 years ago—Jancsó produces a timeless meditation on tyranny and rebellion—and a resounding call to resistance. title: CAMP - A SHORT FILM SHOWCASE
description:
THE NICKEL teams up with cyberfemme studio EVERYONE IS A GIRL for a showcase of short films centred on the theme of CAMP, accompanied with readings.
The Nickel Cinema’s regular roster of B-movies, softcores, and underrated gems has begun to shed some buttery spotlight on underrepresented cinematic traditions. At EIAG, we make collaborative projects about the feminine, the seductive, the virtual, and the covert. For this CAMP showcase, we are joining forces to present films from our community that are not afraid to play, deceive, and perform. Join us for a night of London’s most sparkliest, performative, abject, delicious, and scandalicious emerging cinema.

title: Memories of Murder
description: Bong Joon Ho’s phenomenal breakthrough film stars Park Hae-il as an enigmatic young loner and observer whose innocent demeanor seems too wholesome to be true. Inspired by a true story, Memories of Murder centers around the gruesome serial killings of women in South Korea in the 1980s, investigated by Doo-man (Song Kang-ho), a detective who relies on instinct rather than fact. Bong’s vision, which challenges conventional components of storytelling and blurs the boundaries between genres, is meticulously orchestrated in this crime thriller, and Park’s elegantly simple depiction of a complicated character is phenomenal.

title: RIOTS AND LOVE
description: [RANDALE UND LIEBE – ROCKER, POPPER, TEDS UND PUNKS] “Thomas Schmitt’s film offers unique insights into the alternative subculture of 1980s Cologne. Depending on the concert, the Blue-Shell attracted rockers, punks, and Teddy Boys, while the Café d’Or was a popular hangout for the ‘Popper’ crowd. RANDALE UND LIEBE – ROCKER, POPPER, TEDS UND PUNKS is a magnificent document of its time.” –COLOGNE CINEMA NIGHTS

title: Oldboy
description: Homer with a ball-peen hammer. Kidnapped and stuffed in a hole without explanation for 15 years of solitary confinement, when Oh Dae-su (Choi Min-sik) is suddenly let loose on the streets, he’s stone-cold pissed off and very, very dangerous. Winner of the Grand Prix at Cannes and an international pop phenomenon, Oldboy was a revenge thriller unlike any that had come before, featuring passages of pure bravura filmmaking (that one-shot hallway donnybrook!) and surreal sicko humor that’ll put you off of sushi for a while. “Put together with brutally uncompromising style [and] the cold-steel edge of a knife against your throat. A dark and thrillingly horrible adventure into the realms of the unthinkable.” —The Guardian Part of Classical Cinema

title: Ghost in the Shell: 30th Anniversary Remaster
description: “My codename is Project 2501, and I am a life form that was born in a sea of information.” In the year 2029, the world looks like a hybridization of Hong Kong, Tokyo, and New York, yielding to entropy and technocracy. Cyborg Major Kusanagi, a perfect specimen of human-brained computer engineering is on the case to track and destroy an omnipotent entity known as The Puppet Master—a hacker? a virus?—who threatens world order. Her physical and existential journey deftly detailed by Oshii’s animation, combining traditional hand-drawn cells and computer-generated graphics, creating a haunting, awe-inspiring magnum opus. Part of A Cyberpunk Canon

Middle-aged Mr. Badii (Homayoun Ershadi) drives through the hilly outskirts of Tehran—searching for someone to rescue or bury him.

The burden of being the saviour of mankind torments Jesus throughout his life, leading him to doubt. As he is put to death on the cross, Jesus is tempted by visions of an ordinary life married to Mary Magdalene.

title: Fatherland
description: The new offering from Oscar-winner Pawel Pawlikowski Fatherland centres on the relationship between the Nobel Prize-winning writer Thomas Mann and his daughter Erika, actress, writer and rally driver. In the summer of 1949, at the height of the Cold War, father and daughter embark on a challenging and emotional road trip in a black Buick taking them across a Germany in ruins – from US dominated Frankfurt to Soviet controlled Weimar. Returning home after sixteen years of exile in the US, Thomas Mann has to face not only a divided fatherland, but also deep fracture within his own family.

title: Off-Circuit: The Night is Fading Away
description: Pelu is a thirty-something barely scraping by on his salary as a projectionist at a film theatre that belongs to Cordoba's city hall. After losing his job due to budget cuts, he agrees to stay on as the night watchman, and through a series of increasingly unfortunate twists, he ends up secretly living inside the cinema, surrounded by the films he watches every night. Growing more comfortable in his new home, Pelu begins to form a small community that inhabits the cinema after hours: a group of three naranjitas (informal homeless parking attendants) he lets sleep there, who eventually become his closest friends, and Vale, a former friend he allows to record videos for her OnlyFans channel inside the screening room. But the precarious economic conditions they live under are part of a broader crisis that threatens to shut down the cinema and jeopardise their fragile community. Ramiro Sonzini and Ezequiel Salinas's The Night is Fading Away is a luminous tale of friendship, community, and the power of cinema. The screening on the Friday 23 October will be followed by an in-person Q&A with Ramiro Sonzini and Ezequel Salinas.

title: Possible Love
description: Possible Love follows the intertwined relationship of two married couples facing different paths and hidden desires. Mi-ok (Jeon Do-yeon) lives quietly with her laid-off husband Ho-seok (Sul Kyung-gu) and their young son Cheol until a funeral brings them into the orbit of Ye-ji (Cho Yeo-jeong), a documentary filmmaker chronicling laid-off workers, and her husband Sang-woo (Zo In-sung) – a couple whose affluent lifestyle stands in sharp contrast to their own. When Mi-ok agrees to be filmed, she grows close to Ye-ji, and finds herself uneasily drawn to the unreadable Sang-woo. As their worlds collide, fractures begin to appear in their daily existence. Marking his first release in eight years, highly acclaimed director Lee Chang-dong ( Burning , Poetry , Secret Sunshine ) brings his signature nuance to Possible Love , capturing shifting emotions, conflicts, and contrasting outlooks that shape these relationships.

title: Ken Russell's The Devils: The Director's Cut
description: Censored for over half a century, Ken Russell’s film returns in a landmark director’s cut reconstruction that reveals the full power of his original vision. The restoration many believed would never happen reaffirms Russell’s incendiary masterpiece as among the most overwhelming and uncompromising achievements in British cinema. Assembled from original camera negative, this 4k restoration is Ken Russell’s 2004 preferred edit. Picture and sound restoration by Warner Bros. Washington’s politicians are exploding without warning. Bomb-disposal expert Danny O’Neill has to find the weapon before the next victim discovers they are carrying it inside them. His collapsing marriage is about to become part of the investigation.
Pierce Brosnan brings immaculate pre-Bond composure to a thriller with absolutely no intention of behaving sensibly. Liquid explosives, political conspiracy and domestic melodrama race towards the same detonation. Christian Duguay keeps the set pieces moving and the premise gloriously overheated: early-nineties action with an unusually volatile ingredient.

title: NO FUTURE + ALLET UNITED – PUNK IM POTT
description: Michael Braun NO FUTURE – KEIN BOCK AUF ILLUSIONEN 1981, 44 min, 16mm-to-DCP. In German with English subtitles. “In 1981, film and television producer Michael Braun made this film (which for a long time circulated only on atrociously poor-quality VHS copies) about the punk scene in Duisburg, featuring Willi Wucher, the band ARTLESS, and – here and there – Bernie Blitz (RIP). It is a journey back to the early 1980s, to the Ruhr region…back when the area was even bleaker than it is today. In the 80s, Braun hosted the ‘Michael Braun Talkshow’ on WDR television, featuring guests such as the bands DAF and Östro 430; the show was an early precursor to today's late-night talk shows.” –COMPUTERSTAAT Detlev Puls ALLET UNITED – PUNK IM POTT 1983, 25 min, 16mm-to-DCP. In German with English subtitles. This short film – made for German television during the summer of 1983 – focuses on the punk scene in the industrial Ruhr region, and features the bands Die Kanzlers and Starkbier, members of which later went on to form Body Checks. Total running time: ca. 75 min.

title: NAZA (15)
description: Cloaked in darkness on the rooftops of Tel Aviv, Israeli journalist Yuval Abraham conducts shattering one-on-one interviews with Israeli soldiers and intelligence personnel.

title: I Hate Myself and Want to Die
description: Join us in the microcinema for a refreshing dark comedy that will give you life – J. Davis’ acerbically hilarious I Hate Myself and Want to Die . Jacob is an unrealized artist, freshly dumped, who’s come home to the desert to quietly end his life. The problem is, nothing goes according to plan. His mom needs a ride to the drugstore, his cousin needs a shoulder to cry on, and his best friend just wants to get high. Over a crazy night of parties, fistfights and car chases, Jacob rethinks his life and— maybe—his death.

title: ASILAH OUI: MELEHI + A THOUSAND AND ONE BERBER NIGHTS
description: This screening – presented on the occasion of the Robert Blackburn Printmaking Workshop’s exhibition “Asilah Oui: Robert Blackburn in Morocco” – pairs two films that explore the links between Morocco and New York: Shalom Gorewitz’s MELEHI (1984) and Hisham Aïdi’s A THOUSAND AND ONE BERBER NIGHTS (2023), which together examine two pioneers of Moroccan art in the twentieth century. Commissioned as part of his 1984 solo exhibition at the Bronx Museum, MELEHI documents the work and life of renowned Moroccan painter and Asilah Cultural Moussem founder Mohamed Melehi through his projects as a teacher, painter, and modernist. Forty years after its production, MELEHI provides a career snapshot of the artist contextualized by his influences across the Moroccan landscape, placing him in the larger history of Morocco and its visual culture. A THOUSAND AND ONE BERBER NIGHTS delves into the transatlantic career of dancer, actor, and choreographer Hassan Ouakrim. In the late 1950s, Ouakrim was a young dancer and actor in Morocco. Little did he know that he would soon become the protegé of La Mama Theatre founder Ellen Stewart, performing across America, forming friendships with the likes of jazz virtuosos Ornette Coleman and Randy Weston, and becoming a pioneer in spreading Berber dance and music in North America. “Asilah Oui: Robert Blackburn in Morocco” at the Blackburn Study Center, September 15-December 12, 2026, focuses on the first decade of the Asilah Cultural Moussem. Established in 1978, this international festival brought together printmakers, musicians, intellectuals, and poets from around the globe to create, as founders Mohamed Benaissa and Mohamad Melehi described it, “a permanent center for cultural diffusion, rich in authenticity and steeped in heritage.” The exhibition illuminates how Robert Blackburn’s Printmaking Workshop served as a conduit in connecting the Moussem’s international artists. This screening is organized by the Robert Blackburn Printmaking Workshop, and co-presented with the Bronx Museum. For more info about the exhibition, visit: https://www.rbpmw-efanyc.org/asilah-oui

title: Fallen Angels
description: Lost souls reach out for human connection amid a glimmering Hong Kong in Wong Kar Wai’s hallucinatory, neon-soaked nocturne. Originally conceived as a segment of Chungking Express only to spin off on its own woozy axis, Fallen Angels plays like the dark, moody flip side of its predecessor as it charts the subtly interlacing fates of a handful of urban loners, including a coolly detached hit man (Leon Lai Ming) looking to go straight; his business partner (Michelle Reis), who secretly yearns for him; and a mute delinquent (Takeshi Kaneshiro) who wreaks mischief by night. Swinging between hard-boiled noir and slapstick lunacy with giddy abandon, the film is both a dizzying, dazzling city symphony and a poignant meditation on love, loss, and longing in a metropolis that never sleeps.

title: Pink Palace: WHO KILLED TEDDY BEAR
description: Pink Palace and Lobotomy Room (devoted to Bad Movies for Bad People) present this tough as nails gritty thriller from the mean streets of sixties New York.  We invite you to take a walk on the wild side with this boundary-pushing and ultra-tawdry 1965 exploitation b-movie. Hip, independent and moder...

title: National Theatre Live: Golden Boy
description: Josh O’Connor (The Crown; Challengers) leads the cast in this searing revival of Clifford Odets’ knockout American classic. 1930s New York, at the height of the Depression. Joe Bonaparte is a gifted young violinist with a future in music, until a chance at fame and fortune lures him into the brutal world of professional boxing. He must confront what he’s willing to sacrifice, who he’s willing to become and how to find his place in a world that demands he choose a side. Brought to life with a live string quartet and filmed live from the Almeida Theatre. Olivier Award-winner Sam Yates (Vanya) directs this propulsive drama exploring ambition, identity, and the high price of success.

title: Possible Love
description: The lives of two married couples from different social strata collide in Lee Chang-dong’s brilliantly unfolding narrative about economic precarity, in which a laid-off factory worker and his wife become the camera subjects for a documentary filmmaker. Winner of the Silver Lion at the 2026 Venice Film Festival and South Korea’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: O.V.A. Night – Vol. III
description: Brain Dead Studios presents O.V.A. Night, a surprise screening of obscure anime rarely seen on the big screen.

title: Possible Love (15)
description: South Korea’s master filmmaker Lee Chang-dong ( Burning , Poetry ) returns with an intertwined drama on two married couples facing different paths and hidden desires.

title: I LOVE BOOSTERS
description: A trio of fashion-forward professional shoplifters take aim at a cutthroat fashion maven. It’s like community service. Absurdist crime comedy from Rio favourite Boots Riley.

title: Wildwood
description: The Portland-set story follows Prue McKeel, who enters an enchanted wonderland when her baby brother Mac is taken by a murder of crows into the forest’s depths.

title: Viva Ingrid! with Journey to Italy
description: Viva Ingrid! A moving documentary tribute to a mother, wife, and actress, this mix of home movies, newsreels, and clips from films by Roberto Rossellini paints a shortform portrait of three-time Academy Award-winning Swedish actress Ingrid Bergman, as realized by one of Rossellini’s grandsons.

title: The Devils
description: Ken Russell’s infamous adaptation of Aldous Huxley’s book, about the apparent possession of a group of nuns after one (Vanessa Redgrave) accuses a priest (Oliver Reed) of collaborating with the devil, is at long last available in its full, uncensored splendor.

title: Ghosts: The Possession of Button House
description: Three friends attempt to communicate with the spirits occupying a haunted house, and become embroiled in a supernatural adventure.

title: Ken Russell's The Devils: The Director's Cut
description: Censored for over half a century, Ken Russell’s film returns in a landmark director’s cut reconstruction that reveals the full power of his original vision. Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, accused of bewitching a convent of nuns, The Devils lays bare the collusion of church and state through a searing vision of religious persecution, collective hysteria and institutional corruption. The restoration many believed would never happen reaffirms Russell’s incendiary masterpiece as among the most overwhelming and uncompromising achievements in British cinema. Assembled from original camera negative, this 4k restoration is Ken Russell’s 2004 preferred edit. Picture and sound restoration by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color and Warner Bros. Sound.

title: NFTS Collective Visions of Pleasure: Shakedown
BULKY TRASH + THE FREE ORCHESTRA
description: Helke Misselwitz BULKY TRASH / SPERRMÜLL 1990, 72 min, 35mm-to-DCP. In German with English subtitles. Filmed in the early summer of 1989, this documentary portrays a band of four young musicians who call themselves “Sperrmüll” (“Bulky Trash”), thanks to their proclivity for producing music by drumming on other people’s discarded items. Misselwitz concentrates especially on Enrico, who decides to stay behind when his mother Erika marries in the West, and who insists on maintaining his cultural identity even after the fall of the Wall. The members of “Sperrmüll” wish to remain citizens of their own state, and their attitude towards the looming reunification is one of skepticism. Originally intended as a call for social change, Misselwitz’s film documents the events of the Wende from the perspective of young East Berliners. Preceded by: Petra Tschörtner THE FREE ORCHESTRA / DAS FREIE ORCHESTER 1988, 17 min, 35mm-to-DCP. In German with English subtitles. “Day in, day out, Barbara sells screws at a store in the East Berlin Market Hall. She is frustrated about having to tell her customers most of the time: ‘Ham wa nich!’ (‘We don’t have that!’) In the evening, she is the loud and wild singer of the legendary East Berlin avantgarde and punk band Das Freie Orchester. Playing music with her friends helps her escape the monotony of her job, express her dissatisfaction with everyday life in East Germany in the 1980s, and dream of a different life.” –DEFA FILM LIBRARY Total running time: ca. 95 min.

title: Fatherland
description: Oscar-nominated director Paweł Pawlikowski (Cold War, NYFF56) won Best Director at Cannes for his most potent film yet, following novelist Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler) and his daughter Erika Mann (Sandra Hüller) on a road trip across Germany in the aftermath of World War II. Poland’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: NAZA (15)
description: Cloaked in darkness on the rooftops of Tel Aviv, Israeli journalist Yuval Abraham conducts shattering one-on-one interviews with Israeli soldiers and intelligence personnel.

title: Primetime (15) (AD)
description: A triumphantly unsettling Robert Pattinson embodies Chris Hansen, host of the 2000s hit To Catch a Predator who sets out to make television history.

title: FATHERLAND
description: At the height of the Cold War, the writer Thomas Mann and his daughter—actress, writer, and rally driver—Erika embark on a road trip in a black Buick cruiser across a divided Germany in ruins, traveling from the Allied-occupied city of Frankfurt to Soviet-controlled Weimar.

title: RICOCHET
description:
One arrest makes Nick Styles a television hero. Years later, the man he put away comes back with a plan to destroy everything the cameras helped him build: career, family, reputation and trust in his own mind.
Denzel Washington and John Lithgow turn Russell Mulcahy’s revenge thriller into a ferocious contest between charisma and obsession. Lithgow’s villain does not just want his enemy dead; he wants control of the story everyone tells about him. Fast, lurid and wildly excessive, RICOCHET pushes studio action towards a full-blown media nightmare.

title: Wicker
description: On the outskirts of a village by the sea, lives a Fisherwoman; smelly, single and perpetually ridiculed. One day, fed up with her stuffy, small-minded neighbors, she commissions herself a husband to be made from wicker. In an otherwise conservative town, this unconventional romance sparks outrage, jealousy and chaos.

title: Wicker
description: On the outskirts of a village by the sea, lives a Fisherwoman; smelly, single and perpetually ridiculed. One day, fed up with her stuffy, small-minded neighbors, she commissions herself a husband to be made from wicker. In an otherwise conservative town, this unconventional romance sparks outrage, jealousy and chaos.

title: The Devils
description: Censored for more than half a century, Ken Russell’s visionary masterpiece returns to the big screen fully restored in 4K and cut to Russell’s direction – the first publicly released version of the film as intended by the filmmaker. Unveiled at the 79th Cannes Film Festival, the definitive version arrives 55 years after the film’s original release. An enduring masterpiece of cinema starring Oliver Reed and Vanessa Redgrave, Ken Russell’s The Devils is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption. Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, accused of bewitching a convent of nuns, the film lays bare the collusion of church and state through a searing vision of religious persecution, collective hysteria and institutional corruption. In addition to powerhouse performances from Reed and Redgrave, Ken Russell’s The Devils showcases the stunning work of artists at the peak of their craft: Academy Award-winning cinematographer David Watkin ( Out of Africa , Chariots of Fire ); editor Michael Bradsell ( Local Hero , Jabberwocky ); and visual artist Derek Jarman ( Jubilee , Caravaggio ), whose work as production designer marked his feature film debut.

title: V For Vendetta
description: In a future British dystopian society, a shadowy freedom fighter, known only by the alias of "V", plots to overthrow the tyrannical government - with the help of a young woman.

title: Godzilla Minus Zero
description: War reduced Japan to zero, and Godzilla plunged it into minus. Two years have passed since then, and the country has faced agonizing struggles to achieve recovery and finally reclaim its daily life. Just as humanity managed to cling to a hard-won peace, a new threat strikes, crushing hope in an instant. There is no third time. Everything ends here.

title: Clayface
description: A shape-shifting creature made of magical clay haunts Gotham City, alternating between villain and ally of Batman. Multiple tragic figures have taken on the Clayface mantle over the years.

title: Double Harness             / Peter Ibbetson
description: Ann Harding and William Powell lend a great dose of chemistry to this lively comedy about a woman who tricks a man into marriage – and only then tries to earn his love the old-fashioned way. Harding plays Joan Colby, a charming young schemer who believes “marriage is a business” and sets her sights on wealthy playboy John Fletcher (Powell). Once Joan slyly arranges for her father to spot her and John in a compromising situation, marriage is no longer an option – it’s a necessity. Smartly directed by John Cromwell, Double Harness was a critical and financial success upon its release; seen today; the movie seems at once modern and nostalgic, offering a vivid reflection of a sophisticated era in filmmaking. (TCM)

title: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
description: After a painful breakup, Clementine (Kate Winslet) undergoes a procedure to erase memories of her former boyfriend Joel (Jim Carrey) from her mind. When Joel discovers that Clementine is going to extremes to forget their relationship, he undergoes the same procedure and slowly begins to forget the woman that he loved. Directed by former music video director Michel Gondry, the visually arresting film explores the intricacy of relationships and the pain of loss.

title: Excalibur
description: Arthur fulfills his fate by bringing together the Knights of the Round Table at Camelot and unifying the country. However, this flawed monarch faces greater tests ahead in pursuit of love, the Holy Grail, and his nation's survival.

title: Bram Stoker's Dracula
description: Coppola at his most boldly baroque, Gary Oldman wearing cinema’s most iconic updo, a puppyish young Keanu Reeves trying to make his way back to Winona Ryder, and Anthony Hopkins as vampire hunter Abraham Van Helsing—it’s all here in this opulent production which returns to the original Stoker text and draws out the piercing sexual ache and romantic longing implicit therein. Part of Winona Ryder Analogue Youth

title: World War Z
description: “The suspense is killer!” proclaims Peter Travers of Rolling Stone in this fast-paced, pulse-pounding epic of the potential last days of the human race. Former United Nations employee Gerry Lane (Brad Pitt) is called upon to help stop the chaotic pandemic that has gripped populations around the world. Lane fights to keep his family safe, while searching for an answer to the outbreak before it destroys all of civilization. David Denby of The New Yorker calls World War Z the “most gratifying action spectacle in years!” (Paramount)

title: News From Home
description: Akerman was 26 years old and living in New York City, away from her native Belgium and her mother, when she teamed with DP Babette Mangolte to film this diary/essay/poem in subway stations and on street corners, their images to eventually be paired with Akerman’s recitals of her mother’s fretful letters. Arguably this extraordinary filmmaker’s most perfect and poignant nonfiction work, both one of the greatest portraits of a city ever put on film and a troubling, touching depiction of maternal love. Screens in the English-language version. “Though Chantal Akerman’s voice can be heard throughout News from Home, her image is only briefly glimpsed, in a reflection on the train. We can’t quite see her, but others undoubtedly can—men, especially, gawk unashamedly, a reminder that the graffiti-covered subway of 1976 New York was often a place of danger and hostility.” —Series curator Genevieve Yue Part of Trains: Local Routes

title: Short Cuts : 35mm Roadshow Tour
description: A multi-storied, fish-eyed look at the human condition against the backdrop of contemporary middle-class LA. Twenty two characters intersect, profoundly and fleetingly, through each other’s lives. It runs the emotional gamut from disturbing to humorous. Don't miss a rare opportunity to see Robert Altman's sprawling epic, showing from an original 35mm print as part of our SHORT CUTS 35mm Roadshow Tour. The 35mm Roadshow Tour will begin at the Prince Charles Cinema, before heading to other sites across the UK in a limited run this November. Special thanks to David Levy for helping us make this happen, and to Curzon for giving us and participating sites access to their print.

title: GuadaLAjara Film Festival – Shorts Block 2: IN GOOD COMPANY
description: From unconventional friendships to shared obsessions, these shorts explore the unexpected but fascinating ways people connect. Each story offers a glimpse into a community, a relationship, or a world where shared experience is what brings people together.

title: Bus Stop
description: This contemporary Western—in which Marilyn Monroe stars as saloon singer Cherie, who dreams of one day making it big in Hollywood—marked a turning point in Marilyn Monroe’s career. She had recently formed Marilyn Monroe Productions and signed a new contract with 20th Century-Fox, earning a higher salary and more creative agency in the process. For the role of Cherie, which was one of the more dramatic and serious of her career to date, she began working with Method acting pioneers Lee and Paula Strasberg, who placed an emphasis on delving into an actor’s own experiences.
director: Joshua Logan PRODUCED BY: Buddy Adler

title: Everytime
description: After a shocking accident befalls a teenage girl in Berlin, her mother, younger sister, and boyfriend drift into a state of suspended grief in Sandra Wollner’s atmospheric, constantly surprising new film, winner of the Cannes Un Certain Regard Prize. Germany’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: Raise the Red Lantern
description: Nineteen-year-old Songlian, a promising student whose family has been destroyed by her father's death, is forced to abandon her studies and marry into wealth, becoming the fourth and newest concubine of the aging, unseen Master Chen. Inside his walled estate, she discovers a household ruled by a merciless ritual: each night, red lanterns are lit outside the chambers of whichever wife the master chooses to visit, granting her privilege and status while the others are cast into cold irrelevance. Songlian is drawn into the orbit of her rivals, each shaped by years of fighting for the same scraps of attention. Determined at first to rise above the games, Songlian is gradually worn down by isolation and humiliation until she strikes back, trading secrets and favors to secure her place in Master Chen’s hierarchy. As petty cruelty turns even more dire, Songlian is forced to confront what these desperate measures will cost her soul. Zhang Yimou’s masterpiece Raise the Red Lantern has been fully restored in 4K.

title: GODS OF TIMES SQUARE
description:
Before the corporate billboards swallowed the skyline, Times Square had other voices: street preachers, prophets, conspiracy theorists and people who believed the end was close. Richard Sandler turns his camera towards the pavement and lets them speak.
Filmed across years of transformation, this extraordinary documentary listens to a neighbourhood arguing about God while the ground changes beneath it. Comic, unsettling, tender and apocalyptic by turns, it preserves personalities no redevelopment plan could accommodate. A city symphony made from competing sermons and the stubborn human need to be heard.

title: The Fifth Element
description: The Earth is about to be destroyed by a huge ball of fire racing toward the planet. Cornelius, an old monk, knows how to stop the burning sphere with the help of Korben Dallas, a taxi driver and former secret agent and a woman named Leeloo.

title: Wild Horse Nine (15)
description: Two eccentric CIA agents ( John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell ) await orders on Easter Island, on the cusp of yet another military coup in Martin McDonagh 's latest dark comedy.

Germany’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: WILD HORSE NINE
description: Shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup, CIA agents Chris and Lee are dispatched from Santiago to Easter Island by their bureau chief, MJ. Amongst the Island's iconic statues, and as the longtime partners wrestle with their dark pasts and present conspiracies, Chris's newfound bond with a pair of rebel...

title: GuadaLAjara Film Festival – CENTERPIECE GALA: 14th
description: The screening will be followed by a conversation with director and producer Ava DuVernay.

title: GIRLS BITE BACK + ROAD MOVIE
description: Wolfgang Büld GIRLS BITE BACK aka WOMEN IN ROCK 1980, 45 min, 16mm-to-DCP. In English and German with English subtitles. “Canvassing a selection of female musicians squarely at the forefront of the post-punk tide, director Wolfgang Büld finds plenty of restless, spiky personalities and intriguing approaches to music and performance. Metal-heads Girlschool, tribal dub merchants The Slits, No Wave experimentalists Mania D, and operatic rock diva Nina Hagen are all featured in live performances, but best of all is a supremely sarcastic Siouxsie Sioux, filmed and interviewed on tour in Berlin.” –SCHAMROCK LiLiPUT ROAD MOVIE 1982/2006, 29 min, Super-8mm-to-digital Recorded in 1982 by the legendary all-female Swiss punk band LiLiPUT (née Kleenex) while on the road, the film captures both the exhilaration and the tedium of touring. Total running time: ca. 80 min.

title: Doc'n'Roll FF: The Best Summer + Q&A
WHO KILLED CAPTAIN ALEX?
description:
Captain Alex is dead, the army wants answers and the Tiger Mafia is taking the fight into the skies above Kampala. Revenge arrives by gunfight, kung fu and helicopter, while Video Joker Emmie supplies a running commentary no conventional action film could survive.
Nabwana I.G.G. and the Wakaliwood team turn scant resources into outrageous invention. The effects are homemade, the commitment is total and the pleasure of making movies is everywhere on screen. An action sensation whose real superpower is the unstoppable creative energy of a community.

title: Cría Cuervos
description: Taking its title from the Spanish proverb “Raise ravens and they will pick your eyes out,” Saura’s lauded allegorical masterwork, set during the twilight of Spain’s Franco dictatorship, stars Ana Torrent (also seen in Spirit of the Beehive, in the same series) as a traumatized eight-year-old, second of three sisters living with a domineering aunt in Madrid following the death of their parents, who feels herself to be drifting freely between the worlds of the living and the dead and is increasingly convinced she has the ability to snuff out her adult persecutors’ lives. “Both an uncanny drama of family dysfunction and a historical parable of the end of Franco-ism… [Geraldine] Chaplin and Torrent are both outstanding.” —The Guardian Part of The Remembered Lives of G. Chaplin & C. Saura

title: The Greg Proops Film Club Presents PARIS BLUES
description: When two Paris nightclub jazz players (Paul Newman and Sidney Poitier) meet two vacationing American beauties (Joanne Woodward and Diahann Carroll), their passion for music is suddenly challenged by their desire for love.

title: AVEDON
description: From world leaders to pop culture icons, and international supermodels, Richard Avedon’s influence helped create the blueprint for our image-driven world. His photographs didn’t just reflect culture, they shaped it.

title: LAST STOP FOR THE CIRCULAR TICKET
description: THE THEATER OF THE MATTERS & TAUFIC PRESENT: JEAN-CLAUDE ROUSSEAU’S ‘THE PASTORAL CONCERT’ + ‘LAST STOP FOR THE CIRCULAR TICKET’ This book launch event celebrates the release of Jean-Claude Rousseau’s unclassifiable, long-unavailable film text, The Pastoral Concert, published for the first time in English this October by Taufic. The evening will culminate in a special premiere screening of Rousseau’s new feature film, LAST STOP FOR THE CIRCULAR TICKET (winner of a Jury Special Mention at this year’s FIDMarseille), alongside his 2006 short, FAUX DÉPART. The Pastoral Concert marks the first English translation of Rousseau’s early written work Le Concert champêtre, begun in 1968, some fifteen years before his debut film. Rousseau continued shaping the work as a screenplay until its rejection by the Centre National de la Cinématographie in 1983. Unrealized, Le Concert champêtre became the matrix from which Rousseau’s subsequent films would emerge. Taking its title and three central characters (A, B, and C) from the eponymous painting long attributed to Giorgione and now to Titian, The Pastoral Concert begins as a letter written by a young man to his cousin in the countryside on the eve of her wedding, before mutating into a diary entry, a screenplay, and finally a film imagined through the failure of its own realization. In this restless fluctuation between registers, The Pastoral Concert expresses, in the words of Jean-Marie Straub, “something magnificent [and] entirely different from a screenplay or a découpage.” Translated from the French by artist and filmmaker Kevin Weil, this edition includes an extensive appendix of extra-diegetic materials written by Rousseau, as well as correspondence with contemporaries such as Dominique Noguez, Marcel Hanoun, and Jean-Marie Straub, which form a picture of the work’s early reception. For more info about The Pastoral Concert visit: https://taufic.org/the-pastoral-concert Jean-Claude Rousseau LAST STOP FOR THE CIRCULAR TICKET / DERNIER ARRÊT POUR LE BILLET CIRCULAIRE 2026, 87 min, DCP. No dialogue. Rousseau’s longest film since THE ENCLOSED VALLEY from 1995 (the summit of his 8mm era), LAST STOP FOR THE CIRCULAR TICKET refers to the looped ferry route that plies the waters of Lake Como in Northern Italy. Firmly grounded in place, Rousseau’s solitary camera finds desolate poetry in the void of the spectacular landscape and in the anonymous crowds of passengers seemingly entranced at the edge of an abyss. Musical chords and voices magnify their gestures and the movement of the vessel on the lake. Closing the circle, the specter of the end looms: “On the ferry, among the travelers, I recognized Mrs. Death…” Preceded by: Jean-Claude Rousseau FAUX DÉPART (2006, 13 min, DCP. No dialogue.)

title: La Bola Negra
description: Spain, 1932. A young man seeks admission to the local casino. In 1937, a conscripted nationalist soldier stands guard over a Republican prisoner. In 2017, a former playwright inherits an unexpected document from his grandfather. Through a dazzlingly constructed and performed triptych, La Bola Negra traces the hidden connections between three men separated by time but bound by experience and the way in which queer lives, memories and histories endure across generations.

title: La Bola Negra (15) (AD)
description: A genre-defying queer epic spanning generations, inspired by the legacy of beloved Spanish poet and playwright Federico García Lorca.

title: MYSTERY MOVIE
description:
Take a seat without knowing what is coming. Our mystery screenings explore the bold, disreputable and gloriously unclassifiable world of psychotronic cinema: discoveries that make you wonder how they were made, who they were made for, and why nobody showed you sooner.
The title stays secret until showtime. Curiosity is essential; good taste is negotiable.
Strictly for adult audiences. Films may contain offensive and upsetting content. Do not attend if you are of a sensitive disposition.

title: George Michael: The Faith Tour
description: Shot at the iconic Palais Omnisports de Paris-Bercy during the European leg of the Faith Tour in 1988, the film captures a turning point that transformed George Michael from a global superstar into a singular, era-defining artist, whose influence continues to reverberate across music, fashion, and culture today. George Michael: The Faith Tour invites audiences to experience the tour as it was meant to be seen and heard. Directed by longtime collaborators Andy Morahan and David Austin, this once lost film has been meticulously restored and remastered, revealing George’s original vision with breathtaking clarity and power. The result is an intimate yet explosive glimpse of an artist in complete command of his voice and stagecraft. A triumph in archival filmmaking, the film transforms footage assembled from a 14-camera shoot captured on 35mm film over two nights, into an extraordinary cinematic event. George Michael: The Faith Tour is a celebration of ambition and fearless artistry at its peak, and a moment when the then 24-year-old George Michael changed the course of his career. This global theatrical event invites audiences to rediscover the power and joy of George Michael in full flight. George Michael: The Faith Tour will open with an original short film by Mary McCartney, titled ‘Finding Faith’, offering an intimate introduction contextualising the tour’s cultural significance, through a sensitive and cinematic lens. In George’s own words, the film features voiceover from an unheard interview alongside unseen images captured by legendary American photographer Herb Ritts, and behind-the-scenes footage of the Faith music video.

Determined to free Tetsuo from capture, Kaneda sneaks into the army research lab. However, a regimen of extreme experimental procedures has awakened a new power in his friend, and now he is consumed by madness..
