description: Spain, 1932. A young man seeks admission to the local casino. In 1937, a conscripted nationalist soldier stands guard over a Republican prisoner. In 2017, a former playwright inherits an unexpected document from his grandfather. Through a dazzlingly constructed and performed triptych, La Bola Negra traces the hidden connections between three men separated by time but bound by experience and the way in which queer lives, memories and histories endure across generations.

title: The Adventures of Prince Achmed
description: This performance will feature a live score performed by Hugo Max . Lotte Reiniger’s The Adventures of Prince Achmed is an enchanting amalgamation of stories from the Arabian Nights animated in cut paper silhouettes, an exquisite artefact of Weimar Cinema and a genre-defying experiment in melding international folk art traditions with the technical possibilities of a new medium. Taken from The Arabian Nights, a wicked sorcerer and the beautiful prince Achmed battle one another in a series of wondrous adventures. Please view this YouTube video for a sample of Hugo's work.

The Torrance family are heading to The Overlook Hotel to spend the winter - but they're got a big surprise coming to them. One of the greatest horror movies of all time The Shining is a masterpiece by one o...

title: In the Company of Men + The Deep North (15)
description: Two films that explore psychodrama as a way of analysing and addressing racial inequality through group workshops, from 1969 and 1988.

title: THE BATTLE OF TUNTENHAUS
description: Juliet Bashore THE BATTLE OF TUNTENHAUS, PART 1 1991, 24 min, DCP. In German with English subtitles. THE BATTLE OF TUNTENHAUS, PART 2 1992, 19 min, DCP. In German with English subtitles. “The Wall has fallen. Berlin has reunified. But there are new zones of transgression to be carved out and explored. Mainzer Straße is a hot spot of squatters and anti-fascist fights. One of the squats on this notorious street, the Tuntenhaus (‘House of Queers’), becomes a specific target of both their neo-Nazi neighbors and the iron fist of the capitalist state. Juliet Bashore’s legendary documentary follows the daily struggle of the queens and queers to create and defend a place for themselves in the chaos and unrest after the fall of communism. The extraordinary union of the anarchist/autonomous and gay scenes meets the onlooking yet involved sympathizers, who also end up in conflict with the squatters as a result of their filming. The film is a unique testimony to the violent and momentous eviction of the people from the streets.” –THE BEACON

title: CYBERCON: Telefantasy Studios Presents Neurocrash w/ Blake Anderson & Friends
EAST OF EDEN (2026) / EAST OF EDEN in 35mm (1955)
description: Hollywood legend James Dean stars in this adaptation of John Steinbeck’s classic novel EAST OF EDEN. Teenaged Cal Trask (Dean–REBEL WITHOUT A CAUSE, GIANT) longs for the affection that his father reserves for his brother Aron, but his efforts meet only rejection. Also attracted to Aron’s girlfriend, Cal becomes so frustrated in his search for love and acceptance that he reveals a long-held secret about their mother to Aron . . . knowledge that now tears the family apart.

title: THE CREATION OF THE HUMANOIDS + SINS OF THE FLESHAPOIDS
description: Wesley Barry THE CREATION OF THE HUMANOIDS 1962, 84 min, 16mm “The Now Future arrived in late 1964, when David Bourdon began his lengthy Village Voice review of Andy Warhol’s ‘Flower Paintings’ with a lengthy account of Wesley Barry’s CREATION OF THE HUMANOIDS, a sci-fi cheapster as color-coded as RED DESERT and more impoverished than ALPHAVILLE… ‘The denouement comes when the heroine and the hero (a militant anti-humanoid who goes around throwing bombs at uppity “clickers”) discover themselves to be machines. This is the happy ending of what Andy Warhol calls the best movie he has ever seen.’” –J. Hoberman, “The New Futurism and the Then Zeitgeist,” ACROSS THE MOVI-VERSE Mike Kuchar SINS OF THE FLESHAPOIDS 1965, 48 min, 16mm. With Bob Cowan, George Kuchar, Donna Kerness, Gina Zuckerman, Maren Thomas, and Julius Middleman. “In the winter of 1964-65, even before THE CREATION OF THE HUMANOIDS was listed, along with feathered boas and Warhol’s SLEEP, in a random list of things The New York Times Magazine deemed as ‘generally agreed’ examples of ‘Pure Camp,’ Mike Kuchar – a 22-year-old photo retoucher living in the Bronx – conceived his own 16mm version of Warhol’s favorite movie…the junkyard analog to the cycle of European films that includes RED DESERT, ALPHAVILLE, and THE TENTH VICTIM.” –J. Hoberman, “The New Futurism and the Then Zeitgeist,” ACROSS THE MOVI-VERSE Total running time: ca. 135 min.

description: Vidiots is thrilled to welcome cinema legends Alison Anders and Illeana Douglas for a special 30th Anniversary Screening of Grace of my Heart !

title: EINSTURZENDE NEUBAUTEN: LIEBESLIEDER
description: An essential text for anyone with a love for the avant-garde. The explosive soundscapes of industrial music titans Einstürzende Neubauten first shook Berlin – then the whole world – to its core in the 1980s. In LIEBESLIEDER, co-directors Klaus Maeck and Johanna Schenkel wield a fractured feast of killer Neubauten performances from Euro television: ones that highlight the group’s cinematic presence, wild handmade instruments, and totally unique style. For those who are at all curious about industrial or noise music in general, this sweaty documentary is unmissable. For Neubauten fans, this humanizing portrait of their first decade provides a fresh take on the band.

title: The Odyssey
description: Odysseus, the legendary King of Ithaca, embarks on a long and perilous journey home following the Trojan War. Throughout his voyage, he is forced to confront the whims of gods, mythological monsters, and trials that stretch both his cunning and his humanity to the breaking point.

title: War for the Planet of the Apes
description: The third film in the contemporary version of the Planet of the Apes series finds the ape leader Caesar (another remarkable motion capture performance by Andy Serkis) seeking a safe haven for the survivors of a human-led massacre, only to wind up in a labor camp run by a vicious military officer (Woody Harrelson). The film was nominated for the visual effects by Joe Letteri, Daniel Barrett, Dan Lemmon and Joel Whist, who depict the film’s ape characters and wintry, post-apocalyptic setting with astonishing realism.

description: In 1962 Hong Kong, neighbors Su Li-zhen (Mrs. Chan) and Chow Mo-wan (Mr. Chow) discover their spouses are having an affair. As they spend time together, they develop feelings for each other, but their relationship remains chaste and unspoken, reflecting societal constraints and their own moral compass.

title: The Getaway (IB Tech Print)             / Charley Varrick
description: A thief is granted early parole from the State Pen in exchange for pulling off one last bank heist. But when things go awry, the ex-con and his wife must hit the asphalt and make their getaway – cash in hand and with both cops and criminals in pursuit – while navigating a series of deadly double-crosses that threaten to get them caught or killed. Steve McQueen and Ali MacGraw star in Sam Peckinpah’s hard-nosed thriller, featuring a memorable score by Quincy Jones and a lean script from Walter Hill based on Jim Thompson’s novel.

title: Angel's Egg
description: In an underwater city, a young girl takes care of a large egg she holds carefully in her arms. A boy with a gun arrives in search of a bird he saw in his dream. At first, it seems as if feelings of sympathy are developing between the two. Forty years after the film’s original release, Anime Limited is proud to present an all-new 4K restoration of the film, supervised by director Mamoru Oshii, in cinemas nationwide for the very first time. The film is a creative collaboration between acclaimed director Mamoru Oshii (Ghost in the Shell), who wrote and directed the feature, and revered artist Yoshitaka Amano (Final Fantasy, Vampire Hunter D). The film beautifully intertwines Oshii’s thematic reflections on philosophy and theology with Amano’s distinctive ink painting style, culminating in an arrestingly beautiful hand-drawn allegorical fantasy.

title: Benedetta
description: With this orgiastic immersion in the mystic reveries of a real-life historical figure, the king of the erotic thriller Paul Verhoeven gives the nunsploitation flick a high-art makeover. Elegant, perverse, and teasingly scandalous, Benedetta critiques religious hypocrisy with an impish grin.

title: Kingdom of Heaven: Director's Cut
description: Ridley Scott's extended cut of an epic adventure about a common man who finds himself thrust into a decades-long war. Orlando Bloom plays a humble blacksmith who discovers that he is the son of a knght, and travels to the Holy Land to fight in the crusades. A stranger in a strange land, he serves a doomed King, falls in love with an exotic and forbidden Queen, and rises to knighthood. Ultimately, he must protect the people of Jerusalem from overwhelming forces, while striving to keep a fragile peace.

title: The Love Witch
description: “She Loved Men... To Death.” Addicted to love, Elaine – the love witch – casts love and sex spells to seek her perfect man, finding herself with more dead bodies than she does a long-term partner… A visually-striking, humorous and thought-provoking film by the continuously playful Anna Biller, The Love Witch has caused immense debate by audiences through its feminist themes. Visually drenched in 1970s fashion and cinematography, the film´s style feels as magical as the love witch herself. The Love Witch is featured as part of MANEATERS, a season exploring the female supernatural on screen. The season is presented with the National Film and Television School’s Film Studies, Programming and Curation MA.

title: CYBERCON: Forge Your Node – Build Your Own Mesh Network Device Workshop W/ Lisa Winter
Imamura: History of Postwar Japan as Told by a Bar Hostess
Short Films by William Greaves 1959-1974 (15)
description: From Cinema Verité docs and observational filmmaking, to public information films exploring Black history, this selection from the renowned filmmaker shows the versatility in his works and styles.

title: NIGHTMARES COME AT NIGHT
description:
A dancer wakes from dreams of murder convinced that she may have committed the crimes herself. Inside a remote villa, reassurance only makes things stranger: every lover, doctor and memory seems to have another purpose.
Diana Lorys gives Jesús Franco’s elusive thriller a fragile centre as the story drifts between gaslighting, desire and nightmare. Mirrors, bedrooms and unstable recollections take the place of firm ground. Its pleasure lies in that disorientation: an intimate psychological mystery that keeps changing shape just when you think you have found a way through.
Presented by Cosmik Debris.

title: George Michael: The Faith Tour
description: Shot at the iconic Palais Omnisports de Paris-Bercy during the European leg of the Faith Tour in 1988, the film captures a turning point that transformed George Michael from a global superstar into a singular, era-defining artist, whose influence continues to reverberate across music, fashion, and culture today. George Michael: The Faith Tour invites audiences to experience the tour as it was meant to be seen and heard. Directed by longtime collaborators Andy Morahan and David Austin, this once lost film has been meticulously restored and remastered, revealing George’s original vision with breathtaking clarity and power. The result is an intimate yet explosive glimpse of an artist in complete command of his voice and stagecraft. A triumph in archival filmmaking, the film transforms footage assembled from a 14-camera shoot captured on 35mm film over two nights, into an extraordinary cinematic event. George Michael: The Faith Tour is a celebration of ambition and fearless artistry at its peak, and a moment when the then 24-year-old George Michael changed the course of his career. This global theatrical event invites audiences to rediscover the power and joy of George Michael in full flight. George Michael: The Faith Tour will open with an original short film by Mary McCartney, titled ‘Finding Faith’, offering an intimate introduction contextualising the tour’s cultural significance, through a sensitive and cinematic lens. In George’s own words, the film features voiceover from an unheard interview alongside unseen images captured by legendary American photographer Herb Ritts, and behind-the-scenes footage of the Faith music video.

title: Never Watching Movies: SMOKE SIGNALS
description: NEVER WATCHING MOVIES presents Smoke Signals (1998), the first feature film written, directed and produced by an all Native American filmmaking crew (going on to win the audience award and filmmaker trophy at Sundance 1998). The film follows childhood friends Victor  and Thomas as they travel off th...

title: POSTCOLONIAL MOTION: TAXIS AND TRAVELOGUES
description: While not as long-standing as the romance with trains, cinema has a love affair with taxis. A cab ride is often more than just a means of getting from one place to another. The taxi is a cinematic apparatus in motion, a confessional, an urban microcosm, a transition, a temporary intimacy, an archive of daily life, a nightmare of forced conversation, an eavesdropper’s dream. Yet beneath such metaphors are material threats: the gig economy, prior and enduring precarities and exploitation of labor, movements of migration conditioned by colonization. POSTCOLONIAL MOTION: TAXIS AND TRAVELOGUES draws together three films combining oral testimonies and the kinetics of transport. Frank Sweeney, Karimah Ashadu, and Timoteus Anggawan Kusno each consider the movements of people, goods and images, tracing how workers warp the barriers of historical categories and economic constraints as they cross borders. Guest-programmed by Yasmina Price, who wrote the introduction and individual film descriptions. Frank Sweeney GO YE AFAR 2026, 24 min, DCP Irish research-based artist Frank Sweeney’s latest work, GO YE AFAR (2026), stages a historical examination of economy, religion, national identity, and state power through the nocturnal taxi journey of a Nigerian driver in Dublin and Calabar. Making a link between the IMF’s role in imposing a debt structure on Ireland in the 2010s and the economic dependency still inflicted on the African continent, Sweeney makes a taxi journey an illuminating lens onto the dubious legacies of Catholic missionaries and European philanthropy, global privatization and the erosion of the commons. Karimah Ashadu BROWN GOODS 2020, 12 min, DCP BROWN GOODS (2020), by British-born Nigerian artist and director Karimah Ashadu, both shares and reconfigures a similar terrain. The film scans the intermingled economies and geographies of Africa and Europe, conjuring Nigeria from its viewpoint in Germany. The setting is specifically Hamburg, a hub of international trade and multinational corporations. Ashadu’s agile camerawork delves through docks, weaving amongst ship containers and stacks of tires as Emeka – the self-sufficient central figure, excluded from formal work due to his humanitarian status – voices a sharp analysis of manufacturing and industrial monopolies, the politics of resources and global capital. Timoteus Anggawan Kusno OBSCURA 2026, 14 min, DCP Indonesian filmmaker and visual artist Timoteus Anggawan Kusno’s OBSCURA (2026) echoes the unsettling, spectral dreaminess and mediatized archival memory of GO YE AFAR. Operating between Indonesia and the Netherlands, the film critically reworks the form of the ethnographic travelogue and colonial imagery through a story of theft (another kind of informal job). Gallery workers liberate a painting and carry it out in a truck, performing how images physically travel, are taken apart, literally unframed and reframed. Total running time: ca. 55 min. The screening will be followed by a conversation with filmmaker and artist Frank Sweeney!

title: NARROW ROOMS: DRUNKEN NOODLES
description: Lucio Castro DRUNKEN NOODLES 2025, 83 min, DCP. In English and Spanish with English subtitles. When Adnan (Laith Khalifeh) arrives in New York to work at a Lower East Side gallery for the summer, he’s newly single and ready to mingle. He cruises strangers in the park at night and begins a flirtation with a delivery driver. At work, he’s helping to exhibit the recently discovered work of Sal Salandra, a real-world gay artist and elder who crafts tableaus of gay orgies and sex club scenes in vibrant needlepoint. These artworks – and Sal himself, played by Ezriel Kornel – become the connective thread for a time-jumping narrative that unfolds in four parts. Made for little money, with a small crew and total creative control, the latest by Lucio Castro (END OF THE CENTURY) is a delightful, sexually-charged short-story collection with whimsical elements of dreamy magical realism. Released during the full flower of NYC PRIDE season, DRUNKEN NOODLES is well worth watching – or rewatching – before making your Best-of-2026 lists. We’ll be joined by director Lucio Castro and cast members for a Q&A following the screening!

title: Pink Palace: IN A YEAR OF 13 MOONS
description: Pink Palace presents this beautifully restored, rarely seen melancholic gem by the “enfant terrible” of New German Cinema, Rainer Werner Fassbinder.  Made in response to the suicide of Rainer Werner Fassbinder's lover Armin Meier, IN A YEAR OF 13 MOONS is a story of unrequited love, a tortured past ...

description: Join us at Brain Dead Studios for an intimate screening of the 1985 animated classic Angel’s Egg , featuring a live score performed on stage by Iggor Cavalera (Sepultura, Soulwax, Cavalera).

title: NFTS Collective Visions of Pleasure: The Cruel Woman
FEMALE VAMPIRE
description:
Countess Irina Karlstein moves through an island landscape with a hunger she cannot escape. Those drawn to her become victims; the poet who recognises her loneliness offers the possibility of something more dangerous than feeding: intimacy.
Lina Romay gives Jesús Franco’s vampire reverie its strange mixture of command and vulnerability. Drifting camera movements, misty locations and Daniel White’s score suspend the story between erotic fantasy and a melancholy dream. A film less interested in the mechanics of vampirism than in the terrible solitude of wanting what you cannot keep.
Presented by Cosmik Debris.

title: Akira
description: Iconic and game-changing, AKIRA is the definitive anime masterpiece! Katsuhiro Otomo's landmark cyberpunk classic obliterated the boundaries of Japanese animation and forced the world to look into the future. AKIRA's arrival shattered traditional thinking, creating space for future generations of ground-breaking movies. July, 1988 - World War III breaks loose. Then, in 2019, in megalopolis Tokyo...As the leader of a group of young robust delinquents, Kaneda spent his nights tearing through the urban wastes, racing his motorbike against rival groups. One night while riding with his gang, his friend Tetsuo suddenly encounters a strange boy - the product of human experimentation and is injured in the ensuing crash. Shortly thereafter, a military squadron appears on the scene to take the boy and Tetsuo away to an army research facility. Determined to free Tetsuo from capture, Kaneda sneaks into the army research lab. However, a regimen of extreme experimental procedures has awakened a new power in his friend, and now he is consumed by madness..

title: Have A Gd Trip presents Welcome To Hell & Bag of Suck Double Feature
description: For one night only, Have A Gd Trip brings Skateboarding Film Club back to Prince Charles Cinema for an essential double bill celebrating two definitive eras of skate culture. Kicking off the night is the 20th anniversary of Enjoi’s Bag of Suck (2006)—a Transworld Video of the Year winner that balanced jaw-dropping technical progression (anchored by Jerry Hsu’s legendary parts) with the irreverent, fun-first humour that made Enjoi an instant classic. Followed by the 30th anniversary of Toy Machine’s Welcome to Hell (1996)—a relentless masterpiece that set the standard for high-impact handrail skating, immortalised Jamie Thomas’s raw style, and helped launch legends like Elissa Steamer. Welcome to Hell 1996 | 45mins | USA | (18) | Skateboarding Video Directed by Jamie Thomas, Video introduction by Ed Templeton Starring Jamie Thomas, Ed Templeton, Elissa Steamer, Chad Muska, Brian Anderson, Donny Barley Bag of Suck 2006 | 50mins | USA | (18) | Skateboarding Video Directed by Matt Eversole and Kyle Camarillo, Video introduction by Louie Barletta Starring Jerry Hsu, Louie Barletta, Marc Johnson, Caswell Berry, Stevie Williams, Cairo Foster "Pandas, heavy handrails, and pure raw energy." Two iconic videos, three decades of skate history, together for one night only. Rarely seen on the big screen—don't miss out.

title: Snatch
description: Guy Ritchie, writer/director of Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels , delivers another awe-inspiring directorial masterpiece, Snatch – an edgy and hilarious film about a diamond heist gone wrong, a colorful Irish gypsy-turned-prize fighter… and a very temperamental dog. In the heart of gangland, two novice unlicensed boxing promoters, Turkish (Jason Statham) and Tommy (Stephen Graham), get roped into organizing a rigged bare-knuckle fight with local kingpin/villain and fellow boxing promoter Brick Top (Alan Ford). But all goes wrong when wildcard boxer One Punch Mickey O’Neil (Brad Pitt) starts playing by his own rules, and the duo find themselves heading for a whole lot of trouble. Meanwhile, Franky Four Fingers (Benicio Del Toro) and his stolen 86-carat diamond have gone missing in London. Head honcho Avi (Dennis Farina) hires local legend Bullet Tooth Tony (Vinnie Jones) to find them, launching everyone into a spiral of double-crossing vendettas and events, most of them illegal. (Columbia Pictures)

title: The Killing of a Sacred Deer
Amelie - 25th Anniversary
description: 23-year-old Amélie is lonely. After an isolating childhood, she moves to Paris and becomes a waitress at the Café des Deux Moulins, a bar restaurant filled with a colourful cast of diners and employees. One night, Amélie happens across a box of treasures hidden in her apartment, left by a little boy in the Fifties, that changes the course of her life. Henceforth, she dedicates herself to giving back to her community, tracking down the owner of these keepsakes, consoling a widowed neighbour and befriending a reclusive artist. When completing these good deeds, she crosses paths with Nino, a photobooth collagist who shares her oddball sensibilities. She quickly falls in love with him.

title: Some Like It Hot
description: Marilyn Monroe’s work in director Billy Wilder’s comedic classic is often cited as her best. The film was controversial for its racy humor and story about two musicians (Tony Curtis and Jack Lemmon) who disguise themselves as women to evade the Mafia. But of equal scandal were the Oscar-winning costumes made by Orry-Kelly for Monroe’s Sugar Kane Kowalczyk. Both dresses are on display in the exhibit Marilyn Monroe: Hollywood Icon , on view through February 28, 2027. Some Like It Hot was made during a year of dramatic highs and lows for Monroe, with this film standing as a high point.
director: Billy Wilder PRODUCED BY: Billy Wilder

title: Ken Russell's The Devils: The Director's Cut
description: Censored for over half a century, Ken Russell’s film returns in a landmark director’s cut reconstruction that reveals the full power of his original vision. Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, accused of bewitching a convent of nuns, The Devils lays bare the collusion of church and state through a searing vision of religious persecution, collective hysteria and institutional corruption. The restoration many believed would never happen reaffirms Russell’s incendiary masterpiece as among the most overwhelming and uncompromising achievements in British cinema. Assembled from original camera negative, this 4k restoration is Ken Russell’s 2004 preferred edit. Picture and sound restoration by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color and Warner Bros. Sound.

title: Porco Rosso (Japanese with English Subtitles)
description: From the legendary Studio Ghibli , creators of Spirited Away , and Academy Award-winning director Hayao Miyazaki , comes a dazzling aerial adventure set in and above the scenic port towns of the Adriatic Sea. “Porco Rosso” is a world-weary flying ace-turned-bounty-hunter, whose face has been transformed into that of a pig by a mysterious spell. When he infuriates a band of sky pirates with his heroics, the pirates hire Curtis, a hotshot American rival, to get rid of him. But with the help of the teenage girl Fio, an aspiring airplane designer, and a sultry lounge singer named Gina, Porco takes to the skies for what may be his final high-flying showdown.

title: FOR Y'UR HEIGHT ONLY
description:
Agent 00 has a kidnapped scientist to rescue, an evil mastermind to stop and a gadget for almost every occasion. The odds are absurd. Weng Weng treats them as an invitation.
Eddie Nicart’s Filipino spy adventure gives its star a full arsenal of rooftop escapes, martial-arts encounters and Bond-style ingenuity. What makes it irresistible is the commitment: the film plays its impossible mission with an infectious mixture of swagger and invention. A scrappy international cult favourite powered by a performer who makes every entrance his own.

title: Members Only Preview: All of a Sudden
Jason and the Argonauts
description: Jason, a fearless sailor and explorer, returns to his home land of Thessaly after a long voyage to claim his rightful throne. He learns, however, that he must first find the magical Golden Fleece. To do so, he must embark on an epic quest fraught with fantastic monsters and terrible perils.

title: The Time Masters
description: Directed by visionary science-fiction animator René Laloux (Fantastic Planet) and designed by the legendary Jean Giraud (a.k.a. Mœbius) The Time Masters is a visually fantastic foray into existentialist space adventure. After his parents are killed on the dangerous planet Perdide, young Piel (voiced by Frédéric Legros) survives by maintaining radio contact with Jaffar (Jean Valmont), a pilot transporting the exiled Prince Matton (Yves-Marie Maurin) and Princess Belle (Monique Thierry) from their former kingdom. Jaffar seeks the help of Silbad (Michel Elias), a cheerful old-timer who knows how to circumvent Perdide’s hazards, including brain-devouring insects and watery graves. Along the way, Jaffar and company encounter a pair of impish homunculi stowaways, identity-less angels controlled by an amorphous hive mind, and the Masters of Time, mysterious beings who can bend reality and perhaps reveal to the heroes their secret origins and destinies. Restored in 4K in 2023 at the initiative of CITE FILMS in collaboration with the Fondazione Cineteca di Bologna and with the support of the CNC

title: CYBERCON: Peow Studio Book Launch & Exhibition W/ Zimmerit Panel + Godzilla: Final Wars
description: Humanity finally rids themselves of Godzilla, imprisoning him in an icy tomb in the South Pole. All is peaceful until various monsters emerge to lay waste to Earth’s cities. Overwhelmed, humanity is seemingly saved by a race of benevolent aliens known as Xiliens. But not all is what it seems with these bizarre visitors. If humanity wishes to survive, they must reluctantly resurrect their most hated enemy, Godzilla.

title: BARBARA
description: With Jeanne Balibar, Mathieu Amalric, Vincent Peirani, Aurore Clement, and Grégoire Colin. Amalric’s seventh feature-length film as a director is both a heartfelt tribute to the legendary chanteuse Barbara (1930-97), and a vehicle for another peerlessly talented French luminary, the actress and singer Jeanne Balibar. Amalric’s films are remarkable for their intuitive freedom, and their emphasis on emotional textures and states of feeling rather than on straightforward narrative construction or easily grasped meanings. BARBARA is a case in point: eschewing anything like a coherent, birth-to-death account of the events of her life, the film instead orchestrates fragments of the singer’s life and performances into a free and quasi-abstract meditation on Barbara’s identity and cultural presence. And by casting Balibar not as Barbara per se but more self-referentially as an actress making a film-within-the-film about the singer, his film becomes an even broader investigation into the concept of biographical filmmaking, representation, and identity. An experimental biopic in the tradition of Stanley Kwan’s CENTER STAGE, Peter Watkins’s EDVARD MUNCH, and Paul Leduc’s FRIDA, it features a typically riveting, charismatic performance from Balibar.

title: An Unfinished Film
description: ★★★★★ “An utterly unique and very important movie about Covid, the crisis that affected all of us.” – The Guardian Director Xiaorui convinces his cast and crew to resume the shooting of a film halted ten years earlier. In January 2020, with the shoot almost complete, rumours regarding an illness begin to circulate. A hairdresser from Wuhan is sent home, while the crew follows the news on their phones. The director has to decide whether to halt the filming once again. Some of the crew and actors manage to leave before the hotel is locked down by security guards and everyone left on set is confined to their hotel rooms. As all communication is reduced to phone screens, Wuhan is locked down. The crew continues to communicate via video calls, whilst the quarantined main actor Jiang Cheng struggles to support his wife who is now locked-down with their month-old baby in Beijing.

title: Blood Simple
description: Sexy, smart, and smoldering, this shocking neo-noir shot the Coen brothers into the upper echelons of filmmakers right off the bat. Far beyond your average freshman fare, the Coen Brothers debut film Blood Simple is stylish, brutal, and tinged with that signature Coen wit. The owner of a seedy small-town Texas bar discovers that one of his employees is having an affair with his wife. A chaotic chain of misunderstandings, lies, and mischief ensues after he devises a plot to have them murdered.

title: Pushkin House: Hard to Be a God
LPFF 2026: Opening Night - Who is Still Alive (15*) + ScreenTalk
The Odyssey
description: Odysseus, the legendary King of Ithaca, embarks on a long and perilous journey home following the Trojan War. Throughout his voyage, he is forced to confront the whims of gods, mythological monsters, and trials that stretch both his cunning and his humanity to the breaking point.

title: Black Fire
description: Since 2013, artist Kevin Jerome Everson and author and historian Claudrena N. Harold have cooperated on a series of lyrical short films—13 to date—that explore Black intellectual, social, and political life at the University of Virginia in Charlottesville, where both are professors. Collectively titled Black Fire , these works highlight the spaces where Black students have studied, learned, and organized through the years, including the school's student-run newspaper and a bus stop that became a locus for collective action. Through short films spotlighting figures such as Paulette Jones Morant, one of the first Black woman scholastic athletes at UVA, and Vivian Gordon, the director of UVA’s Black Studies program from 1974–1980, Black Fire creates significant space for otherwise under-the-radar figures. Employing interviews and reenactment, often casting their students as performers, Everson and Harold's films bring the history of UVA, as well as the historical experiences of Black students and faculty across the US, into meaningful conversation with the present day. Filmmakers Kevin Jerome Everson and Claudrena N. Harold appear in conversation after the films, moderated by filmmaker Cauleen Smith. Special thanks to Madeleine Molyneaux, Sam Raphael, and Now Instant Image Hall.

title: Evangelion: Death (True)² + The End of Evangelion : Double Feature
description: EVANGELION: DEATH (TRUE)²: A recap of the first 24 episodes of Neon Genesis Evangelion. Fifteen years after the Second Impact, apathetic teen Shinji joins his father's group NERV to fight the Angels. But the truth may destroy them all. THE END OF EVANGELION: Concurrent theatrical ending of the TV series Neon Genesis Evangelion (1995). Seele orders an all-out attack on NERV, aiming to destroy the Evas before Gendo can trigger Third Impact and Instrumentality under his control.

title: HOLD ME TIGHT / SERRE MOI FORT
description: With Vicky Krieps, Arieh Worthalter, Anne-Sophie Bowen-Chatet, and Sacha Ardilly. “Propelled by a fierce, tour-de-force performance by Vicky Krieps, who is fast becoming one of the most sought-after actors on the international scene, HOLD ME TIGHT is an ingenious memory piece exploring the grief of separation and the paradoxical comforts and claustrophobia of the domestic home. As Clarisse flees her family at daybreak and hits the open road, leaving her husband and two children behind, the film shuttles between time and space, becoming a mental landscape whose contours are gradually revealed like fleeting moments of reminiscence – those that ultimately make up a life. With its beguiling, puzzle-piece structure that builds to a shattering denouement, HOLD ME TIGHT powerfully keeps its audience in a state of hypnotic reverie as we share in the protagonist’s profound sense of disorientation, the sort of disembodied surrealism that uncertainty can unleash. Yet Krieps gives a surprisingly earth-bound, visceral performance as a woman negotiating a new path for herself, all while trying to stay close to those she loves and attempting to make sense of it all.” –Andréa Picard, TIFF

title: The Return of the Living Dead
description: The most fun you’ll ever have with the undead! A gang of Punks and New Wave ne’er-do-wells get trapped in a cemetery as the dead begin to rise and start to crash their party. And these aren’t your average zombies. They can talk, reason, and even make jokes, but make no mistake — they are still out for your brains. A total blast from start to finish, this monster bash features killer special effects, a rockin’ soundtrack, and one of scream queen Linnea Quigley’s most iconic moments. You’d be a ghoul to miss it!

title: Drive
description: Drawing inspiration from Walter Hill’s The Driver, Refn’s high-style tour-de-force stars Ryan Gosling as a loner Los Angeles stunt driver who moonlights as a getaway wheelman on armed stickups, who’s put on a collision course with a nefarious criminal syndicate thanks to his protective affection for neighbor Carey Mulligan. A terse, tough, and morosely moody film propelled by a shimmering synth-pop score, with an extraordinary supporting cast that includes an against-type Albert Brooks as a sullen, profane gangster kingpin. Part of Pulse

title: Once Upon A Time In… Hollywood
description: Quentin Tarantino’s Once Upon a Time in… Hollywood visits 1969 Los Angeles, where everything is changing, as TV star Rick Dalton (Leonardo DiCaprio) and his longtime stunt double Cliff Booth (Brad Pitt) make their way around an industry they hardly recognize anymore. The ninth film from the writer-director features a large ensemble cast and multiple storylines in a tribute to the final moments of Hollywood’s golden age.

title: Lady Terminator
description: The spirit of an ancient evil queen possesses the body of a young anthropological student, who then goes on a murderous rampage.

title: The Burning             / Madman
description: A legend of terror isn’t a campfire story anymore! Five years after a prank horribly went wrong, the deranged former caretaker of Camp Blackfoot returns with his shears set for a summer camp slaughter. One of the best & bloodiest to follow in the wake of Friday the 13 th , The Burning is a vicious slasher blast filled with a before-they-were-stars cast, including Brian Backer ( Fast Times at Ridgemont High ), Jason Alexander, Fisher Stevens, and Holly Hunter.

title: Kung Fu Panda
description: Prepare for awesomeness with DreamWorks Animation’s Kung Fu Panda, “a delightful movie that can stand among the very best animated features” (Leonard Maltin, Entertainment Tonight). Jack Black is perfect as the voice of Po, a noodle-slurping dreamer who must embrace his true self – fuzzy flaws and all – in order to become the Dragon Warrior. With groundbreaking animation, an all-star cast and high-kicking humor, the Academy Award-nominated Kung Fu Panda is delightful entertainment for the whole family! (Universal)

title: The Westerner
description: Judge Roy Bean, a self-appointed hanging judge in Vinegarroon, Texas, befriends saddle tramp Cole Harden, who opposes Bean's policy against homesteaders.

title: FFC: Ernest and Celestine - Winter Tales (U*)
description: The delightful duo, Ernest and Celestine – a grumpy bear and a feisty mouse – are back in a series of four short stories perfect for a family cinema snuggle!

title: The Pirates! In an Adventure with Scientists!
description: Another gem from Aardman Productions, adapted by Gideon Defoe from his children's book. The Pirates! In an Adventure with Scientists! follows a crew…

title: Troy
description: In year 1250 B.C. during the late Bronze age, two emerging nations begin to clash. Paris, the Trojan prince, convinces Helen, Queen of Sparta, to leave her husband Menelaus, and sail with him back to Troy. After Menelaus finds out that his wife was taken by the Trojans, he asks his brother Agamemnon to help him get her back. Agamemnon sees this as an opportunity for power. They set off with 1,000 ships holding 50,000 Greeks to Troy.

title: Frankenweenie
description: Based on Tim Burton’s 1984 short film, Frankenweenie follows young Victor Frankenstein as he goes about his childhood making short films with his four-legged canine friend, Sparky. When Sparky is killed by a car, a distraught Victor resurrects him. Soon other children start resurrecting their own pets, and a horde of undead creatures wreaks havoc, spurring the adults to plot Sparky’s permanent demise. This black-and-white stop motion Frankenstein adaptation features a score by frequent Burton collaborator Danny Elfman and is filled with homages to the classic horror films Burton grew up loving, resulting in a scary and sweet fairytale that will dazzle children and charm adults.
director: Tim Burton PRODUCED BY: Allison Abbate, Tim Burton

title: TWO SEASONS, TWO STRANGERS
description: Based on two mangas by Yoshiharu Tsuge, Miyake’s bifurcated live-action feature observes (and draws parallels and contrasts from) a summertime meet-cute between Nagisa and Natsuo and a snowbound winter encounter between screenwriter Li and innkeeper Benzo.

title: PRIFF Programme 1
description: BETWEEN WORLDS brings together two stories of people searching for their place in the world. In Manila, half-Filipina Nia trains in secret with queer outcast Malic to join a Filipino Martial Arts team, learning that winning begins with accepting who she is. In a remote Senegalese village, young albino Ousmane faces daily insults and threats rooted in superstition, until he and his mother set out across the desert towards Europe, facing exhaustion, dehydration and ruthless smugglers along the way. Together, these films explore what it means to be different, and how difference can become a source of rejection or of shared strength.

title: The Princess Bride
description: A fairy tale adventure about a beautiful young woman and her one true love. He must find her after a long separation and save her. They must battle the evils of the mythical kingdom of Florin to be reunited with each other.

title: Big Hero 6
description: Disney meets Marvel in this thrilling and charming tale of robotic friendship and fighting for what’s right. A special bond develops between plus-sized inflatable robot Baymax, and prodigy Hiro Hamada, who team up with a group of friends to form a band of high-tech heroes. So join us in San Fransokyo with your family and inflatable friends.

title: Ratatouille
description: He’s dying to become a chef. In Pixar’s critically acclaimed blockbuster, a Parisian rat with a passion for cooking finds an unlikely partner for his culinary dreams. Now the improbable human-rodent duo will hilariously turn the restaurant world upside down with their delicious dishes, if their differences don’t derail them first. Winner of the Academy Award for the Best Animated Feature Film of the Year.

description: Mitsuha and Taki are total strangers living completely different lives. But when Mitsuha makes a wish to leave her mountain town for the bustling city of Tokyo, they become connected in a bizarre way. She dreams she is a boy living in Tokyo, while Taki dreams he is a girl from a rural town he has ne...

title: PRIFF Programme 2
description: INHERITANCE brings together six films about what we inherit from our families and the systems that shape our lives. Alone in an empty church, a writer sets out to sever his relationship with God, only for a childhood memory of violence to turn his accusation back on himself. Malaika prepares for her wedding while struggling to live up to the ideal bride imposed by her mother and her Kenyan heritage. Released from prison, young father Obi arrives at a Nigerian café in a spacesuit, stretching the lie that he has been in space just long enough to win over his curious daughter. In racially divided 1950s Britain, an Afro Caribbean miner struggles to find acceptance above ground. Sound recordist Dina turns to her craft to preserve the presence of her mother, a classical singer, as her health fades. And Out of the Ashes follows the organisers who, in 2020, built a fund of their own for Black and brown communities, challenging centuries of deciding who deserves help.

title: DÉJÀ VU
description: Called in to recover evidence in the aftermath of a horrific explosion on a New Orleans ferry, Federal agent Doug Carlin (Denzel Washington) gets pulled away from the scene and taken to a top-secret government lab that uses a time-shifting surveillance device to help prevent crime. But can it help Carlin change the past? Hold on to your seat for an explosive and intriguing thrill ride you’ll want to experience again and again.

title: LPFF 2026: Who is Still Alive (15*) + ScreenTalk
description: Nine voices from Gaza. Nine people who tell of their lives before and amid the destruction, in the neighbourhoods whose outlines they draw in chalk on the ground.

title: And Your Bird Can Sing preceded by August 8th
The Grand Budapest Hotel
description: In the 1930s, the Grand Budapest Hotel is a popular European ski resort, presided over by concierge Gustave H. (Ralph Fiennes). Zero, a junior lobby boy, becomes Gustave's friend and protege. Gustave prides himself on providing first-class service to the hotel's guests, including satisfying the sexual needs of the many elderly women who stay there. When one of Gustave's lovers dies mysteriously, Gustave finds himself the recipient of a priceless painting and the chief suspect in her murder.

title: MUSIC IS MUSIC + BEFORE IT'S TOO LATE
description: Mathieu Amalric MUSIC IS MUSIC 2017, 20 min, DCP “In a poetic composition of song, narration, and images, this film follows Canadian soprano and orchestra conductor Barbara Hannigan, accompanied by the Ludwig Orchestra, as she records her album ‘Crazy Girl Crazy’. Why did she choose these three pieces, in essence so different, but which intimately resonate with her: Berio’s ‘Sequenza III’, Berg’s ‘Lulu Suite’, and Gershwin’s ‘Girl Crazy’?” –INTERNATIONAL FESTIVAL OF FILMS ON ART Mathieu Amalric BEFORE IT’S TOO LATE / AVANT QU’IL NE SOIT TROP TARD 2023, 65 min, DCP “After 47 years together, the Emerson String Quartet records their last album, ‘Infinite Voyage’, in three days. For this farewell, they invited soprano Barbara Hannigan, and a film was born. Their precise work, the moments of enthusiasm and fear, the research and the jokes, the age limit of these men and Hannigan’s flamboyance, the admiring friendship full of irony and rigor, the profession and yet the discovery, humor as a cog towards concentration, the individual and the group…all this composes a portrait of the usually invisible production of music. Before everyone resumes their path.” –DOCLISBOA Total running time: ca. 90 min.

title: TIMES SQUARE
description:
Two teenagers escape a psychiatric hospital and turn the streets of New York into their stage. As the Sleez Sisters, Pamela and Nicky invent a noisy new identity that parents, police and respectable society cannot comfortably contain.
Trini Alvarado and Robin Johnson give Allan Moyle’s cult film its bruised, rebellious heart. A tremendous punk and new-wave soundtrack propels a vision of friendship as self-invention, against a Midtown that has since disappeared. Ragged, romantic and fiercely attached to its outsiders, TIMES SQUARE is a love song to girls making themselves heard.

title: On the Waterfront
description: I coulda been a contender. I coulda been somebody, instead of a bum, which is what I am, let’s face it. You might know that iconic quote, and you might be aware that Marlon Brando’s performance in this movie was a game-changer in film history, helping to popularize the more naturalistic style known as Method acting. But don’t let that overshadow the film itself, a masterpiece that earned eight Academy Awards (including Best Picture) and remains just as powerful 70 years later. Brando plays Terry Malloy, a longshoreman and former boxer who grows to resent the mobsters who control his local union. And in her film debut, Eva Marie Saint is luminous as Terry’s love interest, who acts as his conscience and inspires him to take a stand and fight back – no matter what the cost.

title: EC: INTOLERANCE
description: Griffith’s immensely influential silent epic intercuts four parallel tales from history (spanning Babylon, Christ’s Judea, Reformation Europe, and turn-of-the-century America) to embroider a moral tapestry on personal, social, and political repression through the ages. The visual poetry is overwhelming, especially in the massed crowd scenes, and the unbridled eroticism of the Babylon harem scenes demonstrates just what Hollywood lost when it later bowed to the Hays Code. While the (partly self-financed) production ruined Griffith financially and baffled audiences with its multiple plots and labyrinthine structure, it has been enormously influential on generations of filmmakers, including Eisenstein, who studied the film closely. title: Predator
description: A team of elite commandos on a secret mission in a Central American jungle come to find themselves hunted by an extraterrestrial warrior.

title: ZORN I + II
description: Mathieu Amalric ZORN I (2010-2016) 2017, 54 min, DCP “The tense, but smiling face of maverick composer legend John Zorn listening to music might just restore your faith in human beauty. Every muscle moves in harmony with sounds and chords, it’s like seeing a soul wandering off into another realm. Mathieu Amalric has been filming this zestful musician for more than 12 years now. They first met when the actor and filmmaker narrated Zorn’s vocal album Shir Hashirim live in Paris. Those familiar with Amalric’s haptic cinema will immediately understand what drew him to Zorn and vice versa. They connect through their constant and obsessive drive for feelings and sensations, their tireless energy devoted to the art, their hunger for life. In the style of a home movie, Amalric accompanies Zorn at concerts, city walks, inside the sound studio or at practice.” –Patrick Holzapfel, VIENNALE Mathieu Amalric ZORN II (2016-2018) 2018, 59 min, DCP “In the second part of his ongoing portrait of the prolific musician, Amalric shows the artist as a social man. Like a sponge, Zorn takes in whatever surrounds him: people (mostly colleagues from the New York Underground scene), dreams, technology, cinema (screening films by Maya Deren or Harry Smith during his performances), places and the emotions evoked by sounds. […] Amalric chooses a more structured approach than in the first part. Text inserts reveal details about the composer’s life and his philosophy. The camera gets more in tune with Zorn’s eruptive movements, as he goes onstage at sold-out concert halls as if he were just discovering the instruments there during an evening stroll. He plays each note as if it was the first or last, and Amalric tries to film him accordingly.” –Patrick Holzapfel, VIENNALE Total running time: ca. 120 min.

description: As the nights draw in, we're very excited to be screening one of the earliest horror masterpieces, The Phantom of the…

title: Fargo
description: Minnesota car salesman Jerry Lundegaard's inept crime falls apart due to his and his henchmen's bungling and the persistent police work of the quite pregnant Marge Gunderson.

title: STAY
description:
STAY tells the story of an artist (The Artist) sentenced to do time in The Curfew Tower, with only a handheld puppet of Elvis (Puppet Elvis) as company. While doing time, The Artist is expected to write the second-best song he has ever written. And this song is for the Ghost of Elvis and is to be performed at The 25 Comeback Special. In reality The Artist is just trying to escape the gathering storm clouds of his inevitable midlife crisis. That, and the reality of being a bad father. The only dialogue in the film is an internal one between The Artist and Puppet Elvis.
STAY is probably the bleakest film you could ever watch. It contains no sex or violence, no kissing or killing, not even any fucking or fighting, or any of those other things some might want to vicariously experience via the medium of film. STAY is a film without HOPE.
The screening at The Nickel is to be the only screening in UK in 2026. Tracey Moberly, Tony Wright & Puppet Elvis will be there for a post screening interrogation. The former Bill Drummond will be there to chair the interrogation. He will also be there to stamp people’s wrists as they enter the building.
WARNING: It is expected that everyone attending this screening will bring their own handheld puppet to watch the film with them – No Puppet, No Entry. Also... Puppet Elvis will be the judge of the post Interrogation Puppet Contest.

title: The Last Picture Show (Director’s Cut)
description: The restored 1992 Director’s Cut version of an American classic! Screening from a 35mm print courtesy of the Sony Archives.

title: Pretty in Pink
description: Put on your dancing shoes and get ready for this all-time teen classic of high school romance, jealousy, resourcefulness, and classism. Molly Ringwald plays Andie, a creative outcast from the wrong side of the tracks who falls for a rich kid (80’s heartthrob Andrew McCarthy) and ends up causing rifts in both their worlds. This sweet and stylish romance features incredible performances from the entire cast including Annie Potts as the fashionista record store owner, Jon Cryer as the Otis Redding lip-syncing obsessed best friend, James Spader as the vilest of the upper crust, and of course Vidiots favorite Harry Dean Stanton as her single father.

title: CYBERCON: SOSUPERSAM & Kyle Ng Live Score to Interstella 5555 (2003)
description: Join us at Brain Dead Studios for an intimate screening of the 2003 animated classic Interstella 5555, featuring a live DJ score performed by SOSUPERSAM and Kyle Ng.
director: Daisuke Nishio, Hirotoshi Rissen, Kazuhisa Takenouchi, Leiji Matsumoto

title: Jealousy Is My Middle Name
description: Park Hae-il plays Lee Won-sang, the hero of Park Chan-ok’s debut feature, in his second big-screen appearance. Lee is a 27-year-old graduate student in literature, finishing up his thesis before he leaves for London. When he starts writing an article for a magazine as a favor, he realizes that the head editor, Han Yun-shik, is the reason his girlfriend left him. Lee’s complicated feelings toward Han, a mixture of admiration and jealousy, brings more confusion when he is introduced to a mesmerizing photographer, Park Sung-yeon, a cool, down-to-earth woman who is also having an affair with Han. Calm on the surface but roiling underneath, the story explores human emotions in a macro lens, excavating endless variables that shape characters while they struggle to stay composed. Park’s undefinable approach to Lee allows his character’s purity and honesty to roam free.

title: The Killing of a Sacred Deer
EC: EGGELING / GRANT / JACOBS & FLEISCHNER
description: Viking Eggeling SYMPHONIE DIAGONALE (1924, 8 min, 35mm, silent) “This early experimental short is one of only two films completed by Swedish-born artist Viking Eggeling, who worked in Paris, Milan, and ultimately Germany. It utilizes paper cutouts, tin foil, and frame-by-frame photography to create a playful show in which cubist, even art deco, circles and lines dance – diagonally – across the black screen.” –FACETS Dwinell Grant COMPOSITION #2 CONTRATHEMIS (1941, 5 min, 16mm, silent) “An attempt to develop visual abstract themes and to counterpoint them in a planned, formal composition.” –Dwinell Grant STOP MOTION TESTS (1942, 3 min, 16mm, silent) A pixillated self-portrait of the filmmaker in his studio. COLOR SEQUENCE (1943, 3 min, 16mm, silent) “Pure solid-color frames which fade, mutate and flicker. A research into color rhythms and perceptual phenomena.” –William Moritz Ken Jacobs & Bob Fleischner BLONDE COBRA 1959-63, 35 min, 16mm-to-35mm blow-up. With Jack Smith. Preserved by Anthology Film Archives with support from The Film Foundation. “BLONDE COBRA is an erratic narrative – no, not really a narrative, it’s only stretched out in time for convenience of delivery. It’s a look in on an exploding life, on a man of imagination suffering pre-fashionable Lower East Side deprivation and consumed with American 1950s, 40s, 30s disgust. Silly, self-pitying, guilt-strictured and yet triumphing – on one level – over the situation with style… enticing us into an absurd moral posture the better to dismiss us with a regal ‘screw off.’” –Ken Jacobs Total running time: ca. 60 min. title: Ken Russell's The Devils: The Director's Cut
description: Censored for over half a century, Ken Russell’s film returns in a landmark director’s cut reconstruction that reveals the full power of his original vision. Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, accused of bewitching a convent of nuns, The Devils lays bare the collusion of church and state through a searing vision of religious persecution, collective hysteria and institutional corruption. The restoration many believed would never happen reaffirms Russell’s incendiary masterpiece as among the most overwhelming and uncompromising achievements in British cinema. Assembled from original camera negative, this 4k restoration is Ken Russell’s 2004 preferred edit. Picture and sound restoration by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color and Warner Bros. Sound.

description: A genre-defying queer epic, dazzlingly constructed and rooted in the legacy of beloved writer Federico García Lorca, La Bola Negra tells the story of three men whose lives are intimately connected across three different eras.  Spain, 1932. A young man awaits to see if he has secured membership of th...

title: ZORN III
description: Mathieu Amalric ZORN III (2018-2022) 2022, 82 min, DCP. With John Zorn and Barbara Hannigan. “Why can’t Mathieu Amalric stop filming John Zorn? It’s because consciously or unconsciously, he understands that he can only get closer to this man if he imitates his restlessness. It’s this Sisyphean tirelessness, the fact that we must imagine Zorn (whose surname translates into German as anger) as a happy man, which is at the core of his art. He makes music in order to be alive. This time, however, Zorn is not the only protagonist, as the Canadian soprano Barbara Hannigan enters the wild world of the composer. Much more straightforward than its previous iterations, the film captures Hannigan’s rehearsals for a performance of Zorn’s song cycle ‘Jumalattaret’ together with pianist Stephen Gosling. The work pushes her vocal capacities to the limit, with the sudden shifts in register, extended high notes and bird-like chirping demanding everything from her.” –Patrick Holzapfel, VIENNALE

title: Bitter Christmas
description: The incomparable Pedro Almodóvar explores the artist’s tenuous relationship with fiction and reality in this film about an actress writing a script inspired by the lives of those around her—which is itself the invention of an Almodóvar-like filmmaker.

title: Cinema Paradiso [Nuovo Cinema Paradiso]
description: A winner of awards across the world including Best Foreign Language Film Oscar, 5 BAFTA Awards including Best Actor, Original Screenplay and Score, the Grand Prize of the Jury at the Cannes Film Festival and many more. Giuseppe Tornatore's loving homage to the cinema tells the story of Salvatore, a successful film director, returning home for the funeral of Alfredo, his old friend who was the projectionist at the local cinema throughout his childhood. Soon memories of his first love affair with the beautiful Elena and all the highs and lows that shaped his life come flooding back, as Salvatore reconnects with the community he left 30 years earlier.

title: CYBERCON: Rubber’s Lover
description: A clandestine group of scientists are conducting brutal experiments on human test subjects in an attempt to unlock psychic powers. An assault of industrial noise, sensory deprivation, and grotesque body horror, Rubber’s Lover (1996) is often considered an unofficial prequel to Fukui’s 964 PINOCCHIO (1991) , expanding on its obsessions with technology, bodily transformation, and the limits of human consciousness.

title: VALERIE AND HER WEEK OF WONDERS
description:
A pair of enchanted earrings offers Valerie protection as her village fills with vampires, corrupt holy men and relatives who will not stay in the same shape. Growing up here means discovering that familiar faces can become the strangest masks.
Jaromil Jireš makes a fairy tale from the collision of innocence, fear and awakening. Jan Curík’s luminous images and Luboš Fišer’s haunting score give the Czech New Wave fantasy the vividness of a half-remembered dream. Beautiful and deeply uncanny, it draws folk horror out of sunlight as readily as shadow.
Presented by Softcore Cinema Club.

title: Stop Making Sense
description: We’re bringing the party back to the big screen to kick off our birthday weekend like rock stars! Join us for one of our favorite cinematic/musical experiences with a reprise of legendary Director Jonathan Demme’s ecstatic musical masterpiece Stop Making Sense. Filmed at the Hollywood Pantages Theater in December 1983, this fascinating piece of musical memorabilia showcases the Talking Heads boundless creativity and showmanship on stage and off. A one-of-a-kind experience, join Vidiots as we revel in 41 years of Vidiots and the 42nd anniversary of this groundbreaking film, newly remastered in a stunning 4K presentation.

title: The Jerk
description: A rags to riches to rags story. In his first feature film starring role, Steve Martin hilariously teams with director Carl Reiner for a crude and quotable comedy classic. When lovable naif Navin R. Johnson (Martin) discovers that he’s adopted, he embarks on a series of madcap misadventures to find himself, while meeting a series of unusual characters along the way and learning what’s truly valuable in life. Bernadette Peters co-stars.

title: Lady Terminator
description: The spirit of an ancient evil queen possesses the body of a young anthropological student, who then goes on a murderous rampage.

title: The Westerner
description: Judge Roy Bean, a self-appointed hanging judge in Vinegarroon, Texas, befriends saddle tramp Cole Harden, who opposes Bean's policy against homesteaders.

title: The Pirates! In an Adventure with Scientists!
description: Another gem from Aardman Productions, adapted by Gideon Defoe from his children's book. The Pirates! In an Adventure with Scientists! follows a crew…

title: Labyrinth - 40th Anniversary
description: Step back into the fantastical world of Jim Henson’s Labyrinth as the beloved classic returns to cinemas for a special 40th-anniversary re-release. Starring David Bowie in one of his most entertaining film performances as the enigmatic Goblin King, this 4K re-issue brings Jim Henson’s dazzling puppetry, imaginative landscapes, and iconic musical moments back to the big screen where they belong. Join the adventure as Sarah (Jennifer Connelly) races against time to navigate the mysterious Labyrinth and rescue her baby brother in this spellbinding cult favourite.

title: Mildred Pierce
description: When Mildred Pierce's wealthy husband leaves her for another woman, Mildred decides to raise her two daughters on her own. Despite Mildred's financial successes in the restaurant business, her oldest daughter, Veda, resents her mother for degrading their social status. In the midst of a police investigation after the death of her second husband, Mildred must evaluate her own freedom and her complicated relationship with her daughter.

title: The Care Bears Movie
description: Join hands and form the circle of friendship with your favorite cuddly toy-turned-cartoon characters. The Care Bears team up with a troubled brother and sister who just moved to a new town to help a neglected young magician’s apprentice whose evil spell book causes sinister things to happen. Who says little furry creatures can’t make a difference?

title: CYBERCON: Blade Runner
description: Presented in the definitive Final Cut featuring additional scenes and remastered sound and image! In decaying Neo-LA, Rick Deckard (Harrison Ford) haunts the streets in search of a fugitive gang of genetically-engineered replicants and encounters a woman who may hold the key to life itself. Through the smog and rain, shine neon-lit existential landscapes of philosophical inquiry: what is humanity? Ridley Scott’s METROPOLIS for the ‘80s is such a spectacle of cinematic craft — from the indelible sci-fi visuals to the Vangelis score to the time-defying special effects, you’d swear its creators were ‘more human than human.’

title: THE PATSY
description: An awkward teenager hopelessly in love with her older sister’s boyfriend tries to make him notice her.

title: An Unfinished Film
description: ★★★★★ “An utterly unique and very important movie about Covid, the crisis that affected all of us.” – The Guardian Director Xiaorui convinces his cast and crew to resume the shooting of a film halted ten years earlier. In January 2020, with the shoot almost complete, rumours regarding an illness begin to circulate. A hairdresser from Wuhan is sent home, while the crew follows the news on their phones. The director has to decide whether to halt the filming once again. Some of the crew and actors manage to leave before the hotel is locked down by security guards and everyone left on set is confined to their hotel rooms. As all communication is reduced to phone screens, Wuhan is locked down. The crew continues to communicate via video calls, whilst the quarantined main actor Jiang Cheng struggles to support his wife who is now locked-down with their month-old baby in Beijing.

title: Imamura: In Search of the Unreturned Soldiers
Ratatouille
description: He’s dying to become a chef. In Pixar’s critically acclaimed blockbuster, a Parisian rat with a passion for cooking finds an unlikely partner for his culinary dreams. Now the improbable human-rodent duo will hilariously turn the restaurant world upside down with their delicious dishes, if their differences don’t derail them first. Winner of the Academy Award for the Best Animated Feature Film of the Year.

title: The Grand Budapest Hotel
description: Writer-director Wes Anderson was inspired by Austrian novelist Stefan Zweig (1881-1942) for his seriocomic and visually dazzling story about a posh resort, its vain concierge (Ralph Fiennes in a peerless comic performance) and a young lobby boy (Tony Revolori). Anderson directed an all-star international cast and brought his distinctive visual sensibilities to his original story (written with Hugo Guinness), set in a fictional European country on the eve of war. The film received nine nominations including Best Picture and won Oscars for Alexandre Desplat’s effervescent score, Milena Canonero’s costume design, the makeup and hair creations of Frances Hannon and Mark Coulier, and the production design of Adam Stockhausen and his set decorator, Anna Pinnock, who transformed a vacant German department store into the eponymous hotel.

title: MAÎTRES ANCIENS – COMÉDIE
description: “Like Reger – the character [Austrian novelist and playwright] Thomas Bernhard placed on a museum bench facing a painting by Tintoretto, an ‘Old Master’ if ever there was one – an actor finds himself alone and thwarted after a notorious virus forces the indefinite closure of theaters. He wanders through an empty auditorium, paces the now-useless backstage areas, and bursts out into a street haunted by masked passersby. Having persuaded a firefighter to keep watch over him and his explosives, he pours out – to the guard and the surrounding silence alike – his loathing for, among other things, Heideggerians, a lack of punctuality, people who admire rather than respect, and the State’s appropriation of children. At the intersection of cinema and theater, despair and the will to survive, 1980s Austria and 2020s France, Bernhard’s text takes on a new resonance: ‘And as for culture in this country, your stomach exists only to turn.’” –Marie Hermann, FIDMarseille Preceded by: Mathieu Amalric C’EST PRESQUE AU BOUT DU MONDE (2015, 16 min, digital. With Barbara Hannigan.) “In C’EST PRESQUE AU BOUT DU MONDE, I explore a mystery that fascinates me: where do these inhuman voices come from? From where in the body does the unsettling anomaly of singing originate?” –Mathieu Amalric Total running time: ca. 100 min.

title: Highlander
description: After inexplicably surviving a mortal wound during a clan battle in the Scottish Highlands in 1536, Connor MacLeod (Christopher Lambert) is accused of witchcraft and banished from his village. Years later, he meets Ramirez (Sean Connery), a swordsman who teaches MacLeod the truth about himself: he belongs to an immortal race who can only die when the head is cut from the body. MacLeod fights his way through the centuries until the time of The Gathering, when the few immortals who have survived the ages will come together to fight until just one remains. In 1980s New York City the final fight is about to begin and, in the end, there can be only one...

title: MYSTERY DOJO: SURPRISE KUNG FU MATINEES
description:
Enter the 36 Chambers of Grindhouse Cinema, with these Sunday mystery martial-arts matinees that harken back to the glory days of 42nd Street.
Expect deep-cut chopsocky plucked from the 70s and 80s screening on both digital and VHS - with bone-crushing bashers from the genre that mixed Chinese folklore and fantasy, spaghetti westerns, melodrama, Japanese samurai films and American genre cinema into an electrifying combo that inspired both the future of action films - and hip hop.
These Kung Fu flicks became an international sensation in the 1970s, particularly at the Grindhouse cinemas that proliferated in impoverished inner-cities. Here were movies in which working-class heroes stood up to oppression, speaking loud and clear to the marginalised underclasses around the world.
Bring the ruckus!

title: CYBERCON: Blade Runner 2049
description: Denis Villeneuve reinvents the world of BLADE RUNNER as a dystopian wasteland thirty years after the events of the first film. Ryan Gosling stars as K, a new Blade Runner whose investigation plunges him into the depths of a crumbling society as he hunts the only man who can save us: Harrison Ford’s Rick Deckard. Thanks in part to the mind-blowing images created by cinematographer Roger Deakins, BLADE RUNNER 2049 defies every expectation for Hollywood sequels and offers an alternative: a staggering, cerebral, self-possessed work which stands alone in its accomplishments.

title: Paisàn
description: The second installment in his WWII trilogy and one of Rossellini’s favorites of his films, the episodic Paisàn is another depiction of the tribulations of the Italians under German occupation. Its title translates to “fellow countryman” and takes a broader view of Italy than his previous Rome, Open City (1945) , moving the action outside the capital to focus on the interactions between American armed forces and the country residents impacted by conflict. Future Italian auteur Federico Fellini co-wrote the screenplay, which came together on the fly, with dialogue of each sequence written just before it was filmed.
director: Roberto Rossellini PRODUCED BY: Rod E. Geiger, Roberto Rossellini

title: Imamura: Pirates of Bubuan + Outlaw-Matsu Returns Home
Imitation of Life (1959) on 35mm
description: Lana Turner, Juanita Moore, and Sandra Dee light up the screen in this Douglas Sirk tearjerking melodrama of single mothers and racial identity. The second screen adaptation of Fannie Hurst’s incendiery novel, Douglas Sirk ratchets up the drama, the color, and the story of this powerful tale of women’s resilience from its predecessor with Claudette Colbert. Lora Meredith (suspected murderess Lana Turner), a white single mother who dreams of being on Broadway, takes in a black widow Annie (Juanita Moore) and her mixed race daughter (Susan Kohner) to live with her and her daughter (Sandra Dee). Together, the women deal with the maelstrom of life’s ups and downs including the toll of success and Annie’s daughter desperately trying to erase her racial identity and come off as white. With incredible female characters and actors, that gorgeous Sirkian Technicolor touch, and a story of race that was decades ahead of its time, this classic melodrama is ready to pull you in and give you all the feels!

description: Misa suffers from severe PMS, which can unravel her otherwise demure disposition with violent disregard for personal or professional company. Finally holding down a job assembling science kits for kids, she befriends Takatoshi, a withdrawn colleague prone to debilitating panic attacks.

EC: UNE SIMPLE HISTOIRE
description: “Based on a true incident, the film chronicles the wanderings of a woman and child looking for work and lodging in Paris. This is the only plot, and Hanoun has little interest in embellishing it with background and motivation: he never even makes it clear, for example, whether the woman is the child’s mother, guardian or companion. UNE SIMPLE HISTOIRE is, more than a narrative, a formal stylistic exercise so rigorously disciplined and understated that it makes the visual asceticism of Robert Bresson seem almost Fellini-esque by comparison.” –TIME CLICK HERE TO BOOK TICKETS NOW!

description: An enduring masterpiece of cinema starring Vanessa Redgrave and Oliver Reed, KEN RUSSELL'S THE DEVILS is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption and a defining work of art from seminal filmmaker Ken Russell presented in newly restored 4K. Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain...

title: Angel's Egg
description: In an underwater city, a young girl takes care of a large egg she holds carefully in her arms. A boy with a gun arrives in search of a bird he saw in his dream. At first, it seems as if feelings of sympathy are developing between the two. Forty years after the film’s original release, Anime Limited is proud to present an all-new 4K restoration of the film, supervised by director Mamoru Oshii, in cinemas nationwide for the very first time. The film is a creative collaboration between acclaimed director Mamoru Oshii (Ghost in the Shell), who wrote and directed the feature, and revered artist Yoshitaka Amano (Final Fantasy, Vampire Hunter D). The film beautifully intertwines Oshii’s thematic reflections on philosophy and theology with Amano’s distinctive ink painting style, culminating in an arrestingly beautiful hand-drawn allegorical fantasy.

title: In a Lonely Place
description: A screenwriter with a violent temper is a murder suspect until his lovely neighbor clears him. However, she soon starts to have her doubts.

title: ZORN I + II
description: Mathieu Amalric ZORN I (2010-2016) 2017, 54 min, DCP “The tense, but smiling face of maverick composer legend John Zorn listening to music might just restore your faith in human beauty. Every muscle moves in harmony with sounds and chords, it’s like seeing a soul wandering off into another realm. Mathieu Amalric has been filming this zestful musician for more than 12 years now. They first met when the actor and filmmaker narrated Zorn’s vocal album Shir Hashirim live in Paris. Those familiar with Amalric’s haptic cinema will immediately understand what drew him to Zorn and vice versa. They connect through their constant and obsessive drive for feelings and sensations, their tireless energy devoted to the art, their hunger for life. In the style of a home movie, Amalric accompanies Zorn at concerts, city walks, inside the sound studio or at practice.” –Patrick Holzapfel, VIENNALE Mathieu Amalric ZORN II (2016-2018) 2018, 59 min, DCP “In the second part of his ongoing portrait of the prolific musician, Amalric shows the artist as a social man. Like a sponge, Zorn takes in whatever surrounds him: people (mostly colleagues from the New York Underground scene), dreams, technology, cinema (screening films by Maya Deren or Harry Smith during his performances), places and the emotions evoked by sounds. […] Amalric chooses a more structured approach than in the first part. Text inserts reveal details about the composer’s life and his philosophy. The camera gets more in tune with Zorn’s eruptive movements, as he goes onstage at sold-out concert halls as if he were just discovering the instruments there during an evening stroll. He plays each note as if it was the first or last, and Amalric tries to film him accordingly.” –Patrick Holzapfel, VIENNALE Total running time: ca. 120 min.

title: DONT LOOK BACK + BOB DYLAN CONCERT FOOTAGE
description:
Dylan on stage is only half the story. In hotel rooms, backstage corridors and combative interviews during his 1965 British tour, he is inventing—and resisting—the public figure everyone wants him to become.
D. A. Pennebaker’s camera catches the wit, the cruelty, the boredom and the sudden electricity without a narrator telling us what to think. From the cue cards of “Subterranean Homesick Blues” to performances alive with concentration, this landmark music documentary puts you in the room at the moment a musician becomes an enigma.
Presented with a programme of Bob Dylan concert footage.

title: LPFF 2026: Partition + The Flowers Stand Silently, Witnessing + ScreenTalk
EC: JEROME HILL
description: These 35mm prints are the result of a preservation project undertaken by the Museum of Modern Art. DEATH IN THE FORENOON (1934/66, 2 min, 35mm) CANARIES (1969, 4 min, 35mm) & FILM PORTRAIT (1971, 81 min, 35mm) “FILM PORTRAIT is an autobiography in the sense that it deals explicitly with Jerome’s most personal life’s relationship to film. It draws on film clips taken in his childhood and his whole childhood involvement in art and life. It comes closest to any kind of filmic answer to Proust. […] FILM PORTRAIT is, I believe, the only direct autobiography we have in film. There is Jonas Mekas’s WALDEN, which is diary but not autobiography in a strict sense. We have Cocteau’s BLOOD OF A POET, ORPHEUS, and TESTAMENT OF ORPHEUS. One could say that this last is autobiographical, but it is also allusive and poetic; whereas Jerome’s FILM PORTRAIT is a very straight attempt to present autobiography on film. Of course, subsequently, James Broughton’s TESTAMENT and my own SINCERITY & DUPLICITY series of autobiographical films were very much inspired by Jerome’s FILM PORTRAIT as well as by Jonas’s WALDEN. […] Jerome Hill’s films are great because they are poised on wit and achieve a balance – a gentle, intentional, particularly American balance.” –Stan Brakhage, FILM AT WIT’S END Total running time: ca. 90 min. title: The Odyssey
description: Odysseus, the legendary King of Ithaca, embarks on a long and perilous journey home following the Trojan War. Throughout his voyage, he is forced to confront the whims of gods, mythological monsters, and trials that stretch both his cunning and his humanity to the breaking point.

title: Germany Year Zero
description: Released the same year the first theories of neo-realism were published in film magazines Esprit, La Revue du Cinéma , and Bianco e Nero by acclaimed critics, including André Bazin, Germany Year Zero rounds out Rossellini’s WWII trilogy and brings a continental scope to the devastating impact of Hitler’s final solution. By centering the story on a young boy navigating the devastating implications of war, Rossellini accentuates the stark contrast between generations. A major influence on François Truffaut’s The 400 Blows (1959) and cast with people the director found by exploring the four zones of Berlin, Germany Year Zero would, Rossellini hoped, “reproduce the truth exactly as the camera saw it for that audience through the entire world which has a heart capable of love and a brain capable of thought.”
