title: FINAL FLESH
description:
A family awaits the end of the world. Four fetish-video companies are separately commissioned to film parts of the same absurd script. They must follow the words; almost everything else is up to them.
The resulting collision is unlike anything a conventional production could plan: mismatched rooms, matter-of-fact performances and apocalyptic non sequiturs delivered with total commitment. Written by Vernon Chatman, FINAL FLESH turns commissioned fantasy into a bizarre experiment in authorship. A Dada family sitcom transmitted from a civilisation that has received all the wrong instructions.

description: A jaw-dropping deep cut of Satanic Cinema, Juan López Moctezuma’s Alucarda is treasure of Mexican Horror dying to be rediscovered at large. School girls cavorting with Baphomet and dabbling in sapphic secrets, self-flagelatting nuns wrapped in bloody gauze, this woefully underseen masterpiece is a whole new level of horror, hungry for new eyes to witness its exquisite strangeness. A young girl’s arrival at a convent after the death of her parents marks the beginning of a series of events that unleash an evil presence on the girl and her mysterious new friend, an enigmatic figure known as Alucarda. Demonic possession, Satan worship, and vampirism follows. A protege of Alejandro Jodorowski, Moctezuma creates a nightmarish world that transcends beyond genre. Don’t miss this rare chance to see this unforgettable experience on our big screen!

title: It's Such a Beautiful Day
description: Originally released as three short films over the course of six years, the picture was captured entirely in-camera on a 35mm rostrum animation stand. Built in the 1940s and used by Hertzfeldt on all of his animated films since 1999, it was one of the last surviving cameras of its kind still operating in the world, indispensable in creating the story's unique images and visual effects. IT'S SUCH A BEAUTIFUL DAY painstakingly blended traditional hand-drawn animation and experimental optical effects with new digital hybrids, printed out one frame at a time, and placed under the camera. The film's signature "split screen" effects were achieved by photographing the animation through small holes that were positioned just beneath the camera lens. One area of the film frame would be individually photographed, the film was then rewound, another section of the frame would be exposed through a different hole, and the process repeated until all elements of a scene were composited together. Towards the end of production, the old camera's motor began to fail and could no longer advance the film properly, riddling the final reels with unintentional light leaks. In 2012, the three completed short films about a man named Bill were seamlessly combined to create a new feature film. Upon its original release, IT'S SUCH A BEAUTIFUL DAY was named by many critics as one of the best films of the year. The L.A. Film Critics Association named it runner-up for “Best Animated Film.”In 2014, Time Out New York ranked IT'S SUCH A BEAUTIFUL DAY #16 on its list of the “100 Best Animated Movies Ever Made.”In 2016, The Film Stage's critics ranked the film #1 on their list of “The 50 Best Animated Films of the 21st Century Thus Far.”In 2019, The Wrap named IT'S SUCH A BEAUTIFUL DAY the #1 “Best Animated Film of the 2010s.”The same year, Vulture's film critics ranked it #12 on their overall list of the “Best Movies of the Decade.”In 2021, IGN's Cinefix placed it #1 on their “Top 10 Animated Films of All Time” list. IT'S SUCH A BEAUTIFUL DAY is currently ranked #103 on Letterboxd’s official list of the Top 500 highest-rated narrative feature films of all time.

title: THE HEROIC TRIO
description:
Babies are vanishing into an underground empire. A masked vigilante, a mercenary and an invisible assassin are drawn into the same fight—and towards the histories that connect them. The city’s future depends on an alliance none of them planned.
Michelle Yeoh, Anita Mui and Maggie Cheung make an unbeatable triangle in Johnnie To’s exhilarating genre collision. Ching Siu-tung’s action sends bodies and blades flying through a world of Gothic monsters, superhero masks and motorcycle stunts. Hong Kong cinema’s imagination running gloriously beyond the speed limit.

title: Repo Man
description: A down and out young punk gets a job working with a seasoned repo man, but what awaits him in his new career is a series of outlandish adventures revolving around aliens, the CIA, and a most wanted ’64 Chevy.

title: ZORN III
description: Mathieu Amalric ZORN III (2018-2022) 2022, 82 min, DCP. With John Zorn and Barbara Hannigan. “Why can’t Mathieu Amalric stop filming John Zorn? It’s because consciously or unconsciously, he understands that he can only get closer to this man if he imitates his restlessness. It’s this Sisyphean tirelessness, the fact that we must imagine Zorn (whose surname translates into German as anger) as a happy man, which is at the core of his art. He makes music in order to be alive. This time, however, Zorn is not the only protagonist, as the Canadian soprano Barbara Hannigan enters the wild world of the composer. Much more straightforward than its previous iterations, the film captures Hannigan’s rehearsals for a performance of Zorn’s song cycle ‘Jumalattaret’ together with pianist Stephen Gosling. The work pushes her vocal capacities to the limit, with the sudden shifts in register, extended high notes and bird-like chirping demanding everything from her.” –Patrick Holzapfel, VIENNALE

title: Ken Russell's The Devils: The Director's Cut
description: Censored for over half a century, Ken Russell’s film returns in a landmark director’s cut reconstruction that reveals the full power of his original vision. Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, accused of bewitching a convent of nuns, The Devils lays bare the collusion of church and state through a searing vision of religious persecution, collective hysteria and institutional corruption. The restoration many believed would never happen reaffirms Russell’s incendiary masterpiece as among the most overwhelming and uncompromising achievements in British cinema. Assembled from original camera negative, this 4k restoration is Ken Russell’s 2004 preferred edit. Picture and sound restoration by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color and Warner Bros. Sound.

title: INVESTIGATION OF A CITIZEN ABOVE SUSPICION
description:
A police chief murders his mistress and leaves evidence pointing directly at himself. He is testing a theory: that an institution built to enforce the law will refuse to recognise the guilt of the man who embodies it.
Gian Maria Volonté is magnificent—swaggering, childish, terrifying—in Elio Petri’s acid political satire. Ennio Morricone’s sly, lurching score helps make authority look both ridiculous and deadly. A murder investigation turned inside out, where the suspense lies in how far power can go before anyone dares to name what is in front of them.

title: RRR
description: Can’t stop! Won’t Stop! The biggest film of the decade has become a Vidiots tradition! RRR is an exhilarating, action-packed spectacular, starring two of India’s biggest superstars, N.T Rama Rao Jr., aka Jr NTR and Ram Charan. Set in the 1920s before their fight for India’s independence began, RRR imagines a fictional meeting between two real-life freedom fighters who helped lead India’s fight for independence from the British Raj.

title: Stardust: A Story of Love and Architecture
description: It was one of the great, untold love stories of the 20th century. For fifty years, Robert Venturi and Denise Scott Brown shared a life of profound tenderness, sharp wit, and creative joy. They also sparked a revolution in architecture, challenging the rigid modernism of the era with their embrace of complexity, symbolism, and the lessons of the everyday landscape.

title: Hot Water (Silent with Live Music Score)
description: A hilarious domestic-life comedy begins with Harold with an armful of packages and a live turkey on a streetcar, followed by a disastrous spin in his new car with his in-laws, and ending with haunted house-type thrills provoked by his mother-in-law (Josephine Cromwell).

From boundary-pushing directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim comes You Can See Everything .

title: The Flowers of St. Francis
description: Inspired by the writings of Saint Francis of Assisi and the hagiographic texts about his loyal follower Brother Juniper, The Flowers of St. Francis is composed of simple vignettes that beautifully illustrate the humane life lessons of the People’s Saint. Using only one professional actor, with the rest of the cast comprised of friars from the Franciscan monastery, Rossellini’s film brings into focus, as he put it in 1950, “the merrier aspect of the Franciscan experience, the playfulness, the ‘perfect delight,’ the freedom that the spirit finds in poverty, and in absolute detachment from material things.”

description: Representing attempts at group portraiture, the films in this program meditate on the diversity of human physiognomies – and the diversity of personalities that they manifest – and in some cases suggest filmic catalogues or collections of portraits. title: MAÎTRES ANCIENS – COMÉDIE
description: “Like Reger – the character [Austrian novelist and playwright] Thomas Bernhard placed on a museum bench facing a painting by Tintoretto, an ‘Old Master’ if ever there was one – an actor finds himself alone and thwarted after a notorious virus forces the indefinite closure of theaters. He wanders through an empty auditorium, paces the now-useless backstage areas, and bursts out into a street haunted by masked passersby. Having persuaded a firefighter to keep watch over him and his explosives, he pours out – to the guard and the surrounding silence alike – his loathing for, among other things, Heideggerians, a lack of punctuality, people who admire rather than respect, and the State’s appropriation of children. At the intersection of cinema and theater, despair and the will to survive, 1980s Austria and 2020s France, Bernhard’s text takes on a new resonance: ‘And as for culture in this country, your stomach exists only to turn.’” –Marie Hermann, FIDMarseille Preceded by: Mathieu Amalric C’EST PRESQUE AU BOUT DU MONDE (2015, 16 min, digital. Professor Brand (Michael Caine), a brilliant NASA physicist, is working on plans to save mankind by transporting Earth's population to a new home via a wormhole. But first, Brand must send former NASA pilot Cooper (Matthew McConaughey) and a team of researchers through the wormhole and across the galaxy to find out which of three planets could be mankind's new home.

title: Dead Poets Society
description: A new English teacher, John Keating (Robin Williams), is introduced to an all-boys preparatory school that is known for its ancient traditions and high standards. He uses unorthodox methods to reach out to his students, who face enormous pressures from their parents and the school. With Keating's help, students Neil Perry (Robert Sean Leonard), Todd Anderson (Ethan Hawke) and others learn to break out of their shells, pursue their dreams and seize the day.

title: COP (VHS)
description:
Lloyd Hopkins sees connections nobody else can see. The trouble is that the LAPD detective also sees rules as somebody else’s problem. Hunting a killer, he pushes his methods, marriage and already threadbare ethics towards breaking point.
James Woods brings terrifying conviction to James B. Harris’s stripped-down adaptation of James Ellroy’s BLOOD ON THE MOON. The case matters, but so does the unsettling pleasure Hopkins takes in being right. A cold, abrasive Los Angeles thriller in which detective brilliance and institutional brutality become dangerously difficult to separate.
Presented on VHS.

description: An entire civilisation must confront its destiny in alternative-animation pioneer René Laloux's final feature, a cult classic of mind-bending science fiction. In a distant world, a merciless army of automata attacks Gandahar, turning its peace-loving people to stone. Hoping to discover the source of these Men of Metal, a council of matriarchs enlists the brave yet inexperienced warrior Sylvain (Pierre-Marie Escourro), who, while journeying through his planet's outer regions, teams up with the Deformed, a race cast out from Gandahar after failed science experiments rendered them mutants. Soon, Sylvain learns that a gargantuan brain called Metamorphis (Georges Wilson) is responsible for his utopian society's strife and—together with the beautiful Airelle (Catherine Chevallier)—travels through time to defeat him, in the process risking their lives and Gandahar's very existence. Featuring stunningly surreal creatures and wondrously bizarre environments designed by renowned comic-book artist Caza, Gandahar is a visceral, visionary head-trip in which animation opens a gateway to the furthest reaches of the imagination.

description: Mr. Watanabe suddenly finds that he has terminal cancer. He vows to make his final days meaningful. His attempts to communicate his anguish to his son and daughter-in-law lead only to heartbreak. Finally, inspired by an unselfish co-worker, he turns his efforts to bringing happiness to others by building a playground in a dreary slum neighborhood. When the park is finally completed, he is able to face death with peaceful acceptance.

description: Born into a family business of race cars, Speed Racer (Emile Hirsch) is one of the track's hot stars. Sitting at the wheel of his Mach 5, he consistently deflates the competition. When Speed turns down an offer from the head of Royalton Industries, he uncovers a secret. Powerful moguls fix the races to boost profits. Hoping to beat the executive, Speed enters the same arduous cross-country race that killed his brother.

title: Rio Film Feminists: DAISIES
description: To celebrate the 60th anniversary of Vera Chytilová’s wildly anarchic feminist classic Daisies, Rio Film Feminists present a special screening of this dazzling Czech New Wave landmark film.  DAISIES follows Marie and Marie who have decided that if the world is rotten, they might as well be rotten to...

title: ERASERHEAD (ON 16MM)
description:
Henry Spencer has a room, a girlfriend and a newborn baby. None of them offers much comfort. Outside, machinery groans; inside, the infant cries and a woman in the radiator promises that everything will be fine.
David Lynch’s handmade first feature turns the terrors of parenthood, sex and responsibility into an entirely private industrial universe. Stark monochrome images and Alan Splet’s enveloping sound make the nightmare physical. Horrifying, oddly tender and very funny in places you may not expect, ERASERHEAD remains an experience that resists explanation and rewards surrender.
Introduced by Dominic Hicks and presented on 16mm with a reel intermission and programme notes.

title: HOLD ME TIGHT / SERRE MOI FORT
description: With Vicky Krieps, Arieh Worthalter, Anne-Sophie Bowen-Chatet, and Sacha Ardilly. “Propelled by a fierce, tour-de-force performance by Vicky Krieps, who is fast becoming one of the most sought-after actors on the international scene, HOLD ME TIGHT is an ingenious memory piece exploring the grief of separation and the paradoxical comforts and claustrophobia of the domestic home. As Clarisse flees her family at daybreak and hits the open road, leaving her husband and two children behind, the film shuttles between time and space, becoming a mental landscape whose contours are gradually revealed like fleeting moments of reminiscence – those that ultimately make up a life. With its beguiling, puzzle-piece structure that builds to a shattering denouement, HOLD ME TIGHT powerfully keeps its audience in a state of hypnotic reverie as we share in the protagonist’s profound sense of disorientation, the sort of disembodied surrealism that uncertainty can unleash. Yet Krieps gives a surprisingly earth-bound, visceral performance as a woman negotiating a new path for herself, all while trying to stay close to those she loves and attempting to make sense of it all.” –Andréa Picard, TIFF

title: Cinematic Void Presents FELLINI'S CASANOVA
description: The incomparable Federico Fellini directs the visually stunning portrait of Casanova, the infamous Italian womanizer, adventurer, author and libertine. In a remarkable performance, Donald Sutherland portrays the great seducer not as an amorous anomaly, but an everyday man living in extraordinary times. Featuring dazzling European settings (although it was filmed entirely in Rome), an unforgettable musical score and Academy Award-winning costumes, Fellini’s Casanova is a cinematic experience to fall in love with.

title: Doctor Who: The Satan Pit
description: Celebrate Doctor Who Day with an exclusive big-screen event marking 20 years of the Tenth Doctor and Rose Tyler. For the first time ever in cinemas, the acclaimed two-part adventure The Impossible Planet and The Satan Pit have been specially re-edited into a single movie-length presentation, created exclusively for theatrical audiences. Join the Doctor (David Tennant) and Rose (Billie Piper) as they travel to Sanctuary Base 6, a remote outpost perched on a planet orbiting a black hole. When an ancient force awakens beneath the surface, the crew find themselves trapped in a battle against an evil older than time itself. This special Doctor Who Day screening also includes exclusive bonus material, featuring previously unseen content and a brand-new interview with a special guest, reflecting on the making of one of the most celebrated stories of the modern era – from encounters with the Ood to facing the terrifying Beast, alongside behind-the-scenes memories from the set.

title: The Host
description: 20th Anniversary! New 4K Restoration plus a bonus pre-recorded conversation with Bong Joon-ho!

title: Yi Yi
description: The extraordinary, internationally embraced Yi Yi (A One and a Two . . .), directed by the late Taiwanese master Edward Yang, follows a middle-class family in Taipei over the course of one year, beginning with a wedding and ending with a funeral. Whether chronicling middle-age father NJ’s tentative flirtations with an old flame or precocious young son Yang-Yang’s attempts at capturing reality with his beloved camera, the filmmaker deftly imbues every gorgeous frame with a compassionate clarity. Warm, sprawling, and dazzling, this intimate epic is one of the undisputed masterworks of the new century. 4K digital restoration carried out by Pony Canyon Inc., with analog and digital processes provided by Imagica Entertainment Media Services, Inc.

title: The Machine That Kills Bad People
description: One of Roberto Rossellini's most singular and unheralded works, this potent blend of neorealism and fantasy is an idiosyncratic, lighthearted fable. In a fishing village on the Amalfi Coast, a stranger claiming to be a saint bestows a photographer’s camera with the power to kill bad people by photographing existing pictures of them. Initially, the photographer uses his newfound weapon to eliminate abusers of power. But before long, he succumbs to the very same amoral selfishness he once claimed to despise. When asked in a 1970 interview whether the film was about filmmaking, Rossellini replied, "It's rather a game, an attempt at comedy, [...] an isolated experiment."
director: Roberto Rossellini PRODUCED BY: Salvo D’Angelo

title: Paris, Texas
description: A disheveled man who wanders out of the desert, Travis Henderson (Harry Dean Stanton) seems to have no idea who he is. When a stranger manages to contact his brother, Walt (Dean Stockwell), Travis is awkwardly reunited with his sibling. Travis has been missing for years, and his presence unsettles Walt and his family, which also includes Travis's own son, Hunter (Hunter Carson). Soon Travis must confront his wife, Jane (Nastassja Kinski), and try to put his life back together.

title: CINÉMATON, PROGRAM 1
description: Gérard Courant CINÉMATON 1978-85, ca. 80 min selection, Super-8mm-or-video-to-digital “Since the 7th of February, 1978, I have made portraits on film of artistic and cultural personalities that I call CINÉMATON. There are ten rules for the cinematon, ten commandments that must not be deviated from: 1) A camera on a tripod; 2) A camera that does not move; 3) A close-up of a face; 4) No sound; 5) No change in focal length; 6) No change in the framing; 7) Running-time of 3 minutes and 25 seconds; 8) One take only; 9) No cutting during the shooting and no editing; 10) The person that is being filmed can do whatever he/she wants. The aims of the CINÉMATON are multiple: the basic aim is to constitute an archive on art and especially on the film, theater, and entertainment scenes in those moments when the subject that is being filmed proposes a great moment of truth about herself or himself. Each CINÉMATON is preceded by three introductory title cards with the chronological number of the shooting of the portrait, the name of the person that is being filmed, his or her nationality, his profession, the date, hour, and place of the shooting. CINÉMATON has theoretically no end.” –Gérard Courant N°31 BABETTE MANGOLTE (1978) N°44 MICHAEL SNOW (1978) N°95 YVONNE RAINER (1980) N°104 ULRIKE OTTINGER (1981) N°105 DEREK JARMAN (1981) N°106 JEAN-LUC GODARD (1981) N°114 MRINAL SEN (1981) N°120 PAUL SHARITS (1981) N°121 STEVE DWOSKIN (1981) N°122 ROBERT KRAMER (1981) N°124 LIONEL ROGOSIN (1981) N°228 RAOUL RUIZ (1982) N°236 MAURICE PIALAT (1982) N°271 GARY INDIANA (1983) N°295 PETER KUBELKA (1983) N°342 JEAN-MARIE STRAUB (1984) N°343 DANIÈLE HUILLET (1984) N°441 JULIET BERTO (1984) N°509 TINA AUMONT (1985) N°573 ALEXANDER KLUGE (1985)

title: DIABOLIQUE (16MM)
description:
A cruel headmaster has made enemies of both his wife and his mistress. Together they devise the perfect murder. Then the body disappears—and the most frightening question becomes whether their victim is really dead.
Henri-Georges Clouzot turns damp corridors, a neglected swimming pool and two extraordinary performances into an almost unbearable machine of suspicion. Simone Signoret’s steel meets Véra Clouzot’s mounting terror in a thriller that understands how guilt makes every ordinary sound threatening. Go in knowing as little as possible; leave the secrets in the cinema.
Presented on 16mm with a reel intermission.

title: BARBARA
description: With Jeanne Balibar, Mathieu Amalric, Vincent Peirani, Aurore Clement, and Grégoire Colin. Amalric’s seventh feature-length film as a director is both a heartfelt tribute to the legendary chanteuse Barbara (1930-97), and a vehicle for another peerlessly talented French luminary, the actress and singer Jeanne Balibar. Amalric’s films are remarkable for their intuitive freedom, and their emphasis on emotional textures and states of feeling rather than on straightforward narrative construction or easily grasped meanings. BARBARA is a case in point: eschewing anything like a coherent, birth-to-death account of the events of her life, the film instead orchestrates fragments of the singer’s life and performances into a free and quasi-abstract meditation on Barbara’s identity and cultural presence. And by casting Balibar not as Barbara per se but more self-referentially as an actress making a film-within-the-film about the singer, his film becomes an even broader investigation into the concept of biographical filmmaking, representation, and identity. An experimental biopic in the tradition of Stanley Kwan’s CENTER STAGE, Peter Watkins’s EDVARD MUNCH, and Paul Leduc’s FRIDA, it features a typically riveting, charismatic performance from Balibar.

title: The Fly (1986)
description: When scientist Seth Brundle completes his teleportation device, he decides to test its abilities on himself. Unbeknownst to him, a housefly slips in during the process, leading to a merger of man and insect. Initially, Brundle appears to have undergone a successful teleportation, but the fly's cells begin to take over his body. As he becomes increasingly fly-like, Brundle's girlfriend is horrified as the person she once loved deteriorates into a monster.

title: Peeping Tom
description: Loner Mark Lewis works at a film studio during the day and, at night, takes racy photographs of women. Also he's making a documentary on fear, which involves recording the reactions of victims as he murders them. He befriends Helen, the daughter of the family living in the apartment below his, and he tells her vaguely about the movie he is making.

title: Goodfellas
description: Young Henry Hill (Ray Liotta), with his friends Jimmy (Robert De Niro) and Tommy (Joe Pesci), grows up in the mob and works very hard to advance himself through the ranks. He enjoys his life of money and luxury, but is oblivious to the horror that he causes. A drug addiction and a few mistakes ultimately unravel his climb to the top. Based on the book "Wiseguy" by Nicholas Pileggi.

title: There Will Be Blood
description: Ruthless silver miner, turned oil prospector, Daniel Plainview moves to oil-rich California. Using his adopted son HW to project a trustworthy, family-man image, Plainview cons local landowners into selling him their valuable properties for a pittance. However, local preacher Eli Sunday suspects Plainviews motives and intentions, starting a slow-burning feud that threatens both their lives.

title: Ken Russell's The Devils: The Director's Cut
description: Censored for over half a century, Ken Russell’s film returns in a landmark director’s cut reconstruction that reveals the full power of his original vision. Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, accused of bewitching a convent of nuns, The Devils lays bare the collusion of church and state through a searing vision of religious persecution, collective hysteria and institutional corruption. The restoration many believed would never happen reaffirms Russell’s incendiary masterpiece as among the most overwhelming and uncompromising achievements in British cinema. Assembled from original camera negative, this 4k restoration is Ken Russell’s 2004 preferred edit. Picture and sound restoration by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color and Warner Bros. Sound.

title: Thief
description: A highly skilled jewel thief, Frank (James Caan) longs to leave his dangerous trade and settle down with his girlfriend, Jessie (Tuesday Weld). Eager to make one last big score in order to begin living a legitimate life, Frank reluctantly associates with Leo (Robert Prosky), a powerful gangster. Unfortunately for Frank, Leo wants to keep him in his employ, resulting in a tense showdown when he finally tries to give up his criminal activities once and for all.

title: LOST FUTURES: Wax, Or the Discovery of Television Among the Bees
description: “Computer programmer/beekeeper Jacob gets a “television” implanted in his brain by a race of telekinetic bees, which causes him to experience severe hallucinations.” So goes the setup for David Blair’s unclassifiable 1991 work Wax, Or the Discovery of Television Among the Bees , but this description only encapsulates a portion of the hyper-digressive, decidedly peculiar contents of this singular, visually arresting film. Part cyberpunk essay, part surrealist faux documentary, and part prismatically polygonal video art experiment, the film, which holds the unusual accolade of becoming, in May 1993 and at two frames-per-second, the first film ever streamed over the internet, is unlike much else made before or since. A film ahead of, and outside of, its own time, across its discursive and colourful journey, it muses on topics including space and time travel, science fiction, myth-making, bees, war, and violence, and, through its dense and abstract aesthetics, offers an acute audiovisual expression of the era of post-internet information overload it presages. Having become a cult film on account of its idiosyncratic and psychedelic qualities and its William S. Burroughs cameo, Wax has an enthusiastic online fanbase with which its still active, still innovating filmmaker maintains an active dialogue . Showing on the occasion of its thirty-fifth anniversary, in reference to the method by which the filmmaker originally self-distributed the film on homemade videotapes, Wax will be screened from a VHS copy created especially for the screening. Several bootlegs will be on sale at the event.

title: ZORN I + II
description: Mathieu Amalric ZORN I (2010-2016) 2017, 54 min, DCP “The tense, but smiling face of maverick composer legend John Zorn listening to music might just restore your faith in human beauty. Every muscle moves in harmony with sounds and chords, it’s like seeing a soul wandering off into another realm. Mathieu Amalric has been filming this zestful musician for more than 12 years now. They first met when the actor and filmmaker narrated Zorn’s vocal album Shir Hashirim live in Paris. Those familiar with Amalric’s haptic cinema will immediately understand what drew him to Zorn and vice versa. They connect through their constant and obsessive drive for feelings and sensations, their tireless energy devoted to the art, their hunger for life. In the style of a home movie, Amalric accompanies Zorn at concerts, city walks, inside the sound studio or at practice.” –Patrick Holzapfel, VIENNALE Mathieu Amalric ZORN II (2016-2018) 2018, 59 min, DCP “In the second part of his ongoing portrait of the prolific musician, Amalric shows the artist as a social man. Like a sponge, Zorn takes in whatever surrounds him: people (mostly colleagues from the New York Underground scene), dreams, technology, cinema (screening films by Maya Deren or Harry Smith during his performances), places and the emotions evoked by sounds. […] Amalric chooses a more structured approach than in the first part. Text inserts reveal details about the composer’s life and his philosophy. The camera gets more in tune with Zorn’s eruptive movements, as he goes onstage at sold-out concert halls as if he were just discovering the instruments there during an evening stroll. He plays each note as if it was the first or last, and Amalric tries to film him accordingly.” –Patrick Holzapfel, VIENNALE Total running time: ca. 120 min.

title: The Last Waltz
description: It’s our favorite time of year again, time to rock out with The Band and a cavalcade of musical superstars in Scorsese’s electrifying concert film. Seventeen years after joining forces as the backing band for rockabilly cult hero Ronnie Hawkins, Canadian roots rockers The Band call it quits with a lavish farewell show at San Francisco’s Winterland Ballroom on Nov. 25, 1976. Filmed by Martin Scorsese, this documentary features standout performances by rock legends such as Bob Dylan, Van Morrison, Eric Clapton, Joni Mitchell, and Muddy Waters, as well as interviews tracing the group’s history and discussing road life.

title: Tampopo
description: FOOD IS LIFE in this mouthwatering “ramen western” about a misfit gang of ramen ronin who guide a noodle-shop owner in her quest for the perfect recipe. Comedy master Jûzô Itami whips kung fu, noir, tearjerkers, Chaplinesque silent antics, and, of course, the spaghetti western into a rich, full-bodied broth and serves it up hot as the wacky, surreal adventures of Tampopo (Itami’s wife Nobuko Miyamoto) are seasoned with the sexy exploits of a gastronome gangster (PERFECT DAYS star Kōji Yakusho). A tasty meditation on human hunger; savory and sweet; nourishing for the body and soul. Umami cinema.

title: Boogie Nights
description: In the San Fernando Valley in 1977, teenage busboy Eddie Adams (Mark Wahlberg) gets discovered by porn director Jack Horner (Burt Reynolds), who transforms him into adult-film sensation Dirk Diggler. Brought into a supportive circle of friends, including fellow actors Amber Waves (Julianne Moore), Rollergirl (Heather Graham) and Reed Rothchild (John C. Reilly), Dirk fulfills all his ambitions, but a toxic combination of drugs and egotism threatens to take him back down.

British Horror Studio: Mr Whispers
description: Introducing a season from the British Horror Studio. An independent British film studio Focusing on Gothic drama and arthouse filmmaking with a distinctive British horror character. Mr Whispers is a raw and unnerving found-footage horror film set within the decaying shadows of an abandoned cinema. When old rumours, local trauma, and a forgotten urban legend begin to close around a group of young investigators, the building becomes more than a location: it becomes a trap, a memory, and a place where something has been waiting in the dark. Directed by Dorian Todd, Oliver Revie, and Seumas MacNeil, and starring Dorian Todd, Sam McMillan, and members of The B-Team repertory, Mr Whispers captures the rough immediacy of grassroots horror while delivering a suffocating atmosphere of dread. It is a film of haunted spaces, buried pain, and the terrible feeling that some places are not empty at all. https://www.britishhorrorstudio.com/

Japan’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: Apocalypse Now : Final Cut
description: In Vietnam in 1970, Captain Willard (Martin Sheen) takes a perilous and increasingly hallucinatory journey upriver to find and terminate Colonel Kurtz (Marlon Brando), a once-promising officer who has reportedly gone completely mad. In the company of a Navy patrol boat filled with street-smart kids, a surfing-obsessed Air Cavalry officer (Robert Duvall), and a crazed freelance photographer (Dennis Hopper), Willard travels further and further into the heart of darkness.

title: Night Moves [1975]
description: Hard-nosed private investigator Harry Moseby (Gene Hackman), to distract himself from a rapidly deteriorating marriage, takes a case from an aging B-movie queen (Janet Ward) to locate her runaway daughter, Delly (Melanie Griffith). His search takes him to the Florida Keys, where the girl has been hiding out with her stepfather, Tom (John Crawford), and Tom's lover, Paula (Jennifer Warren). Harry initiates an affair with Paula and soon learns the case is more complex than he first assessed it.

title: The Adventures of Prince Achmed
description: This performance will feature a live score performed by Hugo Max . Lotte Reiniger’s The Adventures of Prince Achmed is an enchanting amalgamation of stories from the Arabian Nights animated in cut paper silhouettes, an exquisite artefact of Weimar Cinema and a genre-defying experiment in melding international folk art traditions with the technical possibilities of a new medium. Taken from The Arabian Nights, a wicked sorcerer and the beautiful prince Achmed battle one another in a series of wondrous adventures. Please view this YouTube video for a sample of Hugo's work.

title: Empire of Passion
description: With an arresting mix of eroticism and horror, Oshima plunges the viewer into a nightmarish tale of guilt and retribution in Empire of Passion (Ai no borei). Set in a Japanese village at the end of the nineteenth century, the film details the emotional and physical downfall of a married woman and her younger lover following their decision to murder her husband and dump his body in a well. Empire of Passion was Oshima's only true kaidan (Japanese ghost story), and the film, a savage, unrelenting experience, earned him the best director award at the Cannes Film Festival.

title: FAMILY PORTRAITS
description: Here the filmmakers create portraits of their parents, children, siblings, or other relatives, with the resultant films – not surprisingly – proving especially lyrical, emotional, and poetic in their contemplation of aging and loss. Edward Owens REMEMBRANCE: A PORTRAIT STUDY (1967, 6 min, 16mm) Edward Owens PRIVATE IMAGININGS AND NARRATIVE FACTS (1968-70, 9 min, 16mm, silent) Robert Beavers PITCHER OF COLORED LIGHT (2000-07, 23 min, 16mm-to-35mm) Gunvor Nelson TIME BEING (1991, 8 min, 16mm, silent) Friedl vom Gröller PARENTS: MOTHER, FATHER / ELTERN: MUTTER, VATER (1997-99, 6 min, 16mm, silent) Friedl vom Gröller NEC SPE, NEC METU (2013, 4 min, 16mm, silent) Guy Sherwin SHORT FILM SERIES: PORTRAIT WITH PARENTS (1974, 3 min, 16mm) Gunvor Nelson MY NAME IS OONA (1969, 10 min, 16mm) Paige Taul 10:28,30 (2019, 4.5 min, 16mm-to-DCP) Viktoria Schmid KATHARINAVIKTORIA (2011, 1 min, 16mm-to-DCP) Viktoria Schmid KATHARINAVIKTORIA 2(021) (2022, 1 min, 16mm) Total running time: 80 min.

title: THE UMBRELLAS OF CHERBOURG
description:
They are young, in love and certain they will wait for each other. Then Guy is sent to Algeria, Geneviève discovers she is pregnant, and the future begins asking questions their romance cannot answer.
Every line is sung, every colour seems to carry a feeling, and Michel Legrand’s music makes ordinary heartbreak soar. Jacques Demy and Catherine Deneuve create a world of ravishing surfaces without protecting their characters from money, time or compromise. A musical of overwhelming beauty whose greatest surprise is how clear-eyed it is about love.

title: ZORN III
description: Mathieu Amalric ZORN III (2018-2022) 2022, 82 min, DCP. With John Zorn and Barbara Hannigan. “Why can’t Mathieu Amalric stop filming John Zorn? It’s because consciously or unconsciously, he understands that he can only get closer to this man if he imitates his restlessness. It’s this Sisyphean tirelessness, the fact that we must imagine Zorn (whose surname translates into German as anger) as a happy man, which is at the core of his art. He makes music in order to be alive. This time, however, Zorn is not the only protagonist, as the Canadian soprano Barbara Hannigan enters the wild world of the composer. Much more straightforward than its previous iterations, the film captures Hannigan’s rehearsals for a performance of Zorn’s song cycle ‘Jumalattaret’ together with pianist Stephen Gosling. The work pushes her vocal capacities to the limit, with the sudden shifts in register, extended high notes and bird-like chirping demanding everything from her.” –Patrick Holzapfel, VIENNALE

title: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth
description: Brad Pitt returns to his Academy Award-winning role as Cliff Booth, only this time it’s 1977 and it’s a very different Hollywood. Directed by David Fincher from a screenplay by Quentin Tarantino, the film also stars Elizabeth Debicki, Scott Caan, Carla Gugino, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II and Peter Weller. (Netflix)

title: Planes, Trains and Automobiles
description: I like me! Easily excitable Neal Page (Steve Martin) is somewhat of a control freak. Trying to get home to Chicago to spend Thanksgiving with his wife (Laila Robins) and kids, his flight is rerouted to a distant city in Kansas because of a freak snowstorm, and his sanity begins to fray. Worse yet, he is forced to bunk up with talkative Del Griffith (John Candy), whom he finds extremely annoying. Together they must overcome the insanity of holiday travel to reach their intended destination.

title: The Nightmare Before Christmas
description: Tired of scaring humans every October 31 with the same old bag of tricks, Jack Skellington, the spindly king of Halloween Town, kidnaps Santa Claus and plans to deliver shrunken heads and other ghoulish gifts to children on Christmas morning. But as Christmas approaches, Jack’s rag-doll girlfriend, Sally, tries to foil his misguided plans.

title: PLANES, TRAINS AND AUTOMOBILES
description: Steve Martin and John Candy star in John Hughes’ classic tale of holiday travel gone awry. Neal Page (Martin) is an uptight advertising executive trying to get home to Chicago for Thanksgiving. When his flight is rerouted to Wichita, he reluctantly partners with Del Griffith (Candy), an obnoxious yet lovable salesman. Together, they embark on a cross-country adventure that includes various modes of transportation, hilarious mishaps and unforgettable rental car shenanigans.

title: Pink Palace: The Einstein of Sex
description: Pink Palace in collaboration with the Goethe Institute London presents Pink, Kitsch & Revolution, a season of films celebrating the work of Filmmaker and Activist Rosa von Praunheim.  “The Einstein of Sex,” as the American press once called him, Magnus Hirschfeld was one of the most influential pion...

title: The Odyssey
description: Odysseus, the legendary King of Ithaca, embarks on a long and perilous journey home following the Trojan War. Throughout his voyage, he is forced to confront the whims of gods, mythological monsters, and trials that stretch both his cunning and his humanity to the breaking point.

title: SELF-PORTRAITS
description: Just as the realm of two-dimensional portraiture has always encompassed self-portraiture, so too has the corresponding practice within cinema. This program collects instances of filmmakers turning the camera on themselves, or using the techniques of animation to explore their own appearances and identities. Gérard Courant CINÉMATON N°1000: GÉRARD COURANT (1987, 3.5 min, 16mm-to-digital) Kurt Kren 36/78 RISCHART (1978, 3 min, 16mm) Shigeko Kubota SELF-PORTRAIT (ca. 1970-1971, 5 min, video) Tehching Hsieh TIME CLOCK PIECE (ONE YEAR PERFORMANCE 1980-1981) (1980-81, 7 min, 16mm, silent) Gotot Prakosa SELF-PORTRAIT (1982, 3 min, digital) Valie Export SELF-PORTRAIT WITH HEAD / SELBSTPORTRAIT MIT KOPF (1966-67, 4 min, DCP, silent) Vito Acconci WATCH (1971, 9 min, Super-8mm-to-16mm, silent. description: Don't miss our fan favourite MYSTERY MOVIE screenings! On a near weekly basis we will serve up a random mystery movie, with No Clues and No Hints as to what they will be. In 2026, we'll be presenting these as STAFF CURATED selections each and every week by our lovely Front of House, Duty Manager, and Projection Team! We strongly advise that you take this into consideration before purchasing a ticket.

title: WHO ARE YOU, POLLY MAGGOO?
description:
A television crew wants to discover the real Polly Maggoo. The fashion industry wants an image. Admirers want a fantasy. Somewhere inside the competing demands is a young American model who keeps slipping out of the frame.
Photographer William Klein turns his insider’s eye on the absurd theatre of fashion and celebrity. Metallic couture, mock-documentary interviews and surreal interruptions make a wickedly funny pop-art assault on the business of manufacturing personalities. A sixties satire whose question has only become more pointed: who gets to decide what an image means?

title: MUSIC IS MUSIC + BEFORE IT'S TOO LATE
description: Mathieu Amalric MUSIC IS MUSIC 2017, 20 min, DCP “In a poetic composition of song, narration, and images, this film follows Canadian soprano and orchestra conductor Barbara Hannigan, accompanied by the Ludwig Orchestra, as she records her album ‘Crazy Girl Crazy’. Why did she choose these three pieces, in essence so different, but which intimately resonate with her: Berio’s ‘Sequenza III’, Berg’s ‘Lulu Suite’, and Gershwin’s ‘Girl Crazy’?” –INTERNATIONAL FESTIVAL OF FILMS ON ART Mathieu Amalric BEFORE IT’S TOO LATE / AVANT QU’IL NE SOIT TROP TARD 2023, 65 min, DCP “After 47 years together, the Emerson String Quartet records their last album, ‘Infinite Voyage’, in three days. For this farewell, they invited soprano Barbara Hannigan, and a film was born. Their precise work, the moments of enthusiasm and fear, the research and the jokes, the age limit of these men and Hannigan’s flamboyance, the admiring friendship full of irony and rigor, the profession and yet the discovery, humor as a cog towards concentration, the individual and the group…all this composes a portrait of the usually invisible production of music. Before everyone resumes their path.” –DOCLISBOA Total running time: ca. 90 min.

title: Blade Runner : The Final Cut
description: Deckard (Harrison Ford) is forced by the police Boss (M. Emmet Walsh) to continue his old job as Replicant Hunter. His assignment: eliminate four escaped Replicants from the colonies who have returned to Earth. Before starting the job, Deckard goes to the Tyrell Corporation and he meets Rachel (Sean Young), a Replicant girl he falls in love with.

title: Ken Russell's The Devils: The Director's Cut
description: Censored for over half a century, Ken Russell’s film returns in a landmark director’s cut reconstruction that reveals the full power of his original vision. Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, accused of bewitching a convent of nuns, The Devils lays bare the collusion of church and state through a searing vision of religious persecution, collective hysteria and institutional corruption. The restoration many believed would never happen reaffirms Russell’s incendiary masterpiece as among the most overwhelming and uncompromising achievements in British cinema. Assembled from original camera negative, this 4k restoration is Ken Russell’s 2004 preferred edit. Picture and sound restoration by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color and Warner Bros. Sound.

title: Your Name [Kimi no Na wa.]
description: Two teenagers share a profound, magical connection upon discovering they are swapping bodies. Things manage to become even more complicated when the boy and girl decide to meet in person.

title: Gandahar
description: An entire civilisation must confront its destiny in alternative-animation pioneer René Laloux's final feature, a cult classic of mind-bending science fiction. In a distant world, a merciless army of automata attacks Gandahar, turning its peace-loving people to stone. Hoping to discover the source of these Men of Metal, a council of matriarchs enlists the brave yet inexperienced warrior Sylvain (Pierre-Marie Escourro), who, while journeying through his planet's outer regions, teams up with the Deformed, a race cast out from Gandahar after failed science experiments rendered them mutants. Soon, Sylvain learns that a gargantuan brain called Metamorphis (Georges Wilson) is responsible for his utopian society's strife and—together with the beautiful Airelle (Catherine Chevallier)—travels through time to defeat him, in the process risking their lives and Gandahar's very existence. Featuring stunningly surreal creatures and wondrously bizarre environments designed by renowned comic-book artist Caza, Gandahar is a visceral, visionary head-trip in which animation opens a gateway to the furthest reaches of the imagination.

From boundary-pushing directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim comes You Can See Everything .

title: The Last Waltz - 50th Anniversary
description: Seventeen years after joining forces as the backing band for rockabilly cult hero Ronnie Hawkins, Canadian roots rockers The Band call it quits with a lavish farewell show at San Francisco's Winterland Ballroom on Nov. 25, 1976. Filmed by Martin Scorsese, this documentary features standout performances by rock legends such as Bob Dylan, Neil Young, Van Morrison, Eric Clapton, Joni Mitchell and Muddy Waters, as well as interviews tracing the group's history and discussing road life.

title: Ginger Snaps
description: “I get this ache... And I, I thought it was for sex, but it's to tear everything to fucking pieces.” A wild and bloodthirsty hound has ravaged through the small town of Bailey Downs, attacking the neighbourhood's pet dogs. When the two teenage outcasts, the Fitzgerald sisters, stumble upon the creature one night, their lives change forever as Ginger is bitten, and her body starts to change. A true feast of practical effects, 2000s grunge, and snappy one-liners; Ginger Snaps has been credited in hindsight as a predecessor to the “maneater” supernatural woman most famously seen in Jennifer´s Body (2009). A coming-of-age story told in a fresh perspective; for maybe the true terror lies in growing up, or maybe it lies in the bloodthirsty hound who calls herself your sister. Ginger Snaps is featured as part of MANEATERS, a season exploring the female supernatural on screen. The season is presented with the National Film and Television School’s Film Studies, Programming and Curation MA.

He builds a movement to protect their land, preserving the ecosystem and centuries of ecological knowledge. Facing threats from global agribusiness, m...

title: OVER THE EDGE
description:
New Granada has houses, roads and a bright suburban future. It has almost nothing for its teenagers. Boredom becomes solidarity, solidarity becomes defiance, and the adults discover that treating young people as a problem can make their fears come true.
Jonathan Kaplan’s cult youth film catches adolescence with unusual sympathy and bite. A young Matt Dillon, a remarkable rock soundtrack and the unruly energy of its cast make rebellion feel exhilarating before the consequences land. A suburban pressure cooker that refuses to dismiss the kids as either innocents or delinquents.

title: Andrew Lloyd Webber's Starlight Express - Live On
description: Filmed live at the specially designed Starlight Auditorium at Troubadour Wembley Park Theatre, ANDREW LLOYD WEBBER'S STARLIGHT EXPRESS - LIVE ON STAGE will immerse audiences in a world of speed, song and storytelling as an incredible cast of 40 whizz across the screen, performing some of musical theatre’s most beloved songs. As a child’s train set magically comes to life and the engines race to become the fastest in the world, Rusty the steam train has little hope of winning until he is inspired by the legend of the ‘Starlight Express’. A show seen around the world by over 30 million people, and with music by Andrew Lloyd Webber and lyrics by Richard Stilgoe, ANDREW LLOYD WEBBER'S STARLIGHT EXPRESS - LIVE ON STAGE is an electrifying experience for all ages.

title: Solve Along A Murder She Wrote
description: Cult hit event Solve-Along-A-Murder-She-Wrote returns to the Prince Charles Cinema with an interactive screening of a classic Murder, She Wrote episode. Watch as Cabot Cove gets caught up in a murder mystery only JB Fletcher (or you!) can solve! Solve-Along-A-Murder-She-Wrote is a unique and hilarious night featuring games, prizes and audience participation, with special permission from NBC Universal Television. See the show Time Out rated one of 2021 and 2019’s 50 Great Nights Out in London that has played to sell-out audiences across the UK and Australia. Hosted by super-fan Tim Benzie, Solve-Along-A-Murder-She-Wrote features: * A race to solve to the crime, via the Fameometer and the Suspiciometer! * A Cabot Cove quiz! * A singalong to the theme tune with new lyrics! * Clips and biogs of the campy guest stars! Tim Benzie is obsessed with Murder, She Wrote, having watched the original series when it was first broadcast, and now relishing the repeats on television everywhere. Tim is the writer/performer of “It’s a Mystery!”, all about our love of whodunnits. An award-winning playwright and co-writer of the Royal Vauxhall Tavern’s 2017-2023 pantos (‘Goosed’, ‘Rubbed’, ‘Slipped’, ‘Pricked’, ‘Cracked’ and ‘Tossed’). He is the co-producer of the camp club night PopHorror. Visit us at www.solvealongamurdershewrote.com , or follow us on Instagram, Twitter and Facebook @solvealonga. 2026 SCHEDULE: Thursday 26th November 2026 New episode TBC Thursday 17th December 2026 Encore screening - "A Christmas Secret" Directed by Anthony Pullen Shaw Starring Angela Lansbury, Larry Wilcox, Amy Brenneman 1992 | 120mins | USA *** The Critics speak! “You’ll be swept away with Jessica Fletcher feels … it has the BEST HOST.” - Time Out London "A cinematic, theatrical and hilarious experience ... title: SMOOTH TALK
description:
For Connie, summer means music, shopping trips and practising the person she wants to become. Then an older stranger pulls up outside her house while she is alone, and ordinary flirtation begins turning into something she cannot easily name—or escape.
Laura Dern and Treat Williams are extraordinary in Joyce Chopra’s adaptation of Joyce Carol Oates. Sunlit teenage restlessness gives way to a confrontation whose menace grows almost imperceptibly. The film understands the thrill of being seen and the terror of being claimed, making its shift from coming-of-age drama to psychological nightmare devastating.

title: Planes, Trains & Automobiles
description: Easily excitable Neal Page (Steve Martin) is somewhat of a control freak. Trying to get home to Chicago to spend Thanksgiving with his wife (Laila Robins) and kids, his flight is rerouted to a distant city in Kansas because of a freak snowstorm, and his sanity begins to fray. Worse yet, he is forced to bunk up with talkative Del Griffith (John Candy), whom he finds extremely annoying. Together they must overcome the insanity of holiday travel to reach their intended destination.

title: Akira
description: Iconic and game-changing, AKIRA is the definitive anime masterpiece! Katsuhiro Otomo's landmark cyberpunk classic obliterated the boundaries of Japanese animation and forced the world to look into the future. AKIRA's arrival shattered traditional thinking, creating space for future generations of ground-breaking movies. July, 1988 - World War III breaks loose. Then, in 2019, in megalopolis Tokyo...As the leader of a group of young robust delinquents, Kaneda spent his nights tearing through the urban wastes, racing his motorbike against rival groups. One night while riding with his gang, his friend Tetsuo suddenly encounters a strange boy - the product of human experimentation and is injured in the ensuing crash. Shortly thereafter, a military squadron appears on the scene to take the boy and Tetsuo away to an army research facility. Determined to free Tetsuo from capture, Kaneda sneaks into the army research lab. However, a regimen of extreme experimental procedures has awakened a new power in his friend, and now he is consumed by madness..

title: A Confucian Confusion
description: Art versus commerce, friendship versus status, independence versus conformity—values clash and collide in Edward Yang's study of an increasingly Westernized country heading into the twenty-first century without moral guideposts. Moving from breakout hit A Brighter Summer Day's investigation of the past to a critical survey of the present, A Confucian Confusion charts the tangled web of emotional and professional manipulations among a group of young urbanites. At its center is Molly (Ni Shu-chun), director of a floundering public-relations firm. Alienated by the childish fiancé (Bosen Wang) who bankrolls her enterprise—and frustrated by the demands of an assistant, Qiqi (Chen Shiang-chyi), and her own fiancé, Ming (Wang Wei-ming)—Molly lashes out at everyone in her path and threatens to dismantle the company altogether. Meanwhile (amid several other subplots), Molly's talk-show-host sister (Chen Li-mei) attempts to dissuade her separated husband from continuing to write a dark novel about the return of Confucius to a jaded modern society. Injecting comedic elements into his patented brand of earnest soul-searching, Yang finds humor as well as pathos in the desperate behavior of a lost and lonely generation.

title: Singin’ in the Rain
description: Arguably the greatest movie musical ever made, and considered by many  to be one of the greatest films of all time, Singin’ in the Rain remains a singular masterpiece of music, comedy, romance, and dance, set against a breathtaking Technicolor backdrop of imagination and artistry. Gene Kelly and Debbie Reynolds electrify the screen in back-to-back legendary musical numbers. Jean Hagen delights as the perfectly hilarious villain. The entrancing Cyd Charisse shows off her spectacular moves in a dazzling pas de deux with Kelly. It’s an inspiring, entertaining, stunning, and remarkable work of cinematic majesty.

title: Once Upon A Time In… Hollywood
description: Quentin Tarantino’s Once Upon a Time in… Hollywood visits 1969 Los Angeles, where everything is changing, as TV star Rick Dalton (Leonardo DiCaprio) and his longtime stunt double Cliff Booth (Brad Pitt) make their way around an industry they hardly recognize anymore. The ninth film from the writer-director features a large ensemble cast and multiple storylines in a tribute to the final moments of Hollywood’s golden age.

title: Eyes Wide Shut
description: Stanley Kubrick's daring last film is many things. It is a compelling psychosexual journey. A haunting dreamscape. A riveting tale of suspense. A major milestone in the careers of stars Tom Cruise and Nicole Kidman. And "a worthy final chapter to a great director's career" (Roger Ebert). Cruise plays Dr William Hartford, who plunges into an erotic foray that threatens his marriage - and may even ensnare him in a lurid murder mystery - after his wife's (Kidman) admission of sexual longings. As the story sweeps from doubt and fear to self-discovery and reconciliation, Kubrick orchestrates it with masterful flourishes. Graceful tracking shots, controlled pacing, rich colours, startling images: bravura traits that make Kubrick a filmmaker for the ages are here to keep everyone's eyes wide shut.

title: Amelie - 25th Anniversary
description: 23-year-old Amélie is lonely. After an isolating childhood, she moves to Paris and becomes a waitress at the Café des Deux Moulins, a bar restaurant filled with a colourful cast of diners and employees. One night, Amélie happens across a box of treasures hidden in her apartment, left by a little boy in the Fifties, that changes the course of her life. Henceforth, she dedicates herself to giving back to her community, tracking down the owner of these keepsakes, consoling a widowed neighbour and befriending a reclusive artist. When completing these good deeds, she crosses paths with Nino, a photobooth collagist who shares her oddball sensibilities. She quickly falls in love with him.

title: North by Northwest
description: The ultimate Hitchcock thrill ride, centered on the Master of Suspense’s favorite theme: an innocent man accused of a crime he didn’t commit. Here, the poor sucker is an effortlessly cool Cary Grant (or is that redundant?), playing an advertising exec who’s mistaken for a spy named George Kaplan — and then mistaken for a murderer! His efforts to clear his own name and unravel a sinister conspiracy will take across the United States, from an epic train ride to an assassination attempt by airplane to a chase across Mount Rushmore. But hey, he does get to romance Eva Marie Saint along the way, so maybe it’s all worth it?

title: All of a Sudden
description: Virginie Efira and Tao Okamoto shared the Best Actress prize at Cannes for Academy Award–winning director Ryûsuke Hamaguchi’s (Drive My Car, NYFF59) radiant new film about a nursing home director promoting a radical new care program. Japan’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: THE HEARTBREAK KID
description:
Lenny is three days into his honeymoon when he spots the woman he thinks he should have married. The bride is upstairs with sunburn. He is downstairs selling himself a completely different future.
Elaine May makes romantic self-delusion almost unbearably funny. Charles Grodin turns every conversation into a sales pitch, while Jeannie Berlin gives the discarded Lila a presence the film refuses to let him wish away. A romantic comedy with surgical instincts, exposing the monstrous entitlement hidden inside one ordinary man’s idea of the perfect match.

title: The Muppet Christmas Carol
description: 'Tis the season for love, laughter, and one of the most cherished stories of all time! Join Kermit the Frog, Miss Piggy, and all the hilarious Muppets in this merry, magical version of Charles Dickens' classic tale. Academy Award® winner Michael Caine (Best Supporting Actor) gives a performance that's anything but "bah, humbug!" as greedy, penny-pinching Ebenezer Scrooge. One fateful Christmas Eve, Scrooge is visited by the Ghosts of Christmas Past, Present, and Future. Together with kind, humble Bob Cratchit (Kermit the Frog) and his family, the Spirits open Scrooge's eyes -- and his heart -- to the true meaning of Christmas. Filled with original music and dazzling special effects, THE MUPPET CHRISTMAS CAROL will become a holiday tradition your family will treasure all the days of the year. Featuring the film’s famous long-lost song ‘When Love is Gone’! ------ As always you can expect SING ALONG performances of this new version of THE MUPPET CHRISTMAS CAROL this Christmas - and now we don't need to pretend that we weren't going to just play the lost scene regardless! Performances will feature a Hosted Pre-Show with our very own Father Christmas, where you will be prepped on what to do throughout the film. Costumes aren't mandatory, but 'Tis the season, and we love seeing you dressed up in your favourite Christmas Jumpers! All this, and a few more surprises up our sleeves, makes this one of the must-see events this Christmas! All other screenings will be regular performances, and nothing will be written next to the start time.

title: Unzipped
description: Designer Isaac Mizrahi proved a force of nature on the road to his legendary fall 1994 collection, a career-defining triumph that was documented with an effervescent intimacy by Douglas Keeve, Mizrahi’s then-partner. Both a time capsule of the buoyant, raucous 1990s, when pop culture and high art became interchangeable, and a vérité-style, in-the-trenches report on the daily agonies and ecstasies of the creative process, this seminal artistic portrait—sumptuously shot by Ellen Kuras and Robert Leacock—transcends glitz and glamour to offer an extraordinary view of the charisma and force of will inherent to genius, as well as its personal costs. Digitally restored by the Sundance Institute and UCLA Film & Television Archive. Funding provided by Isaac Mizrahi Entertainment. Laboratory services by Roundabout Entertainment, Inc. and Deluxe Media Audio Services.

title: LIAF: Open Night: Elizabeth Hobbs: History, Heresy & Hyenas (15*)
ANDY WARHOL’S 'SCREEN TESTS' + CONRAD VENTUR’S 'SCREEN TESTS REVISITED', PGM 1
description: These two programs pair Warhol’s seminal and often exquisite SCREEN TESTS – the silent, black-and-white, three-and-a-half minute filmic portraits he made between 1964-66, which grew to encompass 472 separate reels, portraying 189 individual subjects (many of them sitting for multiple portraits) – with Conrad Ventur’s 21st-century remakes. For Ventur’s (ongoing) project, he has sought out as many of the surviving SCREEN TESTees as possible, and restaged their portraits, resulting in a poetic tribute to Warhol’s films and to the transformations wrought by time. Conrad Ventur in person on Sat, Nov 21!

title: NAKED LUNCH
description:
The bug powder is addictive. The typewriter is alive. And Bill Lee’s latest assignment may be coming from an insect intelligence service. Fleeing into the Interzone, he tries to write a report from a reality that will not stay still.
David Cronenberg fuses William S. Burroughs’s fiction and biography into a wonderfully deadpan nightmare of addiction and authorship. Peter Weller plays the impossible with perfect weary conviction, while grotesque organic machines make language horribly physical. A literary adaptation that succeeds by becoming its own mutant creature.

title: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth
description: Brad Pitt returns to his Academy Award-winning role as Cliff Booth, only this time it’s 1977 and it’s a very different Hollywood. Directed by David Fincher from a screenplay by Quentin Tarantino, the film also stars Elizabeth Debicki, Scott Caan, Carla Gugino, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II and Peter Weller. (Netflix)

title: Desperately Seeking Susan
description: Susan Seidelman’s stylish New York fairy tale features an effervescent young Madonna in her first film role. Rosanna Arquette stars as Roberta, a bored suburban housewife who is fascinated with a mystery woman, Susan, played by Madonna. When she spots an ad meant for Susan in the personals, Roberta goes to the rendezvous too, and in a series of events involving amnesia and mistaken identity, she steps out of her own sterile existence and into the danger and romance of Susan’s life. With incredible 80s style, two iconic leads, and laughs, intrigue, and tons of fun to boot, we’ve got your Black Friday covered!

title: DAWN OF THE DEAD
description: Writer-director George A. Romero ups the ante on his indie landmark NIGHT OF THE LIVING DEAD with a bigger budget, more gore (courtesy of special effects/makeup artist Tom Savini) and a touch of social commentary. Four people take refuge in a Pennsylvania shopping mall as a mysterious plague turns fresh corpses into flesh-hungry zombies and civilization collapses around them. “One of the best horror films ever made.” – Roger Ebert, Chicago Sun-Times.

title: All of a Sudden
description: Virginie Efira and Tao Okamoto shared the Best Actress prize at Cannes for Academy Award–winning director Ryûsuke Hamaguchi’s (Drive My Car, NYFF59) radiant new film about a nursing home director promoting a radical new care program. title: Love Actually
description: Nine intertwined stories examine the complexities of the one emotion that connects us all: love. Among the characters explored are David (Hugh Grant), the handsome newly elected British prime minister who falls for a young junior staffer (Martine McCutcheon), Sarah (Laura Linney), a graphic designer whose devotion to her mentally ill brother complicates her love life, and Harry (Alan Rickman), a married man tempted by his attractive new secretary.

title: Sing-A-Long-A Rocky Horror Picture Show
description: THE ROCKY HORROR PICTURE SHOW SING ALONG is getting revamped in 2027 – for all future shows, CLICK HERE ! The Campest Cult Classic of all time gets the Singalonga treatment it’s been SCREAMING for! Featuring the film, starring Tim Curry, Susan Sarandon, Meatloaf and Richard O’Brien, it’s the most outrageous, riotous, kitsch, wonderful romp ever. If you’ve done The Time Warp before, you’ll never have done it quite like this! The evening begins with your host leading a vocal warm-up before they show you how to use your free interactive props bag. Fancy dress is not obligatory but highly recommended! Please Note : The 15 rating we have placed upon this screening is due to the Adult content of the hosted pre-show which may not be suitable for those under 15. Please Note : This is a screening of the movie not a live stage show. Also this screening may contain sudden loud noises and flashing lights.

title: MYSTERY MOVIE
description:
Take a seat without knowing what is coming. Our mystery screenings explore the bold, disreputable and gloriously unclassifiable world of psychotronic cinema: discoveries that make you wonder how they were made, who they were made for, and why nobody showed you sooner.
The title stays secret until showtime. Curiosity is essential; good taste is negotiable.
Strictly for adult audiences. Films may contain offensive and upsetting content. Do not attend if you are of a sensitive disposition.

title: Enter the Dragon
description: Bruce Lee kicks all the ass in the ultimate martial arts action masterpiece, Enter the Dragon . A martial artist with a bone to pick, Lee vows to take down a reclusive crime lord by beating him in his own Kung Fu tournament. With remarkable combat choreography by Bruce Lee himself, this is one action-packed classic that never gets old and one of the greatest action movies ever made!

title: Grindhouse
description: Quentin Tarantino and Robert Rodriguez's homage to exploitation double features in the 60s and 70s with two back-to-back cult films that include previews of coming attractions between them.

title: Category H: MALATESTA’S CARNIVAL OF BLOOD + FINAL DESTINATION 3
description: The smell of doughnuts and candyfloss, vomiting on the waltzers and rides that probably haven’t passed any kind of safety test - don’t we all have fond memories of the fun fair? At Category H Film Club, we’re bringing the terror of the fairground Rio’s screen two with a late night double bill of MAL...

title: Once Upon A Time In… Hollywood
description: Quentin Tarantino’s Once Upon a Time in… Hollywood visits 1969 Los Angeles, where everything is changing, as TV star Rick Dalton (Leonardo DiCaprio) and his longtime stunt double Cliff Booth (Brad Pitt) make their way around an industry they hardly recognize anymore. The ninth film from the writer-director features a large ensemble cast and multiple storylines in a tribute to the final moments of Hollywood’s golden age.

title: Station West
description: After two U.S. cavalrymen transporting a gold shipment get killed, U.S. Army Intelligence investigator John Haven goes undercover to a mining and logging town to find the killers.

title: FFC: Chilly Pics Shorts Programme (U*)
description: Come along for a morning of wintry wonderlands in this short film programme curated especially for Family Film Club audiences.

title: Jurassic Park
description: In Steven Spielberg's massive blockbuster, paleontologists Alan Grant (Sam Neill) and Ellie Sattler (Laura Dern) and mathematician Ian Malcolm (Jeff Goldblum) are among a select group chosen to tour an island theme park populated by dinosaurs created from prehistoric DNA. While the park's mastermind, billionaire John Hammond (Richard Attenborough), assures everyone that the facility is safe, they find out otherwise when various ferocious predators break free and go on the hunt.

title: Gremlins
description: Accessible screening On the last Saturday of every month, the museum's Family Matinee is an accessible screening where we offer open captioning, keep the theater dimly lit, and maintain a lower volume for viewers who are neurodiverse. When Billy receives a mysterious creature called a mogwai, affectionately named Gizmo, from his father for Christmas, he must follow three rules: keep it away from sunlight, don’t get it wet, and above all else, never feed it after midnight. When the creature accidentally gets wet and more mogwai spawn with much more devious intentions than the docile Gizmo, mayhem erupts. With the town’s adults out of their depth, it is up to Billy and Gizmo to defeat these menacing creatures. The violence in the PG-rated Gremlins was one of the reasons the Motion Picture Association later created the PG-13 rating; the film is often cited as kick-starting a trend of small creature features in the 1980s. Please note: This film contains discussions about Santa Claus that might not be appropriate for younger viewers.
director: Joe Dante PRODUCED BY: Michael Finnell

title: My Neighbor Totoro
description: Satsuki and Mei's mother has taken ill. In order to be closer to her while she recovers in a rural convalescent hospital, their father moves the two sisters from their home in a city to the countryside. The house they move into is a ramshackle old place in the shadow of an ancient camphor tree, and Satsuki and Mei embark on adventures with the wondrous forest spirits who live nearby.

title: All of a Sudden

title: Fantasia on 35mm
description: Walt Disney’s timeless masterpiece is a breathtaking extravaganza of sight and sound! The feature film that exposed millions of impressionable kiddos to the glory of classical music, this gorgeous and symphonic masterpiece will have you waltzing with mythical centaurs, making magic with Mickey Mouse, pirouetting with hippos, and more! Presented in Fantasound – a precursor to surround sound – Fantasia was the first film ever screened in stereo. Widely considered one of the greatest animated features ever made, and in the top 25 grossing films ever, this breathtaking classic never gets old. See the music come to life, hear the pictures burst into song, and experience the excitement that is Fantasia !

title: Fantastic Mr. Fox
description: The Fantastic Mr. Fox, bored with his current life, plans a heist against the three local farmers. The farmers, tired of sharing their chickens with the sly fox, seek revenge against him and his family.

title: Batman Returns
description: Tim Burton’s massively entertaining follow-up to his groundbreaking Batman blockbuster goes bigger and bolder with the Penguin (Danny DeVito), Catwoman (Michelle Pfeiffer), and corrupt businessman Max Shrek (Christopher Walken) out to rid the world of the caped crusader (Michael Keaton). Batman Returns remains one of filmdom’s most ambitious sequels, showcasing incredible production design and visual effects, along with standout performances.

title: The Odyssey
description: Odysseus, the legendary King of Ithaca, embarks on a long and perilous journey home following the Trojan War. Throughout his voyage, he is forced to confront the whims of gods, mythological monsters, and trials that stretch both his cunning and his humanity to the breaking point.

title: The Worst Person in the World
description: On the verge of turning thirty, Julie is faced with a series of choices that force her to pursue new perspectives on her life in contemporary Oslo. Over the course of four years, she navigates love affairs and existential uncertainty as she starts deciding who she wants to become.

title: Arabic Cinema Club: MAYBE TOMORROW + Q&A
description: Maybe Tomorrow follows Wafa with intimacy and emotional clarity as she navigates the weight of absence, refusing to let her father's story be forgotten. At once a deeply personal act of love and a quiet form of resistance, the film is rooted in the everyday reality of carrying on when closure feels ...

title: Rear Window
description: A wheelchair-bound photographer spies on his neighbors from his apartment window and becomes convinced one of them has committed murder.

title: DIVA
description:
A postman secretly records the opera singer who refuses to be recorded. Another cassette contains evidence that powerful people would kill to suppress. When the two worlds collide, Paris becomes a maze of hired killers, impossible escapes and sudden romance.
Jean-Jacques Beineix makes every surface sing: blue light, wet streets, lofts and métro tunnels turn a thriller into an art-pop daydream. Opera and street culture, immaculate design and scruffy obsession exist in the same enchanted city. A defining burst of cinéma du look, made for anyone who has ever loved an image—or a voice—too much.

title: All of a Sudden

title: Cléo from 5 to 7
description: One of the most delightful films of the French New Wave, iconic filmmaker Agnès Varda eloquently captures Paris in the sixties with this real-time portrait of a singer set adrift in the city. A chronicle of the minutes of one woman’s life as she awaits test results of a biopsy, Cléo from 5 to 7 is a spirited mix of vivid vérité and melodrama, featuring a score by Michel Legrand and cameos by Jean-Luc Godard and Anna Karina.

title: EC: JENNINGS / KIRSANOFF
description: Humphrey Jennings LISTEN TO BRITAIN (1941, 19 min, 35mm) Jennings’s film is a masterpiece of sound mixing; it creates an audio landscape of Britain during the war, with images both accompanying and conflicting with the multitude of sounds. Dimitri Kirsanoff MÉNILMONTANT (1924-25, 38 min, 35mm, silent) “[T]o a remarkable degree, MÉNILMONTANT seems an autonomous creation, as sophisticated and demanding as any narrative film of the silent period, without obvious imitators. Although Richard Abel has astutely called attention to aspects the film shares with Abel Gance’s LA ROUE (1923) and Leon Moussinac’s LE BRASIER ARDENT (1923)…and with Jean Epstein’s COEUR FIDELE (1923)…any comparison of the film as a whole with those admirable works would have to underline the intensity, uniqueness, and exceptional rigor of Kirsanoff’s achievement.” –P. Adams Sitney, THE CINEMA OF POETRY Total running time: ca. 60 min. CLICK HERE TO BOOK TICKETS NOW!

title: The Mummy [1999]
description: The Mummy is a rousing, suspenseful and horrifying epic about an expedition of treasure-seeking explorers in the Sahara Desert in 1925. Stumbling upon an ancient tomb, the hunters unwittingly set loose a 3,000-year-old legacy of terror, which is embodied in the vengeful reincarnation of an Egyptian priest who had been sentenced to an eternity as one of the living dead.

title: PORTRAITS OF THE ARTIST
description: Beginning with Gerard Malanga’s ANDY WARHOL (1964), in which the author of the SCREEN TESTS sits for his own extended portrait, this program finds the directors turning the camera on their fellow filmmakers, or even trading places for complementary films (as in the case of the Friedl vom Gröller and Christiana Perschon films that close the screening). Gerard Malanga ANDY WARHOL: PORTRAITS OF THE ARTIST AS A YOUNG MAN (1964, 21 min, 16mm-to-DCP) Ludwig Schönherr PORTRÄTFILM: KURT KREN (1969, 3.5 min, 16mm-to-DCP, silent) Ludwig Schönherr PORTRÄTFILM: ELISABETH ERKNER (1969, 14 min, 16mm-to-DCP, silent) Barry Gerson PORTRAIT OF ANDREW NOREN (1972, 4 min, 16mm, silent) Friedl vom Gröller I DON’T WANT TO BE FILMED BUT RATHER SHOOT MYSELF / ICH WILL NICHT GEFILMT WERDEN, SONDERN SELBER FILMEN (2023, 3 min, 16mm, silent) Christiana Perschon FRIEDL (2023, 2.5 min, 16mm-to-DCP) Friedl vom Gröller FLO UND KEN JACOBS (2001, 3 min, 16mm, silent) Friedl vom Gröller PETER KUBELKA UND JONAS MEKAS (1994, 2.5 min, 16mm, silent) Jeff Weber PETER (2026, 5.5 min, 35mm, silent) Total running time: ca. 60 min.

title: Sonic Cinema: Daïchi Saïto
description: Sonic Cinema and the Japan Foundation present the films of Montreal-based artist Daïchi Saïto, projected from his personal 35mm prints. A rare encounter with a singular voice in artisanal film practice, this programme highlights Saïto’s skill in bridging metaphysical concepts with sensory experience. Originally from Japan, Daïchi Saïto makes films of intense beauty and power, grounded in abstract approaches to landscape, rhythm, and perception. Produced through expressive use of optical manipulation and painstaking frame-by-frame photochemical treatments, the films in this programme carry a tactile and elemental intensity, teasing out the sensual poetry of the natural world and human subjectivity. Drawing on Saïto's studies in philosophy, literature, and the languages of Hindi and Sanskrit, as much as the language of cinema, these are films built on a poetic dialogue of sound and image. Guided by the expressive improvised soundtracks of Malcolm Goldstein and Jason Sharp, we'll traverse exterior and interior landscapes, from the darkened primordial deserts of Saïto's most recent film earthearthearth (2021), through the stained glass forest of Trees of Syntax , Leaves of Axis (2009), before the torrent of memories and cool mountain vistas carries us away in Engram of Returning (2015). Daïchi will join us in person for a Q&A with series curator Oliver Dickens following the screening. Programme earthearthearth , Canada 2021, 30 min., 35mm Trees of Syntax, Leaves of Axis , Canada 2009, 10 min., 35mm Engram of Returning , Canada, Japan 2015, 18’30 min., 35mm Programmed by Oliver Dickens for Sonic Cinema, presented in partnership with the Japan Foundation.
