title: WHAT IS THE CITY BUT THE PEOPLE?
description: “In 1969 the Department of City Planning attempted to shore up support for its various [development] projects with a multipronged, multimedia public relations blitz. At its center was the publication of a six-volume book, ‘The Plan for New York City’ (1969), which articulated the commissioner’s vision for the metropolis to stem the flight of the middle classes to the suburbs and revitalize urban space. The plan was presented in synopsis form as a propagandistic documentary produced by the Department and co-directed by John Peer Nugent and Gordon Hyatt. Featuring some flashy cinematography from New York location shooter-extraordinaire Arthur J. Ornitz [THE CONNECTION; MINNIE & MOSKOWITZ; SERPICO], WHAT IS THE CITY is an idiosyncratic document of the city in the late 1960s, offering a wide panorama of places and spaces, narrated by one of the plan’s ghost writers, William H. Whyte [THE SOCIAL LIFE OF SMALL URBAN SPACES]. The film flits between footage of and discussion about ‘urban crisis’ (uprisings, poor housing stock, street violence) and purported city-led remedies. Viewed today, the film is both a curious relic of failed urban policy and an index of just how wedded city authorities were (and remain) to the idea that the manipulation of public perception is key to urban governance.” –FILM AT LINCOLN CENTER

title: The Lord of the Rings Trilogy [Theatrical Editions]
description: ALL NIGHTER : FAQs, HOUSE RULES & TIPS Peter Jackson's THE LORD OF THE RINGS TRILOGY is back from the rarely screened Theatrical Editions – from 35mm! Join us as we venture back into Middle-earth the way you would have seen the films on release! THE FELLOWSHIP OF THE RING; A meek Hobbit from the Shire and eight companions set out on a journey to destroy the powerful One Ring and save Middle-earth from the Dark Lord Sauron. THE TWO TOWERS; While Frodo and Sam edge closer to Mordor with the help of the shifty Gollum, the divided fellowship makes a stand against Sauron's new ally, Saruman, and his hordes of Isengard. THE RETURN OF THE KING; Gandalf and Aragorn lead the World of Men against Sauron's army to draw his gaze from Frodo and Sam as they approach Mount Doom with the One Ring. ----------------------------------------------------------------------- NO ADMISSIONS TO THE CINEMA AFTER MIDNIGHT NO ALCOHOL PURCHASED FROM OUTSIDE IS PERMITTED IN THE BUILDING! title: Home Alone
description: When bratty 8-year-old Kevin McCallister (Macaulay Culkin) acts out the night before a family trip to Paris, his mother (Catherine O'Hara) makes him sleep in the attic. After the McCallisters mistakenly leave for the airport without Kevin, he awakens to an empty house and assumes his wish to have no family has come true. But his excitement sours when he realizes that two con men (Joe Pesci, Daniel Stern) plan to rob the McCallister residence, and that he alone must protect the family home.

title: Elf
description: Buddy (Will Ferrell) was accidentally transported to the North Pole as a toddler and raised to adulthood among Santa's elves. Unable to shake the feeling that he doesn't fit in, the adult Buddy travels to New York, in full elf uniform, in search of his real father. As it happens, this is Walter Hobbs (James Caan), a cynical businessman. After a DNA test proves this, Walter reluctantly attempts to start a relationship with the childlike Buddy with increasingly chaotic results.

title: CINEXPÉRIMENTAUX: A MEETING WITH ABIGAIL CHILD
description: Part of Michel Amarger and Frédérique Devaux’s ongoing series of documentary portraits of those who further the cause of experimental cinema in the 21st century (other subjects have included the filmmakers Nicolas Rey, Rose Lowder, and Stephen Dwoskin, as well as scholars, distributors, and curators such as Vivian Ostrovsky, Pip Chodorov, the Light Cone cooperative, and others), A MEETING WITH ABIGAIL CHILD represents a deep dive into the life and work of Child. Encompassing several in-depth interviews, copious footage from her films past and present, and revealing glimpses of the artist at work, the documentary is an essential supplement to Child’s own filmography.

title: THIRD AVENUE: ONLY THE STRONG SURVIVE
description: “This Emmy Award-winning documentary tells the stories of six ‘ordinary’ people who live or work along New York City’s Third Avenue, which runs for sixteen miles through Manhattan, Brooklyn, and the Bronx, cutting through the complex social strata of the city to reveal wildly different economic and ethnic subcultures. The subjects speak for themselves, offering candid glimpses into the disparate worlds of a junkyard dealer who steals cars, a Bowery denizen and the wife he abandoned, a welfare mother living in a condemned building with her five children, a sex worker, a devout Puerto Rican factory worker, and an aging Italian barber and his wife. This unsentimental portrait of the uncommon lives of common people is a subjective sociological study of survival in urban America.” –DCTV

title: LIAF: Closing Night Gala - The Best of the Fest (18*)
description: The judges have deliberated, the audience votes have been added up and we’ve pulled together a final programme that celebrates the highlights of what has been filling the screen all week.

title: The Holdovers
description: From acclaimed director Alexander Payne, THE HOLDOVERS follows a curmudgeonly instructor (Paul Giamatti) at a prestigious American school who is forced to remain on campus during Christmas break to babysit the handful of students with nowhere to go. Eventually he forms an unlikely bond with one of them -- a damaged, brainy troublemaker (newcomer Dominic Sessa) -- and with the school’s head cook, who has just lost a son in Vietnam (Da’Vine Joy Randolph).

title: PRECIPICE (FILMMAKER IN PERSON!)
description: A profoundly working-class community with an intense connection to its land and water is transformed into a pleasure paradise for the wealthy…all while the ground slips into the sea. The new film by moving-image artist, writer, and poet Abigail Child – a leading figure of the generation of experimental filmmakers that emerged in the late 1970s-early 1980s – PRECIPICE focuses on the intersection between climate change and a changing shore community’s response to this global emergency. It’s been decades since fishing, the engine of Nova Scotia’s last 200 years, collapsed. The result: numerous jobs dried up for independent offshore fishermen. A gold rush on the land fills the vacuum, a double-edged sword of economic activity and environmental deterioration. PRECIPICE documents these challenges and explores how community members work to mitigate the human impact: building back the eroding drumlins, creating oyster farms in local bays, practicing regenerative farming, woodlot conservation and organizing the community to buy land to preserve extant wetlands. “On Nova Scotia’s South Shore, where fishing once shaped the communities, new pressures are shifting the landscape. PRECIPICE points the lens at Rose Bay, and up river, tracing the fragile edge between memory and disappearance, as working-class lives are recast against rising seas and fancy coastal development. Echoes of old home movies, Mi’kmaq tales, and present-day restoration (including oyster farming, wetland preservation, woodlot management) interweave into a portrait of resilience.” –Walter Forsyth, LUNENBURG DOC FEST

title: WHAT IS THE CITY: DEAN + NEWSREEL + DANSKA
description: Josephine Hayes Dean THE REBUILDING OF MASCOT FLATS 1992, 59 min, 16mm. Archival print courtesy of the Reserve Film and Video Collection of The New York Public Library for the Performing Arts. “This is a moving story about a group of homeless New Yorkers who set out to renovate an abandoned tenement building. Helped by Habitat for Humanity, including Jimmy Carter, the participants become proficient carpenters and tenant-owners. This group of ethnically diverse people overcomes bureaucracy, skepticism, and lack of money to attain finally a decent affordable place to live.” –ALEXANDER STREET Newsreel THE CASE AGAINST LINCOLN CENTER (Newsreel #17) 1968, 12 min, 16mm-to-DCP More than 20,000 Latino families were displaced to make way for Lincoln Center, home to the Metropolitan Opera and the New York Symphony. This film examines the patrons of the art complex (corporations and wealthy families) and the culture displayed there. Juxtaposing the atmosphere of Lincoln Center with the vibrant street culture of a displaced neighborhood, the film correctly predicts the process by which the West Side was to be turned into a high-rent area for the upper middle class. Herbert Danska UPTOWN: PORTRAIT OF THE SOUTH BRONX 1965, 29 min, 16mm. Print courtesy of the Reserve Film and Video Collection of the New York Public Library for the Performing Arts; preserved with funding from the New York State Library, Division of Library Development. A study of a disadvantaged community within the city, situated in a triangle at the southern tip of the Bronx, UPTOWN includes scenes of tenements, streets, parks, churches, markets, dance halls, and playgrounds, revealing the way of life of its people, their desperation and their hope. Total running time: ca. 105 min.

title: EVERY CONTACT LEAVES A TRACE
description: “For most of her life, filmmaker Lynne Sachs has saved every business card ever placed into her hand – more than 600 fragments of chance encounters, fleeting conversations, and unexpected connections. Drawing on the forensic principle that every contact leaves a trace, Sachs selects seven cards and follows them back into the lives they represent. A German woman reckons with history, an artist reflects on government surveillance, a forensic scientist searches the cards for DNA, and when memory reaches its limits, cinema fills in the gaps. Blending documentary, speculation, performance, and personal reflection with remarkable grace, Sachs transforms an ordinary archive into a meditation on memory, history, and the invisible ways we shape one another’s lives.” –Bryan Wendorf, CHICAGO UNDERGROUND FILM FESTIVAL “Sachs reveals her strength: she captures beauty in the mundane, elevates the casual to poetry, and shows that even the most fleeting encounter leaves a lasting legacy.” –Martijn Smit, CINEMAGAZINE “Sachs extends the interpersonal scale of her inquiry into a more expansive awareness. Her on-screen interlocutors serve as mirrors into her own wandering mind, a gesture toward entanglement reminiscent of Chris Marker’s reflexive SANS SOLEIL. With Sachs, we learn that to be in relation is to come to terms with one’s capacity to do harm and to accept that we might leave imprints that elude our awareness entirely.” –Delaney Holton, SCREEN SLATE “A deeply personal meditation on memory, history, and chance encounters that exemplifies Sachs’s uniquely lyrical approach to nonfiction filmmaking.” –SCREEN MAGAZINE Lynne Sachs will be here in person for all screenings! She will be joined in conversation by the following guests: Fri, Dec 4 7:00 - David Schwartz Sat, Dec 5 5:30 - Stephen Vitiello with film participants Viva and Felix Torres Sun, Dec 6 8:00 - Jessica Bardsley Mon, Dec 7 6:30 - Brydie O’Conner 8:45 - Su Friedrich Wed, Dec 9 6:30 - Rabbi Ellen Lippmann 8:45 - Lee Ann Brown

Brazil
description: Low-level bureaucrat Sam Lowry escapes the monotony of his day-to-day life through a recurring daydream of himself as a virtuous hero saving a beautiful damsel. Investigating a case that led to the wrongful arrest and eventual death of an innocent man instead of wanted terrorist Harry Tuttle, he meets the woman from his daydream, and in trying to help her gets caught in a web of mistaken identities, mindless bureaucracy and lies.

title: The Apartment
description: Insurance worker C.C. Baxter (Jack Lemmon) lends his Upper West Side apartment to company bosses to use for extramarital affairs. When his manager Mr. Sheldrake (Fred MacMurray) begins using Baxter's apartment in exchange for promoting him, Baxter is disappointed to learn that Sheldrake's mistress is Fran Kubelik (Shirley MacLaine), the elevator girl at work whom Baxter is interested in himself. Soon Baxter must decide between the girl he loves and the advancement of his career.

title: Samson et Dalila
description: Sacred, scandalous, and irresistibly alluring, Saint-Saëns’s spectacular take on the biblical hero of legendary strength and the seductive Philistine whose beauty overpowers him returns in the Met’s larger-than-life production.

title: Krampus
description: Frustrated by the constant quarrel between the members of his dysfunctional family, Max loses interest to celebrate Christmas, awakening Krampus, a demon who will punish his entire family.

title: Tokyo Godfathers
description: Middle-aged alcoholic Gin, teenage runaway Miyuki and former drag queen Hana are a trio of homeless people surviving as a makeshift family on the streets of Tokyo. While rummaging in the trash for food on Christmas Eve, they stumble upon an abandoned newborn baby in a trash bin. With only a handful of clues to the baby's identity, the three misfits search the streets of Tokyo for help in returning the baby to its parents.

title: Ken Russell's The Devils: The Director's Cut
description: Censored for over half a century, Ken Russell’s film returns in a landmark director’s cut reconstruction that reveals the full power of his original vision. Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, accused of bewitching a convent of nuns, The Devils lays bare the collusion of church and state through a searing vision of religious persecution, collective hysteria and institutional corruption. The restoration many believed would never happen reaffirms Russell’s incendiary masterpiece as among the most overwhelming and uncompromising achievements in British cinema. Assembled from original camera negative, this 4k restoration is Ken Russell’s 2004 preferred edit. Picture and sound restoration by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color and Warner Bros. Sound.

title: Wake in Fright - 4K Restoration
description: After finishing up the school term in a remote outback town, teacher John Grant (Gary Bond) looks forward to spending his holiday with his girlfriend in Sydney. But John gets waylaid in a mining town where a gambling spree leaves him completely broke. He quickly falls in with the hard-drinking locals, who constantly ply him with alcohol and force him to participate in a gruesome kangaroo hunt. Disgusted, John tries to hitchhike out of town and, when that fails, begins to contemplate suicide.

title: CHILDCARE + BREAK AND ENTER
description: Bonnie Friedman & Karen Mitnik / Newsreel CHILDCARE: PEOPLE’S LIBERATION (Newsreel #56) 1970, 20 min, 16mm-to-DCP Focusing on the need for childcare, this film interviews women who express their desperation to find a safe environment for their children, and shows them taking positive action. Filming in daycare centers, it records what good parent-controlled daycare could mean for children as well as parents. “Being activist filmmakers, we were interested in showing everyday people taking control of their situation by utilizing empty community space to set up their daycare centers. Using equipment shared amongst several projects within the Newsreel collective, we shot mostly on the streets of New York City with a Bolex and Nagra for sound.” –Bonnie Friedman and Karen Mitnik Newsreel BREAK AND ENTER aka SQUATTERS / ROMPIENDO PUERTAS (Newsreel #62) 1971, 42 min, 16mm-to-DCP This film captures the militant antecedents to the housing reclamation movement in New York City. In 1970, several hundred Puerto Rican and Dominican families reclaimed housing left vacant by the city. They pulled the boards off the doors, cleaned and repaired the buildings, and moved in. BREAK AND ENTER documents the activist work of Operation Move-In and the city’s attempts to displace the families. Total running time: ca. 65 min.

title: BRAVE NEW YORK
description: “BRAVE NEW YORK is a free-form documentary that loosely chronicles the last 12 years [as of 2004] of intense change in the East Village ‘hood.’ From the reopening of a newly curfewed Tompkins Square Park and Wigstock in ’92, to the destruction of the cherished Loisaida Community Gardens, to the yuppie invasions of the dot com years, to the present era, indelibly stamped with post 9/11 grief, this durable, lusty neighborhood survives in spite of a real estate gold rush that has excluded all but the well-to-do. The movie’s main voices are those of the artists and street people whose wisdom and commentaries upon the dominant culture give us pause amidst the speedy approach of a ‘Brave New World.’” –Richard Sandler

title: Eyes Wide Shut
description: Stanley Kubrick's daring last film is many things. It is a compelling psychosexual journey. A haunting dreamscape. A riveting tale of suspense. A major milestone in the careers of stars Tom Cruise and Nicole Kidman. And "a worthy final chapter to a great director's career" (Roger Ebert). Cruise plays Dr William Hartford, who plunges into an erotic foray that threatens his marriage - and may even ensnare him in a lurid murder mystery - after his wife's (Kidman) admission of sexual longings. As the story sweeps from doubt and fear to self-discovery and reconciliation, Kubrick orchestrates it with masterful flourishes. Graceful tracking shots, controlled pacing, rich colours, startling images: bravura traits that make Kubrick a filmmaker for the ages are here to keep everyone's eyes wide shut.

title: Black Christmas (1974)
description: As winter break begins, a group of sorority sisters, including Jess (Olivia Hussey) and the often inebriated Barb (Margot Kidder), starts receiving anonymous, lascivious phone calls. Initially, Barb eggs the caller on, but stops when he responds threateningly. Soon, Barb's friend Clare (Lynne Griffin) goes missing from the sorority house, and a local adolescent girl is murdered, leading the girls to suspect a serial killer is on the loose. But no one realises just how near the culprit is.

title: Amelie - 25th Anniversary
description: 23-year-old Amélie is lonely. After an isolating childhood, she moves to Paris and becomes a waitress at the Café des Deux Moulins, a bar restaurant filled with a colourful cast of diners and employees. One night, Amélie happens across a box of treasures hidden in her apartment, left by a little boy in the Fifties, that changes the course of her life. Henceforth, she dedicates herself to giving back to her community, tracking down the owner of these keepsakes, consoling a widowed neighbour and befriending a reclusive artist. When completing these good deeds, she crosses paths with Nino, a photobooth collagist who shares her oddball sensibilities. She quickly falls in love with him.

title: In The Mood For Love
description: In 1962 Hong Kong, neighbors Su Li-zhen (Mrs. Chan) and Chow Mo-wan (Mr. Chow) discover their spouses are having an affair. As they spend time together, they develop feelings for each other, but their relationship remains chaste and unspoken, reflecting societal constraints and their own moral compass.

title: Carol
description: Aspiring photographer Therese spots the beautiful, elegant Carol perusing the doll displays in a 1950s Manhattan department store. The two women develop a fast bond that becomes a love with complicated consequences.

title: Casablanca
description: Rick Blaine (Humphrey Bogart), who owns a nightclub in Casablanca, discovers his old flame Ilsa (Ingrid Bergman) is in town with her husband, Victor Laszlo (Paul Henreid). Laszlo is a famed rebel, and with Germans on his tail, Ilsa knows Rick can help them get out of the country.

title: URBAN VIDEO PROJECT
description: “Urban Video Project (UVP) [was] a media education program [that ran] at Satellite Academy (Forsyth St.) from the mid-1980s through the 90s, providing students with the opportunity to craft half-hour documentaries as a cultural preservation effort, exploring the culture of Black and Latino people in their communities and the legacy of the African diaspora. Started by Salvatore LaSpada, a philanthropic consultant, Urban Video Project became integral to school culture at Satellite. It was emblematic of everything they were about: raising interest in learning and commitment to school through alternative pedagogy, hands-on, immersive experiences, one-on-one instruction, and allowing the students to be in control. […] The mission of these documentaries was twofold: to engage the students in school through media production, allowing them ‘to be the tellers of their stories,’ as LaSpada puts it, and to preserve the cultural heritage and current community of Black and Latino people in New York.” –Maddie DeLaere, XFR Collective This program includes three tapes made by the students at the Lower East Side’s Satellite Academy as part of the Urban Video Project initiative, which have been preserved thanks to the efforts of the XFR Collective, Liz Andersen, and Salvatore LaSpada. NEW YORK, WEST INDIES: VOICES FROM THE JAMAICAN AND TRINIDADIAN MIGRATION 1986, 17 min, video High school students of the Urban Video Project in New York City interview immigrants from Jamaica and Trinidad. EL PASAJE: RECOLLECTIONS FROM THE PUERTO RICAN MIGRATION 1986, 22.5 min, video Interviewing the city’s Puerto Rican residents, the students learn about their history and the history of their classmates. EYES ON HARLEM 1987, 29 min, video In this tape, the students look at the community of Harlem in the mid 1980s as one of the legacies of the African Diaspora. They learn about present aspects of Harlem and the threat of hostile outside developers. Total running time: ca. 75 min. Introduced by Paige Laino (XFR Collective)!

title: PRECIPICE (FILMMAKER IN PERSON!)
description: A profoundly working-class community with an intense connection to its land and water is transformed into a pleasure paradise for the wealthy…all while the ground slips into the sea. The new film by moving-image artist, writer, and poet Abigail Child – a leading figure of the generation of experimental filmmakers that emerged in the late 1970s-early 1980s – PRECIPICE focuses on the intersection between climate change and a changing shore community’s response to this global emergency. It’s been decades since fishing, the engine of Nova Scotia’s last 200 years, collapsed. The result: numerous jobs dried up for independent offshore fishermen. A gold rush on the land fills the vacuum, a double-edged sword of economic activity and environmental deterioration. PRECIPICE documents these challenges and explores how community members work to mitigate the human impact: building back the eroding drumlins, creating oyster farms in local bays, practicing regenerative farming, woodlot conservation and organizing the community to buy land to preserve extant wetlands. “On Nova Scotia’s South Shore, where fishing once shaped the communities, new pressures are shifting the landscape. PRECIPICE points the lens at Rose Bay, and up river, tracing the fragile edge between memory and disappearance, as working-class lives are recast against rising seas and fancy coastal development. Echoes of old home movies, Mi’kmaq tales, and present-day restoration (including oyster farming, wetland preservation, woodlot management) interweave into a portrait of resilience.” –Walter Forsyth, LUNENBURG DOC FEST

title: Home Alone 2 : Lost in New York
description: Instead of flying to Florida with his folks, Kevin ends up alone in New York, where he gets a hotel room with his dad’s credit card—despite problems from a clerk and meddling bellboy. But when Kevin runs into his old nemeses, the Wet Bandits, he’s determined to foil their plans to rob a toy store on Christmas eve.

title: WRECK OF THE NEW YORK SUBWAYS + SUBWAY CITY
description: Julia Reichert / Newsreel THE WRECK OF THE NEW YORK SUBWAYS (Newsreel #47) 1969, 16 min, 16mm-to-DCP During the winter of 1969, the New York Transit Authority increased the public transportation fare from 20 cents to 30 cents – a 50% increase. Infuriated riders scrambled under turnstiles and through exit doors, refusing to pay. In this film riders and subway workers denounce the terrible conditions and constant fare increases. The film analyzes the vicious cycle of bonding the Transit Authority, which profits the banks at the expense of the taxpayers. Nick Lord & Ian Stuttard SUBWAY CITY 1993, 50 min, DCP “Three and a half million travelers use the New York subway system every day. Briefcase wielding city workers share their morning rides with peddlers, street musicians, the down and out, pickpockets, and drug addicts. This film explores the underground world in all its diversity, from the frenetic rush hour traffic to the eerie solitude of early morning runs. Besides those who merely use the subway as transportation, there are those who work there, those who live there, and those who commit crimes there.” –ALEXANDER STREET Total running time: ca. 70 min.

title: Preschool Pics: Wintry Worlds (U*)
description: Join Saskia van Roomen and the team from Small World Cinema to create festive decorations themed around this bumper crop of short stories set in wintry worlds.

title: Your Name [Kimi no Na wa.]
description: Two teenagers share a profound, magical connection upon discovering they are swapping bodies. Things manage to become even more complicated when the boy and girl decide to meet in person.

title: Yi Yi
description: The extraordinary, internationally embraced Yi Yi (A One and a Two . . .), directed by the late Taiwanese master Edward Yang, follows a middle-class family in Taipei over the course of one year, beginning with a wedding and ending with a funeral. Whether chronicling middle-age father NJ’s tentative flirtations with an old flame or precocious young son Yang-Yang’s attempts at capturing reality with his beloved camera, the filmmaker deftly imbues every gorgeous frame with a compassionate clarity. Warm, sprawling, and dazzling, this intimate epic is one of the undisputed masterworks of the new century. 4K digital restoration carried out by Pony Canyon Inc., with analog and digital processes provided by Imagica Entertainment Media Services, Inc.

title: The Night Before
description: Ethan, Isaac and Chris are best friends who have celebrated every Christmas Eve together. Things take a turn when Isaac and Chris decide to end their decade-long tradition.

title: The Shop Around the Corner
description: Alfred Kralik (James Stewart) and Klara Novak (Margaret Sullavan) are employees at Matuschek and Company, a general store in Budapest. Klara and Alfred are constantly at odds with each other, butting heads and disagreeing on almost everything. Both are enamored of their respective pen pals, who serve as welcome distractions in their lives. Little do they know, they are each the other's pen pal and, despite outward differences, have unwittingly fallen in love through their letters.

title: WHAT IS THE CITY: NYC BUSINESSES
description: This program gathers together a selection of film and video works that highlight how important New York’s businesses are for the life of the city: not only economically or commercially, but as sites that knit together communities, provide spaces to gather, give a sense of purpose to their proprietors, and develop and maintain the cultural and social traditions that give meaning to the lives of the city’s residents. The program includes films about the arts of bagel making and cigar rolling, about beloved institutions threatened by development (such as the legendary Times Square sideshow emporium, Hubert’s, and the Upper West Side’s horse-riding stables), and about eccentric businesses such as the Staten Island bicycle-cum-junk shop run by Barry Braverman’s father, which Braverman’s film MURITA CYCLES shows to be less a viable commercial endeavor than a means for self-expression. Nick Manning HOT BAGELS (1979, 16 min, video) Rhody Streeter & Tony Ganz HUBERT’S (1972, 6 min, 16mm) Rhody Streeter CLAREMONT STABLES (1972, 9 min, 16mm) Karen L. Kramer THE LAST OF THE NEW YORK CIGAR ROLLERS (1990, 13 min, 16mm-to-DCP) Barry Braverman MURITA CYCLES (1978, 28 min, 16mm-to-DCP) Total running time: ca. 75 min.

title: EVERY CONTACT LEAVES A TRACE
description: “For most of her life, filmmaker Lynne Sachs has saved every business card ever placed into her hand – more than 600 fragments of chance encounters, fleeting conversations, and unexpected connections. Drawing on the forensic principle that every contact leaves a trace, Sachs selects seven cards and follows them back into the lives they represent. A German woman reckons with history, an artist reflects on government surveillance, a forensic scientist searches the cards for DNA, and when memory reaches its limits, cinema fills in the gaps. Blending documentary, speculation, performance, and personal reflection with remarkable grace, Sachs transforms an ordinary archive into a meditation on memory, history, and the invisible ways we shape one another’s lives.” –Bryan Wendorf, CHICAGO UNDERGROUND FILM FESTIVAL “Sachs reveals her strength: she captures beauty in the mundane, elevates the casual to poetry, and shows that even the most fleeting encounter leaves a lasting legacy.” –Martijn Smit, CINEMAGAZINE “Sachs extends the interpersonal scale of her inquiry into a more expansive awareness. Her on-screen interlocutors serve as mirrors into her own wandering mind, a gesture toward entanglement reminiscent of Chris Marker’s reflexive SANS SOLEIL. With Sachs, we learn that to be in relation is to come to terms with one’s capacity to do harm and to accept that we might leave imprints that elude our awareness entirely.” –Delaney Holton, SCREEN SLATE “A deeply personal meditation on memory, history, and chance encounters that exemplifies Sachs’s uniquely lyrical approach to nonfiction filmmaking.” –SCREEN MAGAZINE Lynne Sachs will be here in person for all screenings! She will be joined in conversation by the following guests: Fri, Dec 4 7:00 - David Schwartz Sat, Dec 5 5:30 - Stephen Vitiello with film participants Viva and Felix Torres Sun, Dec 6 8:00 - Jessica Bardsley Mon, Dec 7 6:30 - Brydie O’Conner 8:45 - Su Friedrich Wed, Dec 9 6:30 - Rabbi Ellen Lippmann 8:45 - Lee Ann Brown

title: BILL MOYERS JOURNAL: ROSEDALE: THE WAY IT IS
description: Amid the recession of the early 1970s, Black families began moving into nearly all-white Rosedale, a working-class Queens neighborhood just across the border from wealthy Nassau County. This film documents the explosive racist violence that followed: Tony and Glenda Spencer, a Black mother and father whose house was bombed twice but who refused to leave, anchor the film. “We’re going to stay here,” Glenda says. “Definitely going to stay.” (They did; as of 2019, she still lived in her home.) Moyers also follows a “home referral service” calling itself R.O.A.R. (Return Our American Rights) that aimed to keep Black people from becoming property owners in Rosedale, while moonlighting as a white supremacist terrorist gang. ROSEDALE was given a second life in 2019 when Sola Olosunde, a Hunter College graduate student in urban planning, sent out a viral tweet featuring the film’s most grotesque sequence, in which several Black children are assaulted by a group of white children. “Black and white alike in the Rosedales of America have been abandoned, condemned together to economic apartheid by a system that rewards the people who can afford to get out, and condemns to bitter, consuming rivalry those left behind,” Moyers opines. “It’s a travesty.”

title: You've Got Mail
description: Struggling boutique bookseller Kathleen Kelly (Meg Ryan) hates Joe Fox (Tom Hanks), the owner of a corporate Foxbooks chain store that just moved in across the street. When they meet online, however, they begin an intense and anonymous Internet romance, oblivious of each other's true identity. Eventually Joe learns that the enchanting woman he's involved with is actually his business rival. He must now struggle to reconcile his real-life dislike for her with the cyber love he's come to feel.

title: Lost, Banned, Reclaimed: The Night of Counting the Years
The Holdovers
description: From acclaimed director Alexander Payne, THE HOLDOVERS follows a curmudgeonly instructor (Paul Giamatti) at a prestigious American school who is forced to remain on campus during Christmas break to babysit the handful of students with nowhere to go. Eventually he forms an unlikely bond with one of them -- a damaged, brainy troublemaker (newcomer Dominic Sessa) -- and with the school’s head cook, who has just lost a son in Vietnam (Da’Vine Joy Randolph).

title: Love Actually
description: Nine intertwined stories examine the complexities of the one emotion that connects us all: love. Among the characters explored are David (Hugh Grant), the handsome newly elected British prime minister who falls for a young junior staffer (Martine McCutcheon), Sarah (Laura Linney), a graphic designer whose devotion to her mentally ill brother complicates her love life, and Harry (Alan Rickman), a married man tempted by his attractive new secretary.

title: The Nightmare Before Christmas
description: The film follows the misadventures of Jack Skellington, Halloweentown's beloved pumpkin king, who has become bored with the same annual routine of frightening people in the "real world." When Jack accidentally stumbles on Christmastown, all bright colors and warm spirits, he gets a new lease on life -- he plots to bring Christmas under his control by kidnapping Santa Claus and taking over the role. But Jack soon discovers even the best-laid plans of mice and skeleton men can go seriously awry.

title: Meet Me in St. Louis
description: In the year before the 1904 St Louis World's Fair, the four Smith daughters, who are attached to their ways of life, reluctantly prepare to move to New York when their father gets a transfer.

title: National Lampoon's Christmas Vacation
description: * ON SALE 1st DECEMBER * As the holidays approach, Clark Griswold (Chevy Chase) wants to have a perfect family Christmas, so he pesters his wife, Ellen (Beverly D'Angelo), and children, as he tries to make sure everything is in line, including the tree and house decorations. However, things go awry quickly. His hick cousin, Eddie (Randy Quaid), and his family show up unplanned and start living in their camper on the Griswold property. Even worse, Clark's employers renege on the holiday bonus he needs.

title: BLACK WOMEN’S HANDS
description: This program surrounds JOJOLO with depictions of Black women artists. Sarah Maldoror’s TOTO BISSAINTHE (1984) chronicles her long-time friend and co-conspirator, the titular Haitian singer, in both the exteriority of performance and subjectivity of the backstage. HANDS OF INGE (1962) celebrates the sculptural craft of Ruth Inge Hardison and was edited by Hortense “Tee” Beveridge, the first Black woman to work as a unionized film editor. The 1962 documentary is among the rich constellation of citations in Simone Leigh and Madeleine Hunt-Ehrlich’s CONSPIRACY (2022), a spellbinding mediation on the artistry, manual skill, and aesthetic labor of Black women across forms. Lebert Bethune & John Taylor JOJOLO 1966, 22 min, 16mm. Collection of the Smithsonian National Museum of African American History and Culture. Sarah Maldoror TOTO BISSAINTHE 1984, 4 min, 16mm-to-DCP John W. Fletcher HANDS OF INGE 1962, 10 min, 16mm. Collection of the Smithsonian National Museum of African American History and Culture. Simone Leigh & Madeleine Hunt-Ehrlich CONSPIRACY 2022, 25 min, DCP Total running time: ca. 65 min.

title: #7 TRAIN + CHINATOWN + TOURIST BUSES GO HOME!
description: Hye Jung Park & J.T. Takagi THE # 7 TRAIN: AN IMMIGRANT JOURNEY 1999, 28 min, DCP Every day 500,000 people from 117 different countries ride a subway that runs from Flushing to Times Square, going through Queens, the most culturally diverse region in the United States. This documentary follows four immigrant passengers: a Korean who works in Harlem, two Otavalen street vendors who work near Chinatown, and a gay Pakistani sari salesman on Fifth Avenue. Their lives and their conflicted relationships with the city and its other residents are juxtaposed with the subway they take each day to Manhattan and their dreams for the future. Jon Alpert & Keiko Tsuno CHINATOWN: IMMIGRANTS IN AMERICA 1980, 27 min, DCP “Produced in response to what DCTV felt were inaccurate media portrayals of New York City’s Chinatown, this award-winning, often startling portrait of an immigrant community probes beneath the tourist’s-eye view to uncover the complexity of an inner-city subculture plagued by poverty and exploitation. ‘This is the story of our neighbors,’ says Alpert. His sympathetic ‘reportage from within’ reveals kitchen workers earning less than $100 for sixty-hour weeks, rents that are among the highest in the city, and garment workers laboring for minimum wages in unsafe conditions. Focusing on individual stories to expose broader issues, this is an unflinching document of Asian immigrants under pressure to assimilate into mainstream culture and struggling to survive in America.” –ELECTRONIC ARTS INTERMIX Tom Tam TOURIST BUSES GO HOME! 1969, 10 min, DCP In this short film – one of the earliest examples of Asian American experimental film – Tom Tam follows the activism and protests against tours of Manhattan’s Chinatown. Total running time: ca. 70 min.

title: Barry Lyndon
description: Stanley Kubrick bent the conventions of the historical drama to his own will in this dazzling vision of a pitiless aristocracy, adapted from a novel by William Makepeace Thackeray. In picaresque detail, Barry Lyndon chronicles the adventures of an incorrigible trickster (Ryan O’Neal) whose opportunism takes him from an Irish farm to the battlefields of the Seven Years’ War and the parlours of high society. For the most sumptuously crafted film of his career, Kubrick recreated the decadent surfaces and intricate social codes of the period, evoking the light and texture of eighteenth-century painting with the help of pioneering cinematographic techniques and lavish costume and production design, all of which earned Academy Awards. The result is a masterpiece—a sardonic, devastating portrait of a vanishing world whose opulence conceals the moral vacancy at its heart. Please Note: The film will be presented with a brief 5-10min intermission.

title: À TOUT PRENDRE
description: “A psychological drama depicting the birth and slow unraveling of a relationship within Montreal’s affluent bohemian circles. In this autobiographical debut feature – made in Quebec using cinéma direct methods and techniques – Claude Jutra reenacts his own romance with Johanne Harrelle. Set in the ‘open’ Montreal of the 1950s and 1960s, the film follows a young man trying to break into the film industry and a young Black woman – an orphan and a married woman – pursuing a modeling career. The two freely engage in a mutual confessional; this game of truth leads Johanne to question Claude about his probable homosexuality. They must also confront the agonizing dilemma of abortion when Johanne becomes pregnant. A slow unraveling of their relationship ensues.” –CINÉMATHÈQUE QUÉBÉCOISE

title: Goodfellas
description: Young Henry Hill (Ray Liotta), with his friends Jimmy (Robert De Niro) and Tommy (Joe Pesci), grows up in the mob and works very hard to advance himself through the ranks. He enjoys his life of money and luxury, but is oblivious to the horror that he causes. A drug addiction and a few mistakes ultimately unravel his climb to the top. Based on the book "Wiseguy" by Nicholas Pileggi.

title: WORLD OF PIRI THOMAS + EL PUEBLO SE LEVANTA
description: NET JOURNAL: THE WORLD OF PIRI THOMAS 1968, 60 min, 16mm-to-digital. Special sequences directed by Gordon Parks; additional photography by Dan Drasin, Paul Glicksberg, Gordon Parks, Jr., and Frank Simon. Digital restoration courtesy of Indiana University Libraries Moving Image Archive. THE WORLD OF PIRI THOMAS depicts life in Spanish Harlem through the eyes – and writings – of Puerto Rican-Cuban poet Piri Thomas, whose memoir “Down These Mean Streets” (1967) had recently become a best-seller. Newsreel EL PUEBLO SE LEVANTA (Newsreel #63) 1971, 42 min, 16mm-to-DCP In the late 1960s, conditions for Puerto Ricans in the U.S. reached a boiling point. Faced with racial discrimination, deficient community services, and poor education and job opportunities, Puerto Rican communities began to address these injustices by using direct action. This film focuses on the community of East Harlem, capturing the compassion and defiance of the Young Lords as they implemented their own health, educational, and public assistance programs and fought back against social injustice. Total running time: ca. 105 min.

title: Tokyo Godfathers
description: Middle-aged alcoholic Gin, teenage runaway Miyuki and former drag queen Hana are a trio of homeless people surviving as a makeshift family on the streets of Tokyo. While rummaging in the trash for food on Christmas Eve, they stumble upon an abandoned newborn baby in a trash bin. With only a handful of clues to the baby's identity, the three misfits search the streets of Tokyo for help in returning the baby to its parents.

title: DIFFERENT IMAGES
description: This program pairs JOJOLO with Alile Sharon Larkin’s 1982 feature, A DIFFERENT IMAGE. Set in Los Angeles, the narrative centers on Alana, an art student, whose incorporation of Afro-diasporic cultural consciousness elaborates a critique of how Eurocentric patriarchal visual standards construct and crossover between commercialized media and intimate relationships. A DIFFERENT IMAGE honors a young Black woman’s multivalent interiority and autonomy over perception. Lebert Bethune & John Taylor JOJOLO 1966, 22 min, 16mm. Collection of the Smithsonian National Museum of African American History and Culture. Alile Sharon Larkin A DIFFERENT IMAGE 1982, 52 min, 16mm. Archival print courtesy of the Academy Film Archive. Total running time: ca. 80 min.

title: THIRD AVENUE: ONLY THE STRONG SURVIVE
description: “This Emmy Award-winning documentary tells the stories of six ‘ordinary’ people who live or work along New York City’s Third Avenue, which runs for sixteen miles through Manhattan, Brooklyn, and the Bronx, cutting through the complex social strata of the city to reveal wildly different economic and ethnic subcultures. The subjects speak for themselves, offering candid glimpses into the disparate worlds of a junkyard dealer who steals cars, a Bowery denizen and the wife he abandoned, a welfare mother living in a condemned building with her five children, a sex worker, a devout Puerto Rican factory worker, and an aging Italian barber and his wife. This unsentimental portrait of the uncommon lives of common people is a subjective sociological study of survival in urban America.” –DCTV

title: Love Actually
description: Nine intertwined stories examine the complexities of the one emotion that connects us all: love. Among the characters explored are David (Hugh Grant), the handsome newly elected British prime minister who falls for a young junior staffer (Martine McCutcheon), Sarah (Laura Linney), a graphic designer whose devotion to her mentally ill brother complicates her love life, and Harry (Alan Rickman), a married man tempted by his attractive new secretary.

title: SIMPLY JOHANNE
description: “Abandoned on the doorstep of a Montreal orphanage, Johanne Harrelle eventually rose to prominence as a gifted artist, actress, and one of North America’s first Black models. SIMPLY JOHANNE deftly explores her complex and audacious life through archival footage, interviews with loved ones, and performances of her writings by three contemporary actresses. The film chronicles the journey of a magnetic and passionate woman who defied the expectations of her time.” –LES FILMS DU 3 MARS

title: Die Hard [is a Christmas Movie]
description: New York City policeman John McClane (Bruce Willis) is visiting his estranged wife (Bonnie Bedelia) and two daughters on Christmas Eve. He joins her at a holiday party in the headquarters of the Japanese-owned business she works for. But the festivities are interrupted by a group of terrorists who take over the exclusive high-rise, and everyone in it. Very soon McClane realizes that there's no one to save the hostages -- but him.

title: NEW YORKERS + BEFORE THE FIRST WORD
description: This program pairs two films, made a decade apart, that vividly demonstrate the vibrant, distinctive, and sometimes paradoxical nature of New York City’s neighborhoods: at once strikingly diverse and worldly, and yet close knit and self-enclosed. NEW YORKERS (1971), by filmmaker Michael Blackwood (who during his long career made several films about the city, as well as dozens of documentaries about artists, architects, and musicians), sets its sights on the Upper East Side, and in particular on the area in and around East 77th Street. BEFORE THE FIRST WORD (1982) – a co-production between WNET and the educational organization Learning Designs, and ostensibly a film designed as a teaching tool for journalism students – is set seventy-something blocks to the south, in Greenwich Village. Both films capture the degree to which their respective neighborhoods have developed specific cultures, institutions, and local networks to create a kind of shelter from the vertiginous, unceasing forces of change that animate Manhattan – and the degree to which they’re nevertheless unmistakably subject to the evolution that is the fate of all city neighborhoods, and to the more aggressive, inorganic tides of gentrification that have increasingly transformed the city over the past fifty years. Michael Blackwood NEW YORKERS 1971, 29 min, 16mm-to-DCP Tom Simon BEFORE THE FIRST WORD 1982, 29 min, video Total running time: ca. 60 min.

title: Elf
description: Buddy (Will Ferrell) was accidentally transported to the North Pole as a toddler and raised to adulthood among Santa's elves. Unable to shake the feeling that he doesn't fit in, the adult Buddy travels to New York, in full elf uniform, in search of his real father. As it happens, this is Walter Hobbs (James Caan), a cynical businessman. After a DNA test proves this, Walter reluctantly attempts to start a relationship with the childlike Buddy with increasingly chaotic results.

title: THE SOCIAL LIFE OF SMALL URBAN SPACES
description: This film emerged from city planner William H. Whyte’s years of research into pedestrian behavior and city dynamics, conducted as part of his Street Life Project. His research resulted both in a film and a book, both of which closely analyzed the functioning of public spaces in various cities, above all in NYC. The book quickly became a classic text within the realm of city planning, and remains beloved not only for the wisdom and elegance of its insights, but for its disarmingly unpretentious, no-nonsense, and often flat-out funny tone. The film version fully embodies all the qualities of the book, and adds one special feature: Whyte’s own voice. Sounding very much like Jimmy Stewart’s city planner cousin, Whyte delivers the narration with an often-self-deprecatory folksiness that’s charmingly at odds with the stentorian tone of most educational films. The film is also effectively a work of street photography. Whyte and his team’s dedication to observing – and recording – the actual behavior of city dwellers, and their sharp eye for the behaviors and gestures that are most revealing of city life, result in a film that is – almost incidentally – a classic city symphony. THE SOCIAL LIFE OF SMALL URBAN SPACES is one of the great films about that strangest of creatures – the city dweller – in its natural habitat.

title: THE SWORD IN THE STONE
description: Disney’s underrated adaptation of the first title in T.H. White’s classic series The Once and Future King relates the coming-of-age of a young King Arthur, here named Wart, and his training by the wizard Merlin. Using the Xerox-transfer technology the studio implemented to great acclaim in its preceding 101 DALMATIANS, THE SWORD IN THE STONE centers on the magical arts of transformation, culminating in an epic battle of Merlin against the evil witch Madam Mim. Preceded by: Georges Méliès LE MAGICIEN (1898, 1 min, 35mm-to-DCP) Like THE SWORD IN THE STONE, George Méliès’s LE MAGICIEN emphasizes mystical metamorphoses. Total running time: ca. 85 min.
director: Wolfgang Reitherman, Clyde Geronimi, and David Hand

title: WHAT IS THE CITY BUT THE PEOPLE?
description: “In 1969 the Department of City Planning attempted to shore up support for its various [development] projects with a multipronged, multimedia public relations blitz. At its center was the publication of a six-volume book, ‘The Plan for New York City’ (1969), which articulated the commissioner’s vision for the metropolis to stem the flight of the middle classes to the suburbs and revitalize urban space. The plan was presented in synopsis form as a propagandistic documentary produced by the Department and co-directed by John Peer Nugent and Gordon Hyatt. Featuring some flashy cinematography from New York location shooter-extraordinaire Arthur J. Ornitz [THE CONNECTION; MINNIE & MOSKOWITZ; SERPICO], WHAT IS THE CITY is an idiosyncratic document of the city in the late 1960s, offering a wide panorama of places and spaces, narrated by one of the plan’s ghost writers, William H. Whyte [THE SOCIAL LIFE OF SMALL URBAN SPACES]. The film flits between footage of and discussion about ‘urban crisis’ (uprisings, poor housing stock, street violence) and purported city-led remedies. Viewed today, the film is both a curious relic of failed urban policy and an index of just how wedded city authorities were (and remain) to the idea that the manipulation of public perception is key to urban governance.” –FILM AT LINCOLN CENTER

Home Alone
description: When bratty 8-year-old Kevin McCallister (Macaulay Culkin) acts out the night before a family trip to Paris, his mother (Catherine O'Hara) makes him sleep in the attic. After the McCallisters mistakenly leave for the airport without Kevin, he awakens to an empty house and assumes his wish to have no family has come true. But his excitement sours when he realizes that two con men (Joe Pesci, Daniel Stern) plan to rob the McCallister residence, and that he alone must protect the family home.

title: WIZARDS
description: Ralph Bakshi’s anti-fascist passion project, developed over decades and released prior to his LORD OF THE RINGS, mixes sci-fi and fantasy to tell the story of a far-future Earth where magic and fairies have returned in the wake of nuclear holocaust. These forces of good must battle an evil wizard who attempts to control the world by reviving the forbidden technologies of war. WIZARDS is pure, unrestrained Bakshi, filled with freaky characters, psychedelic backgrounds, and hallucinatory rotoscoping. Preceded by: Tommy Turner THE MAGICIAN 1998, 9 min, 16mm WIZARDS is paired with Tommy Turner’s THE MAGICIAN, a transgressive take on the rituals of ceremonial magic. Total running time: ca. 95 min.

title: PARADOX ON 72ND STREET
description: Over the course of three years, Gene Searchinger filmed pedestrians, joggers, buskers, bench sitters, stoop sleepers, and countless other types of New Yorker (whom the narration describes as “exaggerated Americans”) at the corner of Broadway and 72nd St. Visually, the film presents an hour-long stream of individuals, each with their own unfathomable inner mindscape, who together comprise “the collective”; the paradox referred to in the title is narrator Lewis Thomas’s assertion that, “It is in our genes to live together and to depend on each other, to be our individual separate selves and at the same time the working parts of others.” Thomas, a biologist and the film’s co-writer, shares narrating duties with the anthropologist Philip Slater, both of whom offer meandering philosophical notes on individualism in American society.

title: Christmas Pyjama Party
description: ALL NIGHTER : FAQs, HOUSE RULES & TIPS THE MUPPET CHRISTMAS CAROL : The Muppets perform the classic Dickens holiday tale, with Kermit the Frog playing Bob Cratchit, the put-upon clerk of stingy Ebenezer Scrooge (Michael Caine). Other Muppets -- Miss Piggy, Gonzo, Fozzie Bear and Sam the Eagle -- weave in and out of the story, while Scrooge receives visits from spirits of three Christmases -- past, present and future. They show him the error of his self-serving ways, but the miserable old man seems to be past any hope of redemption and happiness. ELF : Buddy (Will Ferrell) was accidentally transported to the North Pole as a toddler and raised to adulthood among Santa's elves. Unable to shake the feeling that he doesn't fit in, the adult Buddy travels to New York, in full elf uniform, in search of his real father. As it happens, this is Walter Hobbs (James Caan), a cynical businessman. After a DNA test proves this, Walter reluctantly attempts to start a relationship with the childlike Buddy with increasingly chaotic results. After the McCallisters mistakenly leave for the airport without Kevin, he awakens to an empty house and assumes his wish to have no family has come true. But his excitement sours when he realizes that two con men (Joe Pesci, Daniel Stern) plan to rob the McCallister residence, and that he alone must protect the family home. GREMLINS : A gadget salesman is looking for a special gift for his son and finds one at a store in Chinatown. The shopkeeper is reluctant to sell him the `mogwai' but sells it to him with the warning to never expose him to bright light, water, or to feed him after midnight. All of this happens and the result is a gang of gremlins that decide to tear up the town on Christmas Eve. description: ALL NIGHTER : FAQs, HOUSE RULES & TIPS Peter Jackson's THE LORD OF THE RINGS TRILOGY is back from the rarely screened Theatrical Editions – from 35mm! Join us as we venture back into Middle-earth the way you would have seen the films on release! THE FELLOWSHIP OF THE RING; A meek Hobbit from the Shire and eight companions set out on a journey to destroy the powerful One Ring and save Middle-earth from the Dark Lord Sauron. THE TWO TOWERS; While Frodo and Sam edge closer to Mordor with the help of the shifty Gollum, the divided fellowship makes a stand against Sauron's new ally, Saruman, and his hordes of Isengard. THE RETURN OF THE KING; Gandalf and Aragorn lead the World of Men against Sauron's army to draw his gaze from Frodo and Sam as they approach Mount Doom with the One Ring. ----------------------------------------------------------------------- NO ADMISSIONS TO THE CINEMA AFTER MIDNIGHT NO ALCOHOL PURCHASED FROM OUTSIDE IS PERMITTED IN THE BUILDING! title: THE ORBIT OF MINOR SATELLITES
description: This screening comprises a special NYC sneak preview of the new independent feature film from animator, filmmaker, and performance artist Chris Sullivan, whose experimental film and theater work spans 30 years. THE ORBIT OF MINOR SATELLITES is a doctor-patient story, using hand-drawn animation and live action actors. Through the characters of Durwood Richards, psychiatrist, and his long-time patient Rosemary Hamm, Sullivan investigates love, loss, blame, and forgiveness. In Rosemary’s hallucinations, there is a space station on one of the moons of Saturn, and a giant talking buffalo. As the film flows between the psychiatrist’s office and Rosemary’s imaginary space station world, we all orbit around a larger celestial body of some kind – the most common, strange, unreachable person that we hoped we would be, in orbit around our potential selves. Followed by a Q&A with the artist!

title: EYEWORKS SHORT FILM PGM 1
description: Winston Hacking ACTION BOG (Canada, 2025, 2 min, digital) “Time stretches like soft polymer; metamorphoses creep forward frame by frame, suspiciously slow, as if the film were watching me back.” –Winston Hacking Emma Calder SPRINGFIELD (UK, 1986, 7 min, 16mm-to-digital) “Part woman, part vacuum cleaner, what do these effeminate cyborgs have to say about alienation and the gendered hierarchies we inhabit? A witty and offbeat probing of loss, obsession, desperation, and fear.” –Emma Calder Adebukola Bodunrin LEAKS IN THE LINES (France/U.S., 2026, 4 min, digital) “LEAKS IN THE LINES is a hybrid film combining laser etching, phytograms, and 8mm footage of gardens to explore the tension between organic growth and imposed order.” –Adebukola Bodunrin Chihiro Yamanaka VEILS OF LANDSCAPE / / 霞始めてたなびく (Japan, 2025, 5 min, digital) “The east wind begins to blow, carrying warmth into the water. Landscapes merge without boundaries, and in time, the mountains drift into slumber.” –Chihiro Yamanaka JoAnn Gillerman ORCHID (U.S., 1985, 3 min, digital) “Technology meets sensuality as associations of gender are transposed into a yin/yang of unexpected androgyny. Computer graphics, live video and fluid hand drawn frame-by-frame fracturing animations create unique abstracted forms with unlikely pairings of living orchids, human form, nature and technology.” –JoAnn Gillerman Shana Moulton THE UNDISCOVERED DRAWER (U.S., 2013, 9 min, digital) A series of nested drawers opens for Cynthia, leading her on another journey of self-realization. Sara Petty PRELUDES IN MAGICAL TIME (U.S., 1987, 4 min, 16mm-to-digital) “The [film’s] imagery alludes to a window and curtains dancing in a breeze, which creates a structural element throughout the animation, as it drifts and unfolds into completely non-objective forms.” –VCU SCHOLARS COMPASS Emile Cohl ART’S INFANCY / L’ENFANCE DE L’ART (France, 1910, 4 min, 35mm-to-digital. Piano score by Andrew Dorsett.) “Created before cels were used in animation, this film blended techniques of hand-drawn linework, paper cut-outs, trick photography, human pixilation, and mixed-media live-action into a single experimental short film which explores imagined origins of creativity.” –EYEWORKS Çağıl Harmandar VISION (Japan/Turkey, 2023, 7 min, digital) “Eyes are magical spheres that make up dreams and retain memories. In our eyes, the visions of the within and of the beyond overlap. New worlds come to be when our gazes meet.” –Çağıl Harmandar Julian Antonisz WHAT DO WE SEE AFTER CLOSING OUR EYES AND COVERING OUR EARS (Poland, 1978, 5 min, 35mm-to-digital) One of a series of films Antonisz made using his “pantograf-animograf,” an ingenious mechanical device that scales drawings down to the size of a film frame and mechanically animates transformations between drawings. Ruth Peyser GO TO HELL (U.S., 1994, 8 min, 16mm) “After a fight with her boyfriend, a woman falls through a hole in the stairs into a hellish fantasy world where she is confronted by a series of terrifying situations. When she emerges, her fear turns to anger, giving her the courage to fight back. Along the way, she discovers the power and exhilaration of finding her voice.” –Ruth Peyser Kevin Eskew ENSMOOTHENING (U.S., 2026, 12 min, digital) “Visualize an Earth of such tranquility and peace in nature that it must be the true marvel of all the ages. A land for forever, smoothened and sterilized. That’s the Dream! Yes! A smooth plastic-coated marble world!” –Kevin Eskew Total running time: ca. 75 min.

title: EYEWORKS SHORT FILM PGM 2
description: Sandor Reisenbuchler FAREWELL, LITTLE ISLAND / ISTEN VELED, KIS SZIGET (Hungary, 1987, 12 min, 35mm-to-digital) “A short animation depicting the drowning of a village by modern technology.” –NATIONAL FILM INSTITUTE HUNGARY Fanny Sorgo & Eva Pedroza TAKO TSUBO (Austria/Germany, 2024, 6 min, digital) “Mr. Ham decides to have his heart removed in order to be relieved of his complicated feelings. The doctor assures him that this is no longer a problem at all in this day and age. However, Ham keeps his heart for a while after the removal in order to perhaps understand it better after all. TAKO TSUBO is an animated, surrealistic reflection on dealing with feelings in a meritocracy.” –SIXPACKFILM Jeff Carpenter & Mary Lambert RAPID EYE MOVEMENTS (U.S., 1977, 11 min, 16mm-to-digital) “An obscured world of night lives, eavesdropped phone calls, and philosophical romantic musings.” –Jeff Carpenter & Mary Lambert Alexandre Alagôa XYZ (Luxembourg, 2026, 12 min, digital. Contains strobing imagery.) “An obsessive exploration of the three geometric dimensions in hopes of reaching a fourth. Created by shooting with a camera on a tripod throughout the halls of a building where the filmmaker used to work.” –Alexandre Alagôa Lewis Klahr ALTAIR (U.S., 1995, 7 min, 16mm-to-digital) “ALTAIR offers a cutout animation version of color film noir. The images were culled from six, late forties issues of Cosmopolitan magazine and set to an almost 4-minute segment of Stravinsky’s ‘Firebird’ to create a sinister, perfumed world. The viewer is encouraged to speculate on the nature and details of the woman’s battle with large, malevolent societal forces and her descent into an alcoholic swoon.” –Lewis Klahr Caibei Cai SLIVER CAVE / 银幕 (China, 2021, 14 min, digital) “Stepping into a cave, the sight fluctuates by the firelight. Left to right, top to bottom. The same goes for the screen in front of you. It is a borderless tunnel, presenting domestication and desire. –Caibei Cai Ida Lasic MOLLY DANE (U.S., 2020, 6 min, digital) “Experience the ritz and glamour of a death at the Dane’s fundraiser.” –Ida Lasic Amy Kravitz RIVER LETHE (U.S., 1985, 7 min, 16mm-to-digital) A non-narrative and abstract visual poem in five parts. Its title refers to the underworld river of forgetfulness. The drawings are created from non-traditional animation media including rubbed and erased graphite, pigment, and aluminum powders to make an animate surface of unusual richness. Total running time: ca. 80 min.

title: Love Actually
description: Nine intertwined stories examine the complexities of the one emotion that connects us all: love. Among the characters explored are David (Hugh Grant), the handsome newly elected British prime minister who falls for a young junior staffer (Martine McCutcheon), Sarah (Laura Linney), a graphic designer whose devotion to her mentally ill brother complicates her love life, and Harry (Alan Rickman), a married man tempted by his attractive new secretary.

title: Die Hard [is a Christmas Movie]
description: New York City policeman John McClane (Bruce Willis) is visiting his estranged wife (Bonnie Bedelia) and two daughters on Christmas Eve. He joins her at a holiday party in the headquarters of the Japanese-owned business she works for. But the festivities are interrupted by a group of terrorists who take over the exclusive high-rise, and everyone in it. Very soon McClane realizes that there's no one to save the hostages -- but him.

title: In The Mood For Love
description: In 1962 Hong Kong, neighbors Su Li-zhen (Mrs. Chan) and Chow Mo-wan (Mr. Chow) discover their spouses are having an affair. As they spend time together, they develop feelings for each other, but their relationship remains chaste and unspoken, reflecting societal constraints and their own moral compass.

title: Goodfellas
description: Young Henry Hill (Ray Liotta), with his friends Jimmy (Robert De Niro) and Tommy (Joe Pesci), grows up in the mob and works very hard to advance himself through the ranks. He enjoys his life of money and luxury, but is oblivious to the horror that he causes. A drug addiction and a few mistakes ultimately unravel his climb to the top. Based on the book "Wiseguy" by Nicholas Pileggi.

title: The Muppet Christmas Carol
description: 'Tis the season for love, laughter, and one of the most cherished stories of all time! Join Kermit the Frog, Miss Piggy, and all the hilarious Muppets in this merry, magical version of Charles Dickens' classic tale. Academy Award® winner Michael Caine (Best Supporting Actor) gives a performance that's anything but "bah, humbug!" as greedy, penny-pinching Ebenezer Scrooge. One fateful Christmas Eve, Scrooge is visited by the Ghosts of Christmas Past, Present, and Future. Together with kind, humble Bob Cratchit (Kermit the Frog) and his family, the Spirits open Scrooge's eyes -- and his heart -- to the true meaning of Christmas. Filled with original music and dazzling special effects, THE MUPPET CHRISTMAS CAROL will become a holiday tradition your family will treasure all the days of the year. Featuring the film’s famous long-lost song ‘When Love is Gone’! ------ As always you can expect SING ALONG performances of this new version of THE MUPPET CHRISTMAS CAROL this Christmas - and now we don't need to pretend that we weren't going to just play the lost scene regardless! Performances will feature a Hosted Pre-Show with our very own Father Christmas, where you will be prepped on what to do throughout the film. Costumes aren't mandatory, but 'Tis the season, and we love seeing you dressed up in your favourite Christmas Jumpers! All this, and a few more surprises up our sleeves, makes this one of the must-see events this Christmas! If you're wanting to Sing Along with The Muppet Christmas Carol, simply book for the performances marked SING ALONG [it's next to the start time]. All other screenings will be regular performances, and nothing will be written next to the start time.

title: The Nightmare Before Christmas
description: The film follows the misadventures of Jack Skellington, Halloweentown's beloved pumpkin king, who has become bored with the same annual routine of frightening people in the "real world." When Jack accidentally stumbles on Christmastown, all bright colors and warm spirits, he gets a new lease on life -- he plots to bring Christmas under his control by kidnapping Santa Claus and taking over the role. But Jack soon discovers even the best-laid plans of mice and skeleton men can go seriously awry.

title: THE SWORD IN THE STONE
description: Disney’s underrated adaptation of the first title in T.H. White’s classic series The Once and Future King relates the coming-of-age of a young King Arthur, here named Wart, and his training by the wizard Merlin. Using the Xerox-transfer technology the studio implemented to great acclaim in its preceding 101 DALMATIANS, THE SWORD IN THE STONE centers on the magical arts of transformation, culminating in an epic battle of Merlin against the evil witch Madam Mim. Preceded by: Georges Méliès LE MAGICIEN (1898, 1 min, 35mm-to-DCP) Like THE SWORD IN THE STONE, George Méliès’s LE MAGICIEN emphasizes mystical metamorphoses. Total running time: ca. 85 min.
director: Wolfgang Reitherman, Clyde Geronimi, and David Hand

title: Relaxed Screening: NAZA (15)
description: Cloaked in darkness on the rooftops of Tel Aviv, Israeli journalist Yuval Abraham conducts shattering one-on-one interviews with Israeli soldiers and intelligence personnel.

title: BRIGHTON BEACH
description: At once a charming portrait of the diverse residents of a unique New York City neighborhood, a vibrant time capsule of the city at the very beginning of the 1980s, and a penetrating exploration of the social and political dynamics of a rapidly changing community, BRIGHTON BEACH is a long-lost gem of documentary cinema that has been newly restored by IndieCollect. Directed with great empathy and perceptiveness by Carol Stein & Susan Wittenberg, BRIGHTON BEACH captures the Brooklyn neighborhood known as the poor man’s paradise – a city by the sea down the street from the Coney Island boardwalk. Interspersing interviews with the neighborhood’s residents – including the Soviet Jews who had begun arriving in large numbers at the time – with archival footage of the area fifty years earlier, the film is both a portrait of a very particular time and place as well as a study of the ways in which urban communities function, cohere, and continuously transform themselves.

title: #7 TRAIN + CHINATOWN + TOURIST BUSES GO HOME!
description: Hye Jung Park & J.T. Takagi THE # 7 TRAIN: AN IMMIGRANT JOURNEY 1999, 28 min, DCP Every day 500,000 people from 117 different countries ride a subway that runs from Flushing to Times Square, going through Queens, the most culturally diverse region in the United States. This documentary follows four immigrant passengers: a Korean who works in Harlem, two Otavalen street vendors who work near Chinatown, and a gay Pakistani sari salesman on Fifth Avenue. Their lives and their conflicted relationships with the city and its other residents are juxtaposed with the subway they take each day to Manhattan and their dreams for the future. Jon Alpert & Keiko Tsuno CHINATOWN: IMMIGRANTS IN AMERICA 1980, 27 min, DCP “Produced in response to what DCTV felt were inaccurate media portrayals of New York City’s Chinatown, this award-winning, often startling portrait of an immigrant community probes beneath the tourist’s-eye view to uncover the complexity of an inner-city subculture plagued by poverty and exploitation. ‘This is the story of our neighbors,’ says Alpert. His sympathetic ‘reportage from within’ reveals kitchen workers earning less than $100 for sixty-hour weeks, rents that are among the highest in the city, and garment workers laboring for minimum wages in unsafe conditions. Focusing on individual stories to expose broader issues, this is an unflinching document of Asian immigrants under pressure to assimilate into mainstream culture and struggling to survive in America.” –ELECTRONIC ARTS INTERMIX Tom Tam TOURIST BUSES GO HOME! 1969, 10 min, DCP In this short film – one of the earliest examples of Asian American experimental film – Tom Tam follows the activism and protests against tours of Manhattan’s Chinatown. Total running time: ca. 70 min.

title: Eyes Wide Shut
description: Stanley Kubrick's daring last film is many things. It is a compelling psychosexual journey. A haunting dreamscape. A riveting tale of suspense. A major milestone in the careers of stars Tom Cruise and Nicole Kidman. And "a worthy final chapter to a great director's career" (Roger Ebert). Cruise plays Dr William Hartford, who plunges into an erotic foray that threatens his marriage - and may even ensnare him in a lurid murder mystery - after his wife's (Kidman) admission of sexual longings. As the story sweeps from doubt and fear to self-discovery and reconciliation, Kubrick orchestrates it with masterful flourishes. Graceful tracking shots, controlled pacing, rich colours, startling images: bravura traits that make Kubrick a filmmaker for the ages are here to keep everyone's eyes wide shut.

title: Elf
description: Buddy (Will Ferrell) was accidentally transported to the North Pole as a toddler and raised to adulthood among Santa's elves. Unable to shake the feeling that he doesn't fit in, the adult Buddy travels to New York, in full elf uniform, in search of his real father. As it happens, this is Walter Hobbs (James Caan), a cynical businessman. After a DNA test proves this, Walter reluctantly attempts to start a relationship with the childlike Buddy with increasingly chaotic results.

title: It's A Wonderful Life

Seeing no way out, George considers suicide from the edge of a bridge ­ but Clarence, his guardian angel, intervenes and shows George what his beloved hometown of Bedford Falls would be like without him.

title: Phantom Thread
description: Renowned dressmaker Reynolds Woodcock and his sister Cyril are at the center of British fashion in 1950s London -- dressing royalty, movie stars, heiresses, socialites and debutantes. Women come and go in Woodcock's life, providing the confirmed bachelor with inspiration and companionship. His carefully tailored existence soon gets disrupted by Alma, a young and strong-willed woman who becomes his muse and lover.

title: Tokyo Godfathers
description: Middle-aged alcoholic Gin, teenage runaway Miyuki and former drag queen Hana are a trio of homeless people surviving as a makeshift family on the streets of Tokyo. While rummaging in the trash for food on Christmas Eve, they stumble upon an abandoned newborn baby in a trash bin. With only a handful of clues to the baby's identity, the three misfits search the streets of Tokyo for help in returning the baby to its parents.

title: EC: PETER KUBELKA (THE COMPLETE WORKS): NEW 35MM PRINTS!
description: For this round of the Essential Cinema cycle, we will be showcasing brand new 35mm prints that Anthology has recently acquired of Peter Kubelka’s films. To celebrate these new prints, we will be supplementing the regular EC program with new prints of Kubelka’s POETRY AND TRUTH and ANTIPHON, as well as a vintage print of PAUSE!, which together effectively comprise a complete retrospective of his work! Special thanks to Peter Kubelka and the Austrian Film Museum. MOSAIC IN CONFIDENCE / MOSAIK IM VERTRAUEN (1955, 16 min, 35mm. Made in collaboration with Ferry Radax. Brand new print! ) ADEBAR (1957, 1 min, 35mm. Brand new print! ) SCHWECHATER (1958, 1 min, 16mm. Brand new print! ) ARNULF RAINER (1960, 7 min, 35mm. Brand new print! ) OUR TRIP TO AFRICA / UNSERE AFRIKAREISE (1966, 12 min, 16mm) PAUSE! (1977, 12 min, 16mm) POETRY AND TRUTH / DICHTUNG UND WAHRHEIT (1996-2003, 13 min, 35mm. Brand new print! ) ANTIPHON (2012, 6.5 min, 35mm. Brand new print! ) “Peter Kubelka is the perfectionist of the film medium; and, as I honor that quality above all others at this time finding such a lack of it now elsewhere, I would simply like to say: Peter Kubelka is the world’s greatest filmmaker – which is to say, simply: see his films!…by all means/above all else…etcetera.” –Stan Brakhage Total running time: ca. 75 min.

title: Ken Russell's The Devils: The Director's Cut
description: Censored for over half a century, Ken Russell’s film returns in a landmark director’s cut reconstruction that reveals the full power of his original vision. Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, accused of bewitching a convent of nuns, The Devils lays bare the collusion of church and state through a searing vision of religious persecution, collective hysteria and institutional corruption. The restoration many believed would never happen reaffirms Russell’s incendiary masterpiece as among the most overwhelming and uncompromising achievements in British cinema. Assembled from original camera negative, this 4k restoration is Ken Russell’s 2004 preferred edit. Picture and sound restoration by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color and Warner Bros. Sound.

title: EC: KUCHAR / LYE
description: George & Mike Kuchar PUSSY ON A HOT TIN ROOF 1961, 14 min, 8mm-to-16mm. Preserved by Anthology Film Archives with support from the National Film Preservation Foundation. “It glows with the embers of desire! It smokes with the revelation of men and women longing for robust temptations that will make them sizzle into maturity with a furnace-blast of unrestrained animalism. A film for young and old to enjoy.” –George Kuchar TOOTSIES IN AUTUMN 1963, 15 min, 8mm-to-16mm. Preserved by Anthology Film Archives with support from the National Film Preservation Foundation. A cautionary tale about past-their-prime thespians caught up in a typically Kucharian vortex of madness. Len Lye TUSALAVA (1929, 10 min, 16mm, silent) TRADE TATTOO (1937, 5 min, 35mm) RHYTHM (1957, 1 min, 16mm) FREE RADICALS (1958/79, 4 min, 16mm) A giant of experimental animation, Len Lye was born in New Zealand in 1901. He moved to England in the 1920s and subsequently to New York in 1944, where he spent the last 40 years of his life. A pioneer of “scratch” or “direct” filmmaking, Lye used various tools to mark patterns, shapes, and images directly onto the film’s surface, and often explored the dynamic energy of abstract images propelled into life by lively jazz scores or Pacific-inspired rhythms. Total running time: ca. 55 min.

title: WIZARDS
description: Ralph Bakshi’s anti-fascist passion project, developed over decades and released prior to his LORD OF THE RINGS, mixes sci-fi and fantasy to tell the story of a far-future Earth where magic and fairies have returned in the wake of nuclear holocaust. These forces of good must battle an evil wizard who attempts to control the world by reviving the forbidden technologies of war. WIZARDS is pure, unrestrained Bakshi, filled with freaky characters, psychedelic backgrounds, and hallucinatory rotoscoping. Preceded by: Tommy Turner THE MAGICIAN 1998, 9 min, 16mm WIZARDS is paired with Tommy Turner’s THE MAGICIAN, a transgressive take on the rituals of ceremonial magic. Total running time: ca. 95 min.

title: American Psycho
description: A wealthy New York investment banking executive hides his alternate psychopathic ego from his co-workers and friends as he escalates deeper into his illogical, gratuitous fantasies.

title: (POSTHUMOUS) + NO TITLE
description: Ghassan Salhab (POSTHUMOUS) / (POSTHUME) 2007, 31 min, DCP. In Arabic with English subtitles. “Not long after the Israeli attack of 2006, Ghassan Salhab directed this filmic essay; its images are both absent and present witnesses to an unexpected war. A cinematographic musing on contemporary Lebanon and a wager on the impossibility of recounting the violence of a bruised country, whose ghosts reappear from the ruins and stare at the screen, before disappearing in cross-fade.” –VISIONS DU RÉEL Ghassan Salhab NO TITLE 2025, 42 min, DCP. In Arabic with English subtitles. “[NO TITLE is] a car-bound survey of utterly devastated sites in South Lebanon following the 2024 Israeli airstrikes. In many respects this film can be viewed as an extension of [Salhab’s CONTRETEMPS (2024)], an afterword necessitated by ongoing escalations beyond the cinema screen. It is not to reveal too much about NO TITLE to cite its closing statement, a gnomic endnote that hints at the unfathomably endless horrors of Israel’s war: ‘still today’.” –ALCHEMY FILM & ARTS Total running time: ca. 75 min.

description: From acclaimed director Alexander Payne, THE HOLDOVERS follows a curmudgeonly instructor (Paul Giamatti) at a prestigious American school who is forced to remain on campus during Christmas break to babysit the handful of students with nowhere to go. Eventually he forms an unlikely bond with one of them -- a damaged, brainy troublemaker (newcomer Dominic Sessa) -- and with the school’s head cook, who has just lost a son in Vietnam (Da’Vine Joy Randolph).

title: THE SWORD IN THE STONE
description: Disney’s underrated adaptation of the first title in T.H. White’s classic series The Once and Future King relates the coming-of-age of a young King Arthur, here named Wart, and his training by the wizard Merlin. Using the Xerox-transfer technology the studio implemented to great acclaim in its preceding 101 DALMATIANS, THE SWORD IN THE STONE centers on the magical arts of transformation, culminating in an epic battle of Merlin against the evil witch Madam Mim. Preceded by: Georges Méliès LE MAGICIEN (1898, 1 min, 35mm-to-DCP) Like THE SWORD IN THE STONE, George Méliès’s LE MAGICIEN emphasizes mystical metamorphoses. Total running time: ca. 85 min.
